Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verse 1–10:

It has two hundred and six verses.

Abu Umamah narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever recites Surat al-A'raf, Allah will place between him and Iblis a barrier, and Adam will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection" [170] [[Tafsir al-Kashshaf: 2/193.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Al-Mas is an oath that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swore." 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it is from Allah's praise of Himself. Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: it is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted. Abu al-Duha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "I am Allah, the One who distinguishes." And it was said: it is a disjointed (muwada') spelling. Qatadah: it is one of the names of the Qur'an. It was also said: it is the name of the surah. Mujahid: they are openings with which Allah began His Book. Al-Sha'bi: the openings of the surahs are names of Allah, the Exalted; if they are joined, they become a name.

Abu Rawq said: "I am Allah, the Truthful." Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "I am Allah, the most truthful." Muhammad ibn Ka'b: the opening letter of His name is alif, "One" (ahad) and "first" (awwal) and "last" (akhir); the lam is the opening of His name "Gentle" (latif); the mim is the opening of His name "Glorious" (majid) and "King" (malik); the sad is the opening of His name "Eternal Refuge" (samad), "Truthful" (sadiq), "One" (ahad) and "Creator of creatures" (sani' al-masnu'at).

In some tafsirs I saw the meaning of al-Mas: "Did We not expand for you your breast?" It was also said: they are disjointed letters of the alphabet; it was said: they are the numerical value of the letters (hisab al-jummal); it was said: they are the letters of the Greatest Name of Allah; it was said: they are letters containing many meanings, and that Allah addresses His creation with them, all of this being according to His intention.

Its position is nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and "a Book" (kitab) is its predicate, as if he said: "Alif-Lam-Mim (are) letters. A Book has been sent down to you." It was also said: "a Book" is a predicate of a subject begun here, "this is a book."

It was also said it is nominative by inversion of order, meaning: a Book has been sent down to you, and it is the Qur'an. "So let there be no discomfort in your breast concerning it" (fa-la yakun fi sadrika haraj minhu). Abu al-'Aliyah said: constriction. Mujahid said: doubt. Al-Dahhak said: sin. Muqatil said: let there be no doubt in your heart about the Qur'an, that it is from Allah. It was also said: the meaning is, do not let your heart be burdened by warning those whom We sent you to warn, and by conveying what We commanded you to convey to them. "And a reminder for the believers" (wa dhikra li-l-mu'minin), meaning an admonition and exhortation to them. Its position is nominative, coordinated with "the Book."

It was also said it is accusative as an infinitive, its implied sense being "and it is remembered as a reminder." It is also permissible that it be in the genitive position, in the sense of "li-tundhira" (that you may warn) occupying the genitive place, the meaning being warning and reminder. As for dhikra, it is an infinitive with the feminine suffix alif, like "da'awtu da'wa" and "raji'tu raj'a," except that it is a noun in the place of the infinitive.

"Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord" (ittabi'u ma unzila ilaykum min rabbikum), meaning: say to them, "Follow, and do not follow others besides Him as protectors."

The common readers recite it with the 'ayn, from ittiba' (following). 'Asim al-Jahdari narrated from Abu [al-Shaykh] and Malik ibn Dinar: "wa la tabtaghu" with a ghayn (la tatlubu, do not seek), i.e., do not seek. "Little is it that you remember" (qalilan ma tadhakkarun). "And how many a town We have destroyed" (wa kam min qaryatin ahlaknaha) with punishment. The position of "kam" is nominative as subject, and its predicate is in "ahlaknaha." If you wish, you may make it accusative by the return of the pronoun. "Then Our might came upon them" (fa-ja'aha ba'suna), Our punishment, "by night" (bayatan), at night [as an army comes], "or while they were taking a midday rest" (aw hum qa'ilun), meaning in the daytime at the time of the midday rest; qa'ilun means sleeping at noon. The meaning of the verse: "or while they were taking a midday rest" means that some of these towns were destroyed at night and some were destroyed by day, and they omitted [the one] for their disliking of repetition, following one construction with another. This is the saying of al-Farra'. Al-Zajjaj took "aw" in the sense of choice and permission, its implied sense being: Our might came upon them once at night and once by day.

"Then their claim was not" (fa-ma kana da'wahum), meaning their saying and their calling, like His saying, "and that claim of theirs did not cease" (Qur'an 21:15). The poet said:

"And if my leg goes numb, I call you, seeking relief
by your calling of one whose leg has gone numb, so it eases."

(tafsir note: "madhalla rijlahu" means his leg became numb.)

"When Our might came upon them" (idh ja'ahum ba'suna), Our punishment, "except that they said: Indeed we were wrongdoers" (illa an qalu inna kunna zalimin), sinners, sinful and disobedient to His command; they acknowledged against themselves.

Ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No people perished until they had been given an excuse from themselves." He said: I asked, "How can that be?" Then he recited this verse: "Then their claim was not, when Our might came upon them..." [171] [[Musnad Ahmad 4/260; it does not contain mention of the verse.]].

"Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent" (fa-la nas'alanna alladhina ursila ilayhim), meaning the nations, about their response to the messengers, "and We will surely question the messengers" (wa la nas'alanna al-mursalin) about conveying to the nations. "Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge" (fa-la naqussanna 'alayhim bi-'ilm). Ibn 'Abbas said: their books of deeds will speak to them, as evidenced by His saying, "This Our Book speaks against you with truth" (Qur'an 45:29).

"And We were not absent" (wa ma kunna ghaibin), from the messengers in what they encountered, and from the nations in what they answered. "And the weighing on that Day is the truth" (wa al-wazn yawma'idhin al-haqq). Mujahid said: the judgment that Day is justice. Others said: it means [other than the weighing of deeds]: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sets up the scale for Himself, [with hands and palms] on the Day of Resurrection, and the deeds of the servants, good and bad, are weighed; the scale of good deeds is made heavy at times for the salvation of whom He wills to save, and at times the scale of good deeds is made light as a sign of the ruin of whom He wills to ruin.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in weighing the deeds of the servants, when Allah knows the measure of everything before creating it and after? We say: there are four things. The first: Allah's testing of His servants by faith in Him in this world. The second: making that a sign for the people of happiness and wretchedness in the Hereafter. The third: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, making the servants aware of what there is with Allah in reward for good and evil. The fourth: establishing the proof against them.

Its parallel is His saying, "This Our Book speaks against you with truth" (Qur'an 45:29), and so He informs of what the deeds bring and records them, although He knows them, for the meanings we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

"As for him whose scales are heavy" (fa-man thaqulat mawazinuhu), Mujahid said: his good deeds, "those are the successful" (fa-ulaika humu al-muflihun). "And whose scales are light" (wa man khaffat mawazinuhu) up to His saying, "they wronged" (yazlimun), "they denied." Hudhayfah said: the one in charge of the scales on the Day of Resurrection is Jibril. Allah says, "O Jibril, weigh between them," and he returns some to others. He said: there is no gold or silver there; if the wrongdoer has good deeds, some of his good deeds are taken and returned to the wronged; if he has no good deeds, the sins of his companion are placed upon him. A man will come with the weight of mountains upon him [172].

Ibn 'Abbas said: good deeds and evil deeds are weighed in a scale with a tongue and two pans. As for the believer, his deed is brought to him in its finest form, and it rises in the pan of the scale, and that is the truth; his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, and his deed is placed in Paradise, and he recognizes it by his deed. That is His saying: "As for him whose scales are heavy, those are the successful," the saved, and they will have chambers according to their stations in Paradise when they turn back to them from the people of Paradise, when they turn back to their dwellings.

As for the disbelievers, their deeds are brought to them in their most hideous form, and placed in the pan of the scale, which is falsehood; its weight is light until it falls into the Fire. Then it is said to the disbeliever: "Be given the truth by your deed."

If it is asked: how is the weighing of deeds valid when they are accidents and not bodies, so that it would be permissible to weigh them and describe them as heavy and light? The deeds that are weighed are only the deeds of the servants written down.

This is indicated by the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: a man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection to the scale; then ninety-nine registers will be brought out for him, each register as far as the eye can see, containing his sins and wrongdoings, and they will be placed in the pan; then a card like a fingernail will be brought out for him, in which is written: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His servant and messenger" (ﷺ), and it will be placed in the other pan, and it outweighs his sins and wrongdoings. The parallel of this verse is His saying, "And We set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection" (Qur'an 21:47).

If it is said: why is it plural when it is one scale?

It is said: it is permissible that it be [magnified] collectively, and the meaning is one, like His saying, "those to whom the people said" (Qur'an 3:173), and "O messengers" (Qur'an 23:51). Al-A'sha said:

"A face clear of hue, pure, adorned with
a neck and wrists along with the collar."

He meant "labbah" and "mi'sam" (singular).

It was also said: he meant the deeds that are weighed.

It was also said: the origin is one great scale, and for each servant there is a small scale hung from it.

It was also said: it is plural because the scale encompasses the two pans, the two witnesses and the tongue, and weighing is not achieved except by their gathering.

It was also said: the origin of "mawazin" is: a scale by which truth and falsehood are distinguished, which is reason ('aql); and a scale by which the lawful and the unlawful are distinguished, which is knowledge ('ilm); and a scale by which happiness and wretchedness are distinguished, which is the absence of heedlessness of intention. And success is with Allah.

"And We have certainly established you on the earth" (wa laqad makkannakum fi al-ard): We gave you dominion over the earth and made it easy for you, and made it a settled place for you. "And We made for you therein means of livelihood" (wa ja'alna lakum fiha ma'ayish), by which you live during your lives, from food and drink. Ma'ayish is the plural of ma'isha; its ya' is original, so it is not hamzated. "Little is it that you give thanks" (qalilan ma tashkurun), for what We have done for you.

Others said: it means [other than the weighing of deeds]: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sets up the scale for Himself, [with hands and palms] on the Day of Resurrection, and the deeds of the servants, good and bad, are weighed; the scale of good deeds is made heavy at times for the salvation of whom He wills to save, and at times the scale of good deeds is made light as a sign of the ruin of whom He wills to ruin.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in weighing the deeds of the servants, when Allah knows the measure of everything before creating it and after? We say: there are four things. The first: Allah's testing of His servants by faith in Him in this world. The second: making that a sign for the people of happiness and wretchedness in the Hereafter. The third: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, making the servants aware of what there is with Allah in reward for good and evil. The fourth: establishing the proof against them.

Its parallel is His saying, "This Our Book speaks against you with truth" (Qur'an 45:29), and so He informs of what the deeds bring and records them, although He knows them, for the meanings we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

"As for him whose scales are heavy" (fa-man thaqulat mawazinuhu), Mujahid said: his good deeds, "those are the successful" (fa-ulaika humu al-muflihun). "And whose scales are light" (wa man khaffat mawazinuhu) up to His saying, "they wronged" (yazlimun), "they denied." Hudhayfah said: the one in charge of the scales on the Day of Resurrection is Jibril. Allah says, "O Jibril, weigh between them," and he returns some to others. He said: there is no gold or silver there; if the wrongdoer has good deeds, some of his good deeds are taken and returned to the wronged; if he has no good deeds, the sins of his companion are placed upon him. A man will come with the weight of mountains upon him [172].

Ibn 'Abbas said: good deeds and evil deeds are weighed in a scale with a tongue and two pans. As for the believer, his deed is brought to him in its finest form, and it rises in the pan of the scale, and that is the truth; his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, and his deed is placed in Paradise, and he recognizes it by his deed. That is His saying: "As for him whose scales are heavy, those are the successful," the saved, and they will have chambers according to their stations in Paradise when they turn back to them from the people of Paradise, when they turn back to their dwellings.

As for the disbelievers, their deeds are brought to them in their most hideous form, and placed in the pan of the scale, which is falsehood; its weight is light until it falls into the Fire. Then it is said to the disbeliever: "Be given the truth by your deed."

If it is asked: how is the weighing of deeds valid when they are accidents and not bodies, so that it would be permissible to weigh them and describe them as heavy and light? The deeds that are weighed are only the deeds of the servants written down.

This is indicated by the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: a man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection to the scale; then ninety-nine registers will be brought out for him, each register as far as the eye can see, containing his sins and wrongdoings, and they will be placed in the pan; then a card like a fingernail will be brought out for him, in which is written: "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His servant and messenger" (ﷺ), and it will be placed in the other pan, and it outweighs his sins and wrongdoings. The parallel of this verse is His saying, "And We set up the just scales for the Day of Resurrection" (Qur'an 21:47).

If it is said: why is it plural when it is one scale?

It is said: it is permissible that it be [magnified] collectively, and the meaning is one, like His saying, "those to whom the people said" (Qur'an 3:173), and "O messengers" (Qur'an 23:51). Al-A'sha said:

"A face clear of hue, pure, adorned with
a neck and wrists along with the collar."

He meant "labbah" and "mi'sam" (singular).

It was also said: he meant the deeds that are weighed.

It was also said: the origin is one great scale, and for each servant there is a small scale hung from it.

It was also said: it is plural because the scale encompasses the two pans, the two witnesses and the tongue, and weighing is not achieved except by their gathering.

It was also said: the origin of "mawazin" is: a scale by which truth and falsehood are distinguished, which is reason ('aql); and a scale by which the lawful and the unlawful are distinguished, which is knowledge ('ilm); and a scale by which happiness and wretchedness are distinguished, which is the absence of heedlessness of intention. And success is with Allah.

"And We have certainly established you on the earth" (wa laqad makkannakum fi al-ard): We gave you dominion over the earth and made it easy for you, and made it a settled place for you. "And We made for you therein means of livelihood" (wa ja'alna lakum fiha ma'ayish), by which you live during your lives, from food and drink. Ma'ayish is the plural of ma'isha; its ya' is original, so it is not hamzated. "Little is it that you give thanks" (qalilan ma tashkurun), for what We have done for you.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 7, verses 11–18:**

﴿And We certainly created you﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "We created your origin and your father, Adam." ﴿Then We fashioned you﴾ in the wombs of your mothers. Qatadah, al-Rabiʿ, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: "As for ﴿We created you﴾, it refers to Adam, and as for ﴿We fashioned you﴾, it refers to his offspring." Mujahid said: "We created Adam, then We fashioned you in the loins of Adam."

ʿIkrimah said: "﴿We created you﴾ in the loins of men, and ﴿We fashioned you﴾ in the wombs of women." ʿAṭāʾ said: "They were created in the loins of Adam, then they were fashioned in the wombs."

Yaman said: "Man was created in the womb, then He fashioned him, and He opened his hearing, his sight and his fingers." If it is said: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿Then We said to the angels: prostrate to Adam﴾, when the creation of mankind came after that, and ﴿then﴾ (thumma) requires sequence and delay?

It is like the speaker's saying: "I stood, then I sat," where sitting cannot occur except after standing.

We say: some people said it is by inversion (taqdim wa taʾkhir). Yunus said: "The creating and the fashioning are one [...]" [[unreadable word.]] "to Us," as we say: "We have struck you," while it was actually their chief whom I struck. Al-Akhfash said: "Thumma here means waw (and), and its meaning is: ﴿We said﴾," like the saying of the poet:

"I asked Rabiʿah about the best of her: a father, then a mother; so she said: his mother."

He meant: "a father and a mother."

﴿So they prostrated﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated﴾ to Adam. Then Allah said to Iblis, when he refused to prostrate to Adam: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ Some of them said: "la" here is extra [and in is connective]. The sense of the sentence is: "What prevented you from prostrating to Adam," because the verb "prevent" takes two objects. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And it is forbidden to a town which We have destroyed that they shall not return﴾.

The poet said:

"They blame me for amusement, that I do not love it, while the call to amusement is persistent and never unaware."

He meant: "that I love it."

Another said:

"So I do not blame the fair ones for not mocking me, when they saw me, the white-haired, the old."

Another said:

"His generosity refused, not stinginess, and he was hastened by it; a good youth is one whose killer does not prevent generosity."

He meant: "His generosity refused stinginess."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Haytham al-Juhani narrate from Ahmad ibn Yahya Thaʿlab, who said: "Some of them disliked using al-qala (to say), and they used 'prevention' with the meaning of 'saying', because both saying and doing can prevent. Its sense is: who said to you, 'Do not prostrate'?" Some said: "The meaning of prevention is a barrier between a person and what he wants. The one prevented is compelled to do the opposite of what he was prevented from. So it is as if he said: 'What compelled you to not prostrate?'"

﴿When I commanded you﴾. Iblis replied to Him, saying: ﴿I am better than him, You created me from fire and fire is better, more excellent, purer and brighter than clay.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The first to practice qiyas (analogy) was Iblis, and he erred in analogy. So whoever measures religion by his own opinion has joined him with Iblis."

Ibn Sirin said: "The first to practice analogy was Iblis, and the sun and moon were only worshipped through analogies."

The wise said: "The enemy of Allah erred when he preferred fire over clay, because clay is better than fire in several respects:

First: the essence of clay includes steadiness, calm, dignity, deliberation, forbearance, modesty and patience. This is what called Adam to the happiness that had preceded for him, to repentance, humility and supplication, and it brought him forgiveness, selection, guidance and repentance. The essence of fire is lightness, recklessness, sharpness, rising and agitation. This is what called Iblis, after the wretchedness that had been driven for him, to arrogance and persistence, and so destruction, punishment, curse and dissension overtook him.

Second: clay is the cause of gathering things together, and fire is the cause of scattering them.

Third: the report states that the dust of Paradise is pungent musk, and the report does not state that there is fire in Paradise or dust in Hell.

Fourth: fire is the cause of punishment, and it is Allah's punishment for His enemies, while dust is not a cause of punishment.

Fifth: clay [is watered] by fire, and fire needs a place, and its place is dust."

Then Allah said to him: ﴿Get down from it﴾, meaning from Paradise. It was said: from the heaven to the earth. So He attached him to the islands of the seas, and his authority and greatness are in the treasuries of the seas, his throne is in the green sea, and he does not enter the earth except in the manner of a thief who sneaks in, wearing rags, in which he frightens [whoever comes out] of it. ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, meaning in Paradise. It is not fitting that an arrogant one dwell in Paradise or in heaven, nor to oppose the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Get out, you are of the debased﴾, the humiliated. Debasement (ṣaghar) is abasement and disgrace.

Iblis said at that moment: ﴿Give me respite﴾, delay me, grant me a term and reprieve me, and do not cause me to die ﴿until the day they are raised﴾, meaning from their graves, and that is the final blast at the start of the Hour. The wicked one wanted not to taste death. He said: ﴿You are of those given respite﴾, the delayed ones.

Then He specified the period of respite and reprieve in another place, saying: ﴿Until the day of the appointed time﴾. That is the first blast, when all creation is established. He said: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾. They differed about what he said. Some of them said: it is an interrogative, meaning: "By what did You lead me astray?" Then he began: ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them﴾. It was said: "ma" here is a conditional, meaning: "Since You led me astray, I will surely sit in ambush." It was also said: "ma" is a verbal noun in the position of an oath, its sense being: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in ambush," like His saying: ﴿with what My Lord forgave me﴾, meaning: "by the forgiveness of my Lord."

His saying ﴿You led me astray﴾ means: "You misled me from guidance." It was also said: "You destroyed me," from the Arabs' saying "ghawā al-fasīl" (the young camel was destroyed), meaning it perished when it lacked milk and died. The poet said:

"A bending of the joints; its young one does not milk its milk, nor does the dead one perish."

It is narrated that some tribes of Ṭayy say: "So-and-so became ghāwī," meaning sick and ruined. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "The origin of ighwāʾ in the speech of the Arabs is a man making something attractive to another, until he makes it good in his eyes, so that he is ruined by it."

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Hani informed us, who said: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad [al-Rawsani] narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Abu Muʿawiyah al-Darir narrated to us from a man who was not named, who said: "I was with Tawus in the Sacred Mosque, when a man from those who deny predestination, one of the senior jurists, came and sat with him. Tawus said: [Let him stand or be made to stand]. So the man stood up, and said to Tawus: 'You say this man is a jurist?' Tawus said: 'Iblis is more jurisprudent than him, with the saying of Iblis: ﴿My Lord, because You led me astray﴾, and he says: "I myself led myself astray."'"

﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾, meaning: "I will surely sit on the path of the children of Adam on Your upright way," which is Islam, as in His saying: ﴿Have you hastened the command of your Lord?﴾, meaning "from the command of your Lord."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Shaytan sat in wait for the children of Adam on the roads. He sat in wait for him on the road of Islam and said to him: 'Will you submit and leave your religion and the religion of your fathers?' He disobeyed him and embraced Islam. Then he sat in wait for him on the road of emigration and said: 'Will you emigrate and leave your land and your sky? The likeness of the emigrant is like a horse on a tether.' He disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the road of jihad, which is striving with the self and wealth, and said: 'Will you fight and be killed, so that your wife is married and your wealth is divided?' He disobeyed him and strove."

From ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allah regarding ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾: "It is the road to Makkah." ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾, the verse. ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾ means: "I will cast doubt upon them regarding their Hereafter; ﴿and from behind them﴾ [that he will establish in their book]; ﴿and from their right﴾: the matter of their religion will be confused for them; ﴿and from their left﴾: [I will make] sins appealing to them."

Ṭāʾūs narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "As for ﴿from before them﴾, it is from the direction of their worldly life; as for ﴿from behind them﴾, it is their Hereafter; as for ﴿from their right﴾, it is from the direction of their good deeds; and as for ﴿from their left﴾, it is from the direction of their evil deeds."

Qatadah said: "He came to them from before them and told them there is no punishment, no Paradise and no Fire. ﴿From behind them﴾: from the matters of this world, he adorned it for them, called them to it. ﴿From their right﴾: from the direction of their good deeds, he slowed them down from them. ﴿From their left﴾: he adorned for them the evil deeds and sins, called them to them and commanded them with them. Beware, son of Adam, from every direction, except that he did not come to you from above you, and he could not come between you and the mercy of Allah."

Al-Hakam and al-Suddi said: ﴿I will come to them from before them﴾: meaning the world. I call them to it, make them desire it and adorn it for them. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the direction of the Hereafter; I cast doubt on them and hinder them concerning it. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of the truth; I turn them away from it and test them regarding it. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of falsehood; I make it light for them, adorn it for them and make them desire it.

Mujahid said: ﴿From before them and from their right﴾: from where they see; ﴿and from behind them and from their left﴾: from where they do not see. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of His saying "from where they see" is: they err where they know they are erring, and "where they do not see" means they do not know they are erring.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾: from the direction of their Hereafter; I inform them that there is no Paradise, no Fire and no resurrection. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the direction of their worldly life; so I command them to gather wealth, not giving its due, and I frighten them with the loss of their offspring. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of their religion; I make clear to each people what they used to worship, and if they were upon guidance, I confuse it for them until I take them out of it. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of desires and pleasures; I make them attractive to them.

Shaqiq ibn Ibrahim said: "Every morning Shaytan sits in wait for me in four positions: from before me, behind me, on my right and on my left. As for from before me, I say: 'Do not grieve, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful,' and He says that for ﴿those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and then are guided﴾. As for from behind me, he frightens me with loss for my dependants and family, and I say: ﴿There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah﴾. As for from my right, he comes to me from the direction of praise, and I say: ﴿And the final outcome is for the righteous.﴾ As for from my left, he comes to me from the direction of desires and pleasures, and I say: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire.﴾"

﴿And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to Iblis: ﴿Get out of it, reproached and expelled.﴾ That is: "blamed." Dhaʾm (reproach) and dhaʾm (blame) are the most severe defect, and it is more emphatic than "dhamm." It is said: "He reproached him, reproaches him, reproach, so he is reproached," and "dha'ama," "yadhaʾmuhu," "dhaʾman," "so he is madhʾum, and the reproach was made with 'dhamm,' 'dhaym,'" like "sar, yasir," so he is "mudhaym." Al-madhḥūr (the expelled) is the one pushed away. It is said: "daḥarahu, yadḥaruhu, daḥran," if he removed him and drove him away.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "﴿Madhʾūman﴾ means: turned away from him; ﴿madhʾūman madhḥūran﴾ means: not expelled." Al-Rabiʿ and Mujahid said: ﴿Madhʾūman﴾ means "detested." Ṭāʾūs narrated: "Madhʾūman, detested." Abu al-ʿĀliyah said: "Madhʾūman, disgraced by it."

Al-Kalbi said: "Madhʾūman, blamed; madhḥūran, removed from Paradise and from all good." ʿAṭāʾ said: "Madhʾūman, cursed."

Al-Kisaʾi said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one despised." Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one imprisoned." Abban, from Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad, said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one defective."

Al-Aʿshā said:

"A tribe said, when they saw me, and the beautiful woman does not lack blame."

﴿Whoever follows you of them﴾, of the children of Adam, ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾, with you and your offspring, and with the disbelieving offspring of Adam, ﴿all together.﴾

He disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the road of jihad, which is striving with the self and wealth, and said: 'Will you fight and be killed, so that your wife is married and your wealth is divided?' He disobeyed him and strove."

This is what called Iblis, after the wretchedness that had been driven for him, to arrogance and persistence, and so destruction, punishment, curse and dissension overtook him.

Second: clay is the cause of gathering things together, and fire is the cause of scattering them.

Third: the report states that the dust of Paradise is pungent musk, and the report does not state that there is fire in Paradise or dust in Hell.

Fourth: fire is the cause of punishment, and it is Allah's punishment for His enemies, while dust is not a cause of punishment.

Fifth: clay [is watered] by fire, and fire needs a place, and its place is dust."

Then Allah said to him: ﴿Get down from it﴾, meaning from Paradise. It was said: from the heaven to the earth. So He attached him to the islands of the seas, and his authority and greatness are in the treasuries of the seas, his throne is in the green sea, and he does not enter the earth except in the manner of a thief who sneaks in, wearing rags, in which he frightens [whoever comes out] of it. ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, meaning in Paradise. It is not fitting that an arrogant one dwell in Paradise or in heaven, nor to oppose the command of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Get out, you are of the debased﴾, the humiliated. Debasement (ṣaghar) is abasement and disgrace.

Iblis said at that moment: ﴿Give me respite﴾, delay me, grant me a term and reprieve me, and do not cause me to die ﴿until the day they are raised﴾, meaning from their graves, and that is the final blast at the start of the Hour. The wicked one wanted not to taste death. He said: ﴿You are of those given respite﴾, the delayed ones.

Then He specified the period of respite and reprieve in another place, saying: ﴿Until the day of the appointed time﴾. That is the first blast, when all creation is established. He said: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾. They differed about what he said. Some of them said: it is an interrogative, meaning: "By what did You lead me astray?" Then he began: ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them﴾. It was said: "ma" here is a conditional, meaning: "Since You led me astray, I will surely sit in ambush." It was also said: "ma" is a verbal noun in the position of an oath, its sense being: "By Your leading me astray, I will surely sit in ambush," like His saying: ﴿with what My Lord forgave me﴾, meaning: "by the forgiveness of my Lord."

His saying ﴿You led me astray﴾ means: "You misled me from guidance." It was also said: "You destroyed me," from the Arabs' saying "ghawā al-fasīl" (the young camel was destroyed), meaning it perished when it lacked milk and died. The poet said:

"A bending of the joints; its young one does not milk its milk, nor does the dead one perish."

It is narrated that some tribes of Ṭayy say: "So-and-so became ghāwī," meaning sick and ruined. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: "The origin of ighwāʾ in the speech of the Arabs is a man making something attractive to another, until he makes it good in his eyes, so that he is ruined by it."

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Hani informed us, who said: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad [al-Rawsani] narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: Abu Muʿawiyah al-Darir narrated to us from a man who was not named, who said: "I was with Tawus in the Sacred Mosque, when a man from those who deny predestination, one of the senior jurists, came and sat with him. Tawus said: [Let him stand or be made to stand]. So the man stood up, and said to Tawus: 'You say this man is a jurist?' Tawus said: 'Iblis is more jurisprudent than him, with the saying of Iblis: ﴿My Lord, because You led me astray﴾, and he says: "I myself led myself astray."'"

﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾, meaning: "I will surely sit on the path of the children of Adam on Your upright way," which is Islam, as in His saying: ﴿Have you hastened the command of your Lord?﴾, meaning "from the command of your Lord."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Shaytan sat in wait for the children of Adam on the roads. He sat in wait for him on the road of Islam and said to him: 'Will you submit and leave your religion and the religion of your fathers?' He disobeyed him and embraced Islam. Then he sat in wait for him on the road of emigration and said: 'Will you emigrate and leave your land and your sky? The likeness of the emigrant is like a horse on a tether.' He disobeyed him and emigrated. Then he sat in wait for him on the road of jihad, which is striving with the self and wealth, and said: 'Will you fight and be killed, so that your wife is married and your wealth is divided?' He disobeyed him and strove."

From ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allah regarding ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾: "It is the road to Makkah." ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them﴾, the verse. ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾ means: "I will cast doubt upon them regarding their Hereafter; ﴿and from behind them﴾ [that he will establish in their book]; ﴿and from their right﴾: the matter of their religion will be confused for them; ﴿and from their left﴾: [I will make] sins appealing to them."

Ṭāʾūs narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "As for ﴿from before them﴾, it is from the direction of their worldly life; as for ﴿from behind them﴾, it is their Hereafter; as for ﴿from their right﴾, it is from the direction of their good deeds; and as for ﴿from their left﴾, it is from the direction of their evil deeds."

Qatadah said: "He came to them from before them and told them there is no punishment, no Paradise and no Fire. ﴿From behind them﴾: from the matters of this world, he adorned it for them, called them to it. ﴿From their right﴾: from the direction of their good deeds, he slowed them down from them. ﴿From their left﴾: he adorned for them the evil deeds and sins, called them to them and commanded them with them. Beware, son of Adam, from every direction, except that he did not come to you from above you, and he could not come between you and the mercy of Allah."

Al-Hakam and al-Suddi said: ﴿I will come to them from before them﴾: meaning the world. I call them to it, make them desire it and adorn it for them. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the direction of the Hereafter; I cast doubt on them and hinder them concerning it. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of the truth; I turn them away from it and test them regarding it. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of falsehood; I make it light for them, adorn it for them and make them desire it.

Mujahid said: ﴿From before them and from their right﴾: from where they see; ﴿and from behind them and from their left﴾: from where they do not see. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of His saying "from where they see" is: they err where they know they are erring, and "where they do not see" means they do not know they are erring.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿Then I will come to them from before them﴾: from the direction of their Hereafter; I inform them that there is no Paradise, no Fire and no resurrection. ﴿And from behind them﴾: from the direction of their worldly life; so I command them to gather wealth, not giving its due, and I frighten them with the loss of their offspring. ﴿And from their right﴾: from the direction of their religion; I make clear to each people what they used to worship, and if they were upon guidance, I confuse it for them until I take them out of it. ﴿And from their left﴾: from the direction of desires and pleasures; I make them attractive to them.

Shaqiq ibn Ibrahim said: "Every morning Shaytan sits in wait for me in four positions: from before me, behind me, on my right and on my left. As for from before me, I say: 'Do not grieve, for Allah is Forgiving and Merciful,' and He says that for ﴿those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and then are guided﴾. As for from behind me, he frightens me with loss for my dependants and family, and I say: ﴿There is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah﴾. As for from my right, he comes to me from the direction of praise, and I say: ﴿And the final outcome is for the righteous.﴾ As for from my left, he comes to me from the direction of desires and pleasures, and I say: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire.﴾"

﴿And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ Allah the Mighty and Majestic said to Iblis: ﴿Get out of it, reproached and expelled.﴾ That is: "blamed." Dhaʾm (reproach) and dhaʾm (blame) are the most severe defect, and it is more emphatic than "dhamm." It is said: "He reproached him, reproaches him, reproach, so he is reproached," and "dha'ama," "yadhaʾmuhu," "dhaʾman," "so he is madhʾum, and the reproach was made with 'dhamm,' 'dhaym,'" like "sar, yasir," so he is "mudhaym." Al-madhḥūr (the expelled) is the one pushed away. It is said: "daḥarahu, yadḥaruhu, daḥran," if he removed him and drove him away.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "﴿Madhʾūman﴾ means: turned away from him; ﴿madhʾūman madhḥūran﴾ means: not expelled." Al-Rabiʿ and Mujahid said: ﴿Madhʾūman﴾ means "detested." Ṭāʾūs narrated: "Madhʾūman, detested." Abu al-ʿĀliyah said: "Madhʾūman, disgraced by it."

Al-Kalbi said: "Madhʾūman, blamed; madhḥūran, removed from Paradise and from all good." ʿAṭāʾ said: "Madhʾūman, cursed."

Al-Kisaʾi said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one despised." Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one imprisoned." Abban, from Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad, said: "Al-madhʾūm is the one defective."

Al-Aʿshā said:

"A tribe said, when they saw me, and the beautiful woman does not lack blame."

﴿Whoever follows you of them﴾, of the children of Adam, ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾, with you and your offspring, and with the disbelieving offspring of Adam, ﴿all together.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 19–25:**

﴿Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Then Satan whispered to them﴾, meaning he spoke to them, and its meaning is: he conveyed suggestions to them, ﴿in order to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾, meaning, to make apparent to them what had been covered and hidden from them of their nakedness. Wahb said: there was a light upon them that prevented them from seeing their private parts. Then he explained the whisper: ﴿And he said, "Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or become of the eternal."﴾ Meaning: lest you become angels, or out of dislike that you should become angels who do good and evil.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and Yahya ibn Abi Ma'in read ﴿malikayn﴾ (angels) with a kasra on the lam, deriving it from His words: ﴿"Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾

﴿Or become of the eternal﴾, meaning, of those who remain and do not die.

﴿And he swore to them﴾, meaning he swore an oath and made them a promise. The word ﴿qasama﴾ is of the form of mufa'ala (reciprocal), though the act is from one party, like *mu'afah* (pardon) and *mu'aqabah* (retaliation) and *munawalah* (handing over).

Khalid ibn Zuhayr said:

*And he swore to them by God, with utmost effort, that you are*
*sweeter than manna when its honey is drawn out.* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/186.]]

Qatadah said: he swore to them by God, the Mighty and Majestic, until he deceived them, and a believer may be deceived by God. He said: "I was created before you and I know more than you, so follow me and I will guide you." Some scholars used to say: whoever deceives us by God, has deceived us.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The believer is trusting and generous, and the wicked is cunning and base." [174] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/394.]]

[And] Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi related in some of it, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib recited to us, saying: Nafṭawayh recited to us:

*Indeed the generous, when you wish, you can deceive him,*
*but you will find the base, experienced, not deceived.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/180.]]

﴿"Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisors."﴾ ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾, meaning he deceived them. It is said: "So-and-so continued to *yudli* (lower/lead on) so-and-so," meaning he kept making him aware, i.e., he kept misleading him and speaking to him with false, ornate words. Muqatil said: he made the falsehood appear attractive to them.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: the meaning is that they fell into deception. It is said: "He *tadalla* (lowered himself) by himself and *dalla* (lowered) another." Descent (*tadalli*) occurs only from a height to a lower place. It was also said that the original form was *dallahuma*, and one of the two lams was replaced by a yā', like His words ﴿*yatamatta*﴾ and ﴿*dassaha*﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: *dallahuma* means he took them down, and both derive from *tadlin al-dalw*, when one lowers the bucket into the well to fill it.

﴿So when they tasted the tree﴾, they ate from it, and it reached their bellies. ﴿Their private parts became apparent to them﴾, meaning their nakedness, ﴿and they began to fasten upon themselves﴾ their clothing fell away from them, so that each of them saw the other's nakedness, which had been hidden from them, and they had not been seeing it before.

Qatadah said: the clothing of Adam and Eve in the Garden was a nail-like covering (*zufr*) of light; when they committed the sin, it was stripped from them and their private parts became apparent, so they felt shame. ﴿And they began to join together﴾ [meaning: to fasten/ attach], [and to tie and tear and sew] ﴿upon themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾, which is the leaf of the fig, until it took the shape of a garment; and from this comes the word *khasf* (sewing) of the sandal.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Adam was a [tall] man, as if he were a [tall] palm tree, with abundant hair on his head. When he fell into the sin, his private parts became apparent to him, which he had not been seeing, so he fled running in the Garden. A tree from the trees of the Garden came before him, and it caught hold of him, and he said: 'Release me.' It said: 'I will not release you.' So his Lord called out: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, my Lord, but I am ashamed before You.'" [175] [[al-Mustadrak: 2/262. The *sahuq* palm is the tall one whose fruit is out of reach for the picker.]]

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Adam: "Did you not have, in what I permitted and granted you of the Garden, a sufficiency apart from the tree?" He said: "I kept my covenant, but I did not think that any of Your creation would swear by You falsely." He said: "By My might, I will bring you down to the earth, and you will not attain life except with hardship [only with toil]. Descend from the Garden." So they used to eat in ease, until they came to a state of hardship, of food and drink. He taught him the craft of iron, and commanded him to plough, so he ploughed and sowed, then irrigated until it was harvested. Then he ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate, then swallowed, until he reached what God willed him to reach.

﴿And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree?"﴾ [the verse]. Muhammad ibn Qays said: his Lord called out to him: "O Adam, why did you eat from it, when I had forbidden you?" He said: "My Lord, Eve fed me." He said to Eve: "Why did you feed him?" She said: "The serpent informed me." He said to the serpent: "Why did you command her?" She said: "Iblis commanded me." God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "As for you, O Eve, as you caused the tree to bleed, [so I will cause you to bleed]" [this is a metaphor for menstruation]; "as for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs, so you will walk upon your face, and the dust will be your food, and your head will be struck by whoever meets you; and as for you, O Iblis, you are cursed and expelled."

They said: ﴿"Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾, meaning the ruined. ﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾ ﴿He said: "Therein you will live﴾, meaning on the earth, ﴿and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾

﴿So when they tasted the tree﴾, they ate from it, and it reached their bellies. ﴿Their private parts became apparent to them﴾, meaning their nakedness, ﴿and they began to fasten upon themselves﴾ their clothing fell away from them, so that each of them saw the other's nakedness, which had been hidden from them, and they had not been seeing it before.

Qatadah said: the clothing of Adam and Eve in the Garden was a nail-like covering (*zufr*) of light; when they committed the sin, it was stripped from them and their private parts became apparent, so they felt shame. ﴿And they began to join together﴾ [meaning: to fasten/ attach], [and to tie and tear and sew] ﴿upon themselves from the leaves of the Garden﴾, which is the leaf of the fig, until it took the shape of a garment; and from this comes the word *khasf* (sewing) of the sandal.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Adam was a [tall] man, as if he were a [tall] palm tree, with abundant hair on his head. When he fell into the sin, his private parts became apparent to him, which he had not been seeing, so he fled running in the Garden. A tree from the trees of the Garden came before him, and it caught hold of him, and he said: 'Release me.' It said: 'I will not release you.' So his Lord called out: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' He said: 'No, my Lord, but I am ashamed before You.'" [175] [[al-Mustadrak: 2/262. The *sahuq* palm is the tall one whose fruit is out of reach for the picker.]]

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, said to Adam: "Did you not have, in what I permitted and granted you of the Garden, a sufficiency apart from the tree?" He said: "I kept my covenant, but I did not think that any of Your creation would swear by You falsely." He said: "By My might, I will bring you down to the earth, and you will not attain life except with hardship [only with toil]. Descend from the Garden." So they used to eat in ease, until they came to a state of hardship, of food and drink. He taught him the craft of iron, and commanded him to plough, so he ploughed and sowed, then irrigated until it was harvested. Then he ground it, then kneaded it, then baked it, then ate, then swallowed, until he reached what God willed him to reach.

﴿And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree?"﴾ [the verse]. Muhammad ibn Qays said: his Lord called out to him: "O Adam, why did you eat from it, when I had forbidden you?" He said: "My Lord, Eve fed me." He said to Eve: "Why did you feed him?" She said: "The serpent informed me." He said to the serpent: "Why did you command her?" She said: "Iblis commanded me." God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "As for you, O Eve, as you caused the tree to bleed, [so I will cause you to bleed]" [this is a metaphor for menstruation]; "as for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs, so you will walk upon your face, and the dust will be your food, and your head will be struck by whoever meets you; and as for you, O Iblis, you are cursed and expelled."

They said: ﴿"Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾, meaning the ruined. ﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾ ﴿He said: "Therein you will live﴾, meaning on the earth, ﴿and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 26–30:

﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you﴾ means: We created for you. It is also said: We sent down its means and its instruments, because [the Creator] is the one who [establishes] by what He says.

It is also said: [it was sent down by the decree], like the rest of His creation. This is because the Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked. His words ﴿clothing﴾ refer to what is worn of garments, ﴿to cover your private parts﴾, meaning your nakedness. Its singular is *sawah*, which is a form derived from *al-su'* (evil), and it was called *sawah* because its exposure from the body distresses its owner. ﴿And as finery﴾ means wealth, according to the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. Then [another] said: "al-Rish" is the man when [his condition is good]. Ibn Zayd said: "al-Rish" means beauty.

It is also said: it is clothing. Abu 'Amr related that the Arabs say: "So-and-so gave me a *rishah*," meaning a covering and equipment.

'Uthman ibn 'Affan, al-Hasan, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Abu Raja' and Qatadah read *wa-riyashan* with an alif, which is the plural of *rish*, like *dhi'b* and *dhiyab*, *bir* and *biyar*, *qadh* and *qidah*.

Qutrub said: *al-rish* and *al-riyash* are one and the same, like your saying *dabagh* and *dibagh*, *labis* and *libas*, *hill* and *halal*, *haram* and *haram*. It may also be a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "He fletched it toward him with its feather (*rashahu ilayhi bi-rishihi*), *riyashan*."

In the speech of the Arabs, *al-riyash* means furnishings, what is visible of goods, garments, bedding and other things. Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-riyash* is clothing, livelihood and comfort. al-Akhfash said: *al-riyash* is abundance and means of living.

﴿And the clothing of piety, that is best﴾. The people of Madina and Syria, and al-Kisa'i, read *wa-libasa al-taqwa* with the accusative, as a conjunction to *al-rish*. The rest read it with the nominative, as a beginning, and its predicate is (*khayr*, "best").

They considered that to be a connecting element in the speech. Likewise Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b read: *wa-libas al-taqwa khayr*. They differed concerning what the clothing of piety is, whether it indicates the coat of mail, the arm-guards, the shin-guards, and the instruments by which one protects oneself in war against the enemy.

Qatadah, al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: the clothing of piety is faith. Ma'bad al-Juhani said: it is modesty. Abu al-Qasim al-Sadusi recited to me, saying: Abu 'Urabah al-Dawsi recited to me on its meaning:

"It is as if I see the one without shame or trust
among people, naked."

'Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is righteous deeds. al-Dhabbal ibn 'Amr related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: it is good bearing in the face.

al-Hasan said: I saw 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) on the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wearing a shirt of *qawhi* [an attribution to al-Qawha', with a *damma*, which is a town between Nishapur and Herat; he means a type of white garment], with its button undone. I heard him order the killing of dogs and forbid playing with pigeons. Then he said: "O people, fear Allah regarding these hidden matters, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'By He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one has ever done a deed in secret except that Allah clothes him with its garment openly; if it is good, then it is good, and if it is evil, then it is evil.'" [176] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/216.]] Then he recited this verse: ﴿And as finery, and the clothing of piety, that is best﴾ and said: it is good bearing.

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: ﴿the clothing of piety﴾ is fear of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: it is a covering for the nakedness, by which one fears Allah and so covers his nakedness. ﴿That is among the signs of Allah, that they may remember﴾.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Faith is naked; its clothing is piety, its adornment is modesty, its fruit is jurisprudence, its beauty is chastity, and its produce is righteous deeds.

﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you﴾, meaning: let him not teach you, nor make you slip, so that you would show your opinion to people in circumambulation, through your obedience. ﴿As he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts﴾. ﴿Indeed, he sees you﴾, meaning Satan, ﴿he and his tribe﴾, meaning his horsemen and his soldiers, who are the jinn and the devils, ﴿from where you do not see them﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: [his tribe] means his offspring. Mujahid said: Iblis said: "He has given us four [abilities]: we see and are not seen, and we emerge from beneath the earth." Our shaykh returns to say: a youth.

Malik ibn Dinar said: Indeed, the enemy sees you and you do not see him, which is a severe burden, except for those whom Allah protects.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard my father say: I heard 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi say: "Satan is ancient and you are new; Satan is gentle and you are delicate in your side; Satan sees you and you do not see him; Satan does not forget you and you never cease to forget him; and from yourself you have an aid for him, while you have no aid from him."

It is also said: the chest of the son of Adam is a dwelling for him, and he flows through the son of Adam in the way of blood, and he cannot be withstood except by the help of Allah. From this [a poet] says: "And I do not see him from where he sees me; and when I forget him, he does not forget me. So my master, if You do not rescue [me], he will take me captive as he took Adam from Your gardens."

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: "If he sees you from where you do not see him, then Allah sees him from where he does not see Allah; so seek Allah's help against him." ﴿Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak﴾.

﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe﴾, meaning helpers and companions. ﴿And when they commit an immorality﴾, and their immorality was that they circumambulated the House naked: men by day and women by night. They would say: "We circumambulate as our mothers bore us, and we do not circumambulate in the garments in which we have committed sins."

A woman would place upon her private part a girdle or something, and say:

"Today some of it or all of it appears,
and what appears of it, I do not make lawful."

In the verse there is an implied meaning, which is: ﴿And when they commit an immorality and are forbidden from it, they say: "We found our fathers doing it"﴾. It was said: "From where did your fathers take it?" They said: ﴿"And Allah has commanded us with it."﴾ ﴿Say: "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?"﴾ ﴿Say: "My Lord has commanded justice."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] "there is no god but Allah." al-Dahhak said: monotheism. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: justice.

﴿And set your faces [toward prostration] at every masjid﴾. Mujahid, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: it means direct your faces wherever you are in prayer toward the Ka'bah.

al-Dahhak said: when the prayer comes and you are at the masjid, pray in it, and do not say: "I would love to pray in my own masjid." And if one is not near a masjid, then let him go to any masjid and pray in it.

al-Rabi' said: its meaning is: make your prostration to Allah, the Exalted, sincere, apart from anything other than Him of the gods and rivals. ﴿And call upon Him﴾, meaning worship Him, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, meaning obedience and worship. ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every soul will be resurrected upon what it was upon." [177] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/206.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, the Exalted, began the creation of the son of Adam as believer and disbeliever, as He said: ﴿He is the One who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [[Surat al-Taghabun: 2.]], then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection just as He began their creation, disbeliever and believer. So the believer is raised as a believer and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

Jabir said: they will be raised upon what they died upon: the believer upon his faith, and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy. Abu al-'Aliyah said: they returned to His knowledge concerning them.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: whoever's creation began upon wretchedness will end up at what his creation began upon, even if he works the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis worked the deeds of the people of happiness and ended up at what his creation began upon. And whoever's creation began upon happiness will end up at what his creation began upon, even if he works the deeds of the people of wretchedness, just as the magicians worked the deeds of the people of wretchedness and then ended up at what their creation began upon.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its meaning is: as it was written for you, they will be as such, similar to His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾.

Qatadah said: He created you from dust and to dust you will return, similar to His saying: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 55.]].

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿As He originated you﴾ naked, ﴿you will return﴾ to them naked. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 94.]].

al-Suddi said: as He created you, a group guided and a group astray, so you will return: you will come out from the bellies of your mothers. al-Hasan and Mujahid said: ﴿As He originated you﴾, meaning He created you, a group guided and a group astray. ﴿So you will return﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [[Surat al-Anbiya': 104.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "People will be gathered barefoot and naked, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." [178] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/223.]] Then he recited: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾.

﴿A group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was justly decreed. Indeed, they took the devils as allies, as lords, besides Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, the Exalted, began the creation of the son of Adam as believer and disbeliever, as He said: ﴿He is the One who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [[Surat al-Taghabun: 2.]], then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection just as He began their creation, disbeliever and believer. So the believer is raised as a believer and the disbeliever as a disbeliever.

Jabir said: they will be raised upon what they died upon: the believer upon his faith, and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy. Abu al-'Aliyah said: they returned to His knowledge concerning them.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: whoever's creation began upon wretchedness will end up at what his creation began upon, even if he works the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis worked the deeds of the people of happiness and ended up at what his creation began upon. And whoever's creation began upon happiness will end up at what his creation began upon, even if he works the deeds of the people of wretchedness, just as the magicians worked the deeds of the people of wretchedness and then ended up at what their creation began upon.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: its meaning is: as it was written for you, they will be as such, similar to His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾.

Qatadah said: He created you from dust and to dust you will return, similar to His saying: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out﴾ [[Surat Ta-Ha: 55.]].

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿As He originated you﴾ naked, ﴿you will return﴾ to them naked. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾ [[Surat al-An'am: 94.]].

al-Suddi said: as He created you, a group guided and a group astray, so you will return: you will come out from the bellies of your mothers. al-Hasan and Mujahid said: ﴿As He originated you﴾, meaning He created you, a group guided and a group astray. ﴿So you will return﴾ on the Day of Resurrection. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [[Surat al-Anbiya': 104.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "People will be gathered barefoot and naked, and the first to be clothed will be Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." [178] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/223.]] Then he recited: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾.

﴿A group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was justly decreed. Indeed, they took the devils as allies, as lords, besides Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾

**Al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan), commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 31–36:**

O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship. The exegetes (mufassirun) said: In the pre-Islamic period, the Banu Amir would circumambulate the House naked, the men by day and the women by night. When they came to the mosque at Mina, one of them would place his garments in his baggage, and if he performed the circumambulation while wearing them, they would be struck and torn from him. So God Most High revealed: *O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of worship*, meaning clothing.

Mujahid said: "It is that with which you cover your nakedness for prayer and circumambulation." 'Ata', Abu Rawq and Abu Razin said: "It is the comb." (Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/127.)

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Haytham [al-Juhani] relate from al-Sanukhi the judge: *take your adornment at every place of worship* means raising the hands at the times of prayer.

'Ali narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) in a report, the words of Jibril (peace be upon him) to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, everything has an adornment, and the adornment of prayer is raising the hands in it at three points: when you say the opening takbir [for prayer], when you bow, and when you raise your head from bowing." [179]

*And eat and drink.*

Al-Kalbi said: The Banu Amir would not eat anything except the minimum, and would not eat fatty food during the days of their pilgrimage, thereby magnifying their pilgrimage. The Muslims said: "O Messenger of God, we have a better right to do that," so God Most High revealed *and eat*, meaning meat and fat, *and drink, but do not be excessive*, meaning what is forbidden.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Eat what you wish and wear what you wish, so long as no excess or conceit touches you." Mujahid said: "Extravagance is falling short of God's right. He also said: If you spent the equivalent of Mount Uhud in obedience to God, it would not be extravagance; but if you spent a single dirham or a mudd in disobedience to God, it would be extravagance."

Al-Kalbi said: *and do not be excessive*, meaning do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you... *Indeed, He does not love the excessive*, those who transgress by committing what is forbidden in food and drink.

It has reached me that al-Rashid had a skilled Christian physician, and he said to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid: "There is no knowledge of medicine in your Book, and knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge of religions and knowledge of bodies." 'Ali said: "God has gathered all of medicine into half a verse of our Book." He asked: "And what is it?" He said: God's words: *Eat and drink, but do not be excessive; indeed, He does not love the excessive.* The Christian said: "And is nothing reported from your Messenger regarding medicine?"

'Ali said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gathered medicine in a few words." He asked: "And what are they?" He said: his saying: "The stomach is the house of disease, dieting (al-himya) is the head of every remedy, and give every body what it is accustomed to." [180] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/192.]

The Christian said: "Neither your Book nor your Prophet left any medicine for Galen."

*Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants?* meaning the clothing, *and the good things of provision?* Ibn Zayd said: "There were people who, when they performed the pilgrimage or the minor pilgrimage (umra), forbade themselves sheep, and what came from them, their milk, their fat, their meat and their tallow. So God Most High revealed: *Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has brought forth for His servants?* to the end of the verse."

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "By the good things of provision is meant what the people of the pre-Islamic period had forbidden of the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and left free), the *sa'iba* (a beast set free for the gods), the *wasila* (a ewe that bore twins in succession) and the *ham* (a stallion camel freed after a certain number of covers)." *Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world, exclusively on the Day of Resurrection.* Ibn 'Abbas said: "The believers share the good things of this world with the polytheists. They ate of the good of their food and wore the fine of their clothes, and married as they did... Then God purifies the good things in the Hereafter for those who believed, and the polytheists have no share in them. The meaning of the verse is: *Say: they are for those who believed*, shared in this world, and especially on the Day of Resurrection."

The reading of Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and Nafi' is *khalisatun* with a *damma*, meaning: *Say: they are khalisa* (pure). The rest read it in the accusative (*khalisatan*) as a circumstantial qualifier (*qat'*), because the statement is complete without it.

*Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.*

*Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies (al-fawahish)*, meaning circumambulating naked, *what is apparent of them*, the men's circumambulation by day, *and what is hidden*, the women's circumambulation by night.

It was also said: they are fornication and *al-mukhalla* (illicit intimacy with men).

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one is more fond of praise than God, Glorified is He; for this reason He praised Himself. No one is more jealous than God; for this reason He forbade the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. And no one loves excuse more than God, Mighty and Majestic; for this reason He sent down the Book and sent the Messengers." [181] [Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/602.]

*And sin (al-ithm)*, meaning the wrong and disobedience. Al-Hasan said: "Al-ithm is wine." A poet said:

*I drank sin until my reason was overshadowed, and so it is: sin takes away the minds.*

Another said:

*We drink sin from the cup openly, and we see intoxication borrowed among us.*

*And transgression (al-baghy)*, which is injustice *without right*. *And that you associate with God what He has not sent down any authority (sultan) for*, meaning proof and evidence. *And that you say about God what you do not know*, such as the forbidding of clothing and food.

*And for every nation there is a term (ajal)*, a period and a fixed time. It was also said: the time of the arrival of punishment and the first of the torment. *So when their term comes*, when their appointed time ends. Ibn Sirin read *ajalahum* (their terms). *They cannot delay an hour*, meaning they do not postpone it, *nor can they advance it*, meaning they do not go ahead of it.

*O Children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves*: a conditional clause, meaning: if they come to you [and it is established], then whoever remains (righteous) will be safe. It was also said: then obey them. Muqatil said: By his words *O Children of Adam* He meant: do not associate partners with the Lord; and by "the messengers" He meant Muhammad (ﷺ) alone. *Who recount My signs to you, then whoever fears God and sets his deeds right, there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve. But those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them*, that is, toward belief in Muhammad and the Qur'an, *those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.*
