Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 7, verses 37–43:

﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of the Book﴾: their allotted share (ḥazz) of what was written for them in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Abu Salih said: it means what their deeds have earned for them of punishment.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and 'Ata' said: it means what has preceded for them of wretchedness and happiness. Bakr al-Tawil narrated from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: "People who will do deeds that they must do, but have not yet done them." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: it means their deeds and what has been decreed for them of good or evil; whoever does good will be recompensed for it, and whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Mujahid reported from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: it is what has been promised of good and evil.

'Ata' reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "What has been decreed for them will reach them, and it has been decreed for those who invent lies against Allah that their faces will be blackened," as evidenced by His saying ﴿On that Day, faces will be blackened﴾ [Surah 3:106].[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/225.]]

Al-Rabi', al-Qurazi and Ibn Zayd said: it means what has been decreed for them of provisions, deeds and lifespans. When these are exhausted and [their ruin is complete], ﴿until when Our messengers come to them, taking their souls﴾: they seize their spirits, meaning the Angel of Death and his helpers. ﴿They will say: "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?"﴾, meaning worship. ﴿They will say: "They have strayed from us,"﴾ that is, they have busied themselves with themselves. ﴿And they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾, that is, they acknowledge it. [They said: "We bear witness"] against ourselves [that the messengers delivered the message], and the life of this world deceived them, and they bore witness and acknowledged against themselves that they had been disbelievers.

﴿He will say: "Enter"﴾: Allah, mighty and majestic, says to them on the Day of Resurrection: "Enter" ﴿among nations that passed away before you, of jinn and mankind, into the Fire﴾, meaning the disbelievers of the earlier nations. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ in religion and creed, and it did not say "brother" because it meant by it the community (ummah). So the polytheists curse the polytheists, the Jews the Jews, likewise the Christians the Christians and the Magians the Magians. And the followers curse the leaders, saying: ﴿"May Allah curse you; you deceived us."﴾ Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿until, when they have overtaken one another therein, all together﴾, that is, they have caught up with one another. Al-A'mash recited: "hatta idha tadaraku" (until they have overtaken one another), in the original form. Al-Nakha'i recited: "hatta idha addarku," with the dal pronounced heavy and without an alif, meaning: they were brought down to the lowest level (al-darak).

﴿The last of them will say﴾: Muqatil said: it means the last of them in entering the Fire, and they are the followers, ﴿concerning the first of them﴾, and they are the leaders.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The last of them" means the last of the nations, and "the first of them" means the first of the nations. Al-Suddi said: "The last of them" means those who were in the last times, and "the first of them" means those who established that religion for them. ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray from guidance,"﴾ meaning corruption. ﴿So give them a double punishment in the Fire﴾, that is, give them a multiplied punishment from the Fire. He says: ﴿"For each there is double,"﴾ of punishment, ﴿but you do not know﴾ until it befalls you.

﴿The first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no superiority over us,"﴾ because you disbelieved as he disbelieved, and we and you were equal in disbelief and likewise in punishment. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them﴾ (the doors) ﴿will not have the gates of heaven opened for them.﴾ It is recited with the ya' and with the ta', and both with and without the shaddah. It means: their spirits and deeds are not raised, because they are wicked, so they do not ascend; rather they are cast down to a prison (sijjin) beneath the rock that lies under the earths.

Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "When the dying person is attended by the angels, if he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come forth, O good soul that was in the good body; come forth praised, and rejoice in a spirit from Allah, and sweet provision, and a Lord not angry.' They keep saying this until it departs; then it is raised up to heaven, and it is opened for it, and it is asked: 'Who is this?' [It is said: 'So-and-so.'] They say: 'Welcome to the good soul that was in the good body. Enter praised, and rejoice in spirit, sweet provision and a Lord not angry.' It is told this until it is raised to the seventh heaven.

"But if he is a wicked man, they say: 'Come forth, O wicked soul that was in the wicked body; come forth blameworthy, and receive the news of boiling water and dark, pus-like liquid, and other punishments of similar kind.' They keep saying this until it departs; then it is raised to heaven, and it is opened for it, and it is asked: 'Who is this?' They say: 'So-and-so.' They say: 'No welcome to the wicked soul that was in the wicked body. Return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' Then it is sent down from heaven and from earth, and it goes to the grave."[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/364.]]

﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾: meaning, a camel enters the hole of a needle. [This is a parable, and the "needle" (sammu) is the needle.]

'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited: "al-Jummal," with the jim vowelled with a damma and the mim with a shaddah. It is the rope of a ship, and it is called "al-Fals." 'Ikrimah said: it is the rope by which one climbs up to the palm trees. ﴿Thus We recompense the criminals﴾. ﴿For them from Hell will be a bed,﴾ a bedding of fire, ﴿and above them coverings﴾. The word is the plural of ghashiyah, which is what covers and envelops them. Al-Qurazi and Mujahid said: they are quilts. ﴿Thus We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-Bara' said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The disbeliever will be clothed with two sheets of fire in his grave."[182][[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/85.]] That is His saying: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them coverings.﴾

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds — We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability, and what it can bear and what is lawful for it, so that it does not go beyond it and it is not constrained by it. ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.﴾ ﴿And We will remove what is in their breasts﴾, meaning their hearts, ﴿of resentment,﴾ hatred and enmity which existed among some of them toward others in the world. ﴿And We make them brothers, upon couches facing one another﴾, none envying another for anything which Allah has favoured some of them with and given them preference in.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, he said: "By Allah, it was revealed concerning us, the People of the House: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts of resentment, as brothers upon couches facing one another.﴾"[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/450, no. 4472; Fada'il al-Sahabah of Ahmad: 2/597, no. 1018.]]

'Ali (may Allah honour his face) also said: "I hope that I, 'Uthman, Talhah and al-Zubayr are among those of whom Allah said: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts,﴾ the verse."[[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq: 2/228.]]

Al-Suddi said concerning this verse: When the people of Paradise are led to Paradise, they find at the gate of it a tree at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They drink from one of them, and so what is in their breasts of resentment is removed; that is the pure drink. They wash from the other, and the radiance of bliss flows over them, so they never become disheveled or dirty thereafter.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/241.]]

Al-Jaza'iri narrated from Abu Nadrah, he said: The people of Paradise will be detained until retribution is taken between some of them and others, until they enter Paradise at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other. And the people of the Fire will be detained before the Fire until retribution is taken between some of them and others, and they will enter the Fire at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other.

﴿Rivers flow beneath them,﴾ ﴿and they say: "Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this,"﴾ that is, who granted us success and guided us to this, meaning the way to Paradise. Sufyan al-Thawri said: its meaning is "Praise be to Allah who guided us to the deed of this, its reward." ﴿And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us.﴾

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every people of the Fire sees the station of those in Paradise, and they say: 'If only Allah had guided us, we would have been among the believers.' And every people of Paradise sees the station of those in the Fire, and they say: 'Had it not been that Allah guided us.' This is their gratitude." He said: "There is no disbeliever or believer except that he has a station in Paradise or in the Fire. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and they enter their stations, Paradise is raised for the people of the Fire, and they look at their stations in it. It is said to them: 'These are your stations, had you obeyed Allah.' Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, inherit them by what you used to do.' Then the stations are divided among the people of Paradise, and it is proclaimed: 'Be healthy and never fall ill; live forever and never die; enjoy and never despair; be young and never grow old.'"[[See Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 8/243, with variations.]]

[They said: "We bear witness"] against ourselves [that the messengers delivered the message], and the life of this world deceived them, and they bore witness and acknowledged against themselves that they had been disbelievers.

﴿He will say: "Enter"﴾: Allah, mighty and majestic, says to them on the Day of Resurrection: "Enter" ﴿among nations that passed away before you, of jinn and mankind, into the Fire﴾, meaning the disbelievers of the earlier nations. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ in religion and creed, and it did not say "brother" because it meant by it the community (ummah). So the polytheists curse the polytheists, the Jews the Jews, likewise the Christians the Christians and the Magians the Magians. And the followers curse the leaders, saying: ﴿"May Allah curse you; you deceived us."﴾ Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿until, when they have overtaken one another therein, all together﴾, that is, they have caught up with one another. Al-A'mash recited: "hatta idha tadaraku" (until they have overtaken one another), in the original form. Al-Nakha'i recited: "hatta idha addarku," with the dal pronounced heavy and without an alif, meaning: they were brought down to the lowest level (al-darak).

﴿The last of them will say﴾: Muqatil said: it means the last of them in entering the Fire, and they are the followers, ﴿concerning the first of them﴾, and they are the leaders.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The last of them" means the last of the nations, and "the first of them" means the first of the nations. Al-Suddi said: "The last of them" means those who were in the last times, and "the first of them" means those who established that religion for them. ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray from guidance,"﴾ meaning corruption. ﴿So give them a double punishment in the Fire﴾, that is, give them a multiplied punishment from the Fire. He says: ﴿"For each there is double,"﴾ of punishment, ﴿but you do not know﴾ until it befalls you.

﴿The first of them will say to the last of them: "You had no superiority over us,"﴾ because you disbelieved as he disbelieved, and we and you were equal in disbelief and likewise in punishment. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them﴾ (the doors) ﴿will not have the gates of heaven opened for them.﴾ It is recited with the ya' and with the ta', and both with and without the shaddah. It means: their spirits and deeds are not raised, because they are wicked, so they do not ascend; rather they are cast down to a prison (sijjin) beneath the rock that lies under the earths.

Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "When the dying person is attended by the angels, if he is a righteous man, they say: 'Come forth, O good soul that was in the good body; come forth praised, and rejoice in a spirit from Allah, and sweet provision, and a Lord not angry.' They keep saying this until it departs; then it is raised up to heaven, and it is opened for it, and it is asked: 'Who is this?' [It is said: 'So-and-so.'] They say: 'Welcome to the good soul that was in the good body. Enter praised, and rejoice in spirit, sweet provision and a Lord not angry.' It is told this until it is raised to the seventh heaven.

"But if he is a wicked man, they say: 'Come forth, O wicked soul that was in the wicked body; come forth blameworthy, and receive the news of boiling water and dark, pus-like liquid, and other punishments of similar kind.' They keep saying this until it departs; then it is raised to heaven, and it is opened for it, and it is asked: 'Who is this?' They say: 'So-and-so.' They say: 'No welcome to the wicked soul that was in the wicked body. Return blameworthy, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you.' Then it is sent down from heaven and from earth, and it goes to the grave."[[Musnad Ahmad: 2/364.]]

﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾: meaning, a camel enters the hole of a needle. [This is a parable, and the "needle" (sammu) is the needle.]

'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited: "al-Jummal," with the jim vowelled with a damma and the mim with a shaddah. It is the rope of a ship, and it is called "al-Fals." 'Ikrimah said: it is the rope by which one climbs up to the palm trees. ﴿Thus We recompense the criminals﴾. ﴿For them from Hell will be a bed,﴾ a bedding of fire, ﴿and above them coverings﴾. The word is the plural of ghashiyah, which is what covers and envelops them. Al-Qurazi and Mujahid said: they are quilts. ﴿Thus We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-Bara' said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The disbeliever will be clothed with two sheets of fire in his grave."[182][[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/85.]] That is His saying: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them coverings.﴾

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds — We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability, and what it can bear and what is lawful for it, so that it does not go beyond it and it is not constrained by it. ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.﴾ ﴿And We will remove what is in their breasts﴾, meaning their hearts, ﴿of resentment,﴾ hatred and enmity which existed among some of them toward others in the world. ﴿And We make them brothers, upon couches facing one another﴾, none envying another for anything which Allah has favoured some of them with and given them preference in.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, he said: "By Allah, it was revealed concerning us, the People of the House: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts of resentment, as brothers upon couches facing one another.﴾"[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/450, no. 4472; Fada'il al-Sahabah of Ahmad: 2/597, no. 1018.]]

'Ali (may Allah honour his face) also said: "I hope that I, 'Uthman, Talhah and al-Zubayr are among those of whom Allah said: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts,﴾ the verse."[[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq: 2/228.]]

Al-Suddi said concerning this verse: When the people of Paradise are led to Paradise, they find at the gate of it a tree at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They drink from one of them, and so what is in their breasts of resentment is removed; that is the pure drink. They wash from the other, and the radiance of bliss flows over them, so they never become disheveled or dirty thereafter.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/241.]]

Al-Jaza'iri narrated from Abu Nadrah, he said: The people of Paradise will be detained until retribution is taken between some of them and others, until they enter Paradise at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other. And the people of the Fire will be detained before the Fire until retribution is taken between some of them and others, and they will enter the Fire at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other.

﴿Rivers flow beneath them,﴾ ﴿and they say: "Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this,"﴾ that is, who granted us success and guided us to this, meaning the way to Paradise. Sufyan al-Thawri said: its meaning is "Praise be to Allah who guided us to the deed of this, its reward." ﴿And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us.﴾

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every people of the Fire sees the station of those in Paradise, and they say: 'If only Allah had guided us, we would have been among the believers.' And every people of Paradise sees the station of those in the Fire, and they say: 'Had it not been that Allah guided us.' This is their gratitude." He said: "There is no disbeliever or believer except that he has a station in Paradise or in the Fire. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and they enter their stations, Paradise is raised for the people of the Fire, and they look at their stations in it. It is said to them: 'These are your stations, had you obeyed Allah.' Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, inherit them by what you used to do.' Then the stations are divided among the people of Paradise, and it is proclaimed: 'Be healthy and never fall ill; live forever and never die; enjoy and never despair; be young and never grow old.'"[[See Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 8/243, with variations.]]

Al-Bara' said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The disbeliever will be clothed with two sheets of fire in his grave."[182][[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/85.]] That is His saying: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them coverings.﴾

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds — We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability, and what it can bear and what is lawful for it, so that it does not go beyond it and it is not constrained by it. ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever.﴾ ﴿And We will remove what is in their breasts﴾, meaning their hearts, ﴿of resentment,﴾ hatred and enmity which existed among some of them toward others in the world. ﴿And We make them brothers, upon couches facing one another﴾, none envying another for anything which Allah has favoured some of them with and given them preference in.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, he said: "By Allah, it was revealed concerning us, the People of the House: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts of resentment, as brothers upon couches facing one another.﴾"[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/450, no. 4472; Fada'il al-Sahabah of Ahmad: 2/597, no. 1018.]]

'Ali (may Allah honour his face) also said: "I hope that I, 'Uthman, Talhah and al-Zubayr are among those of whom Allah said: ﴿And We remove what is in their breasts,﴾ the verse."[[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq: 2/228.]]

Al-Suddi said concerning this verse: When the people of Paradise are led to Paradise, they find at the gate of it a tree at the base of whose trunk are two springs. They drink from one of them, and so what is in their breasts of resentment is removed; that is the pure drink. They wash from the other, and the radiance of bliss flows over them, so they never become disheveled or dirty thereafter.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/241.]]

Al-Jaza'iri narrated from Abu Nadrah, he said: The people of Paradise will be detained until retribution is taken between some of them and others, until they enter Paradise at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other. And the people of the Fire will be detained before the Fire until retribution is taken between some of them and others, and they will enter the Fire at the time of entering it, and none of them will demand from another any claim of injustice that one committed against the other.

﴿Rivers flow beneath them,﴾ ﴿and they say: "Praise be to Allah, who guided us to this,"﴾ that is, who granted us success and guided us to this, meaning the way to Paradise. Sufyan al-Thawri said: its meaning is "Praise be to Allah who guided us to the deed of this, its reward." ﴿And we would not have been guided had Allah not guided us.﴾

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every people of the Fire sees the station of those in Paradise, and they say: 'If only Allah had guided us, we would have been among the believers.' And every people of Paradise sees the station of those in the Fire, and they say: 'Had it not been that Allah guided us.' This is their gratitude." He said: "There is no disbeliever or believer except that he has a station in Paradise or in the Fire. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, and they enter their stations, Paradise is raised for the people of the Fire, and they look at their stations in it. It is said to them: 'These are your stations, had you obeyed Allah.' Then it is said: 'O people of Paradise, inherit them by what you used to do.' Then the stations are divided among the people of Paradise, and it is proclaimed: 'Be healthy and never fall ill; live forever and never die; enjoy and never despair; be young and never grow old.'"[[See Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 8/243, with variations.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 7, verses 44–51:**

﴿The companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?"﴾ [This is the statement of Muhammad ibn Jarir.] They will say, "Yes." Al-Kisa'i (a grammarian) said: "نَعَمْ" (*na'am*, "yes") is pronounced with a kasra on the ‘ayn, and it is also permissible to pronounce it with a sukun on the ‘ayn. Both are dialectal forms. ﴿Then a caller will call out between them: "The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers, the disbelievers, who turn away from the way of God," meaning the religion of God, "and seek to make it crooked," meaning they seek to make it deviant and bent. "And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter."﴾ ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾, meaning between the Garden and the Fire there is a barrier, a dividing wall. It is the wall that God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in His words: ﴿So a wall will be set up between them﴾ [57:13].

﴿And upon the A'raf﴾, meaning upon that barrier. Al-A'raf (the heights) is a wall between the Garden and the Fire. It is the plural of ‘urf, which is any elevated mound. From it comes the word ‘urf of the rooster, because it is raised above the rest of its body.

Al-Shammakh said:

*"She stood on raised ground, tall, as if her shapes were spears, aimed by the direction of the wind, planted firmly."*

It is narrated as: *"bi-a'raf qifalan"*, meaning *qifali*, i.e., they turned their necks toward one another. [She stood] "in a ravine of half-donkeys." He likened her figure to spears aimed by the wind's direction, i.e., the direction of the wind. His words *"bi-a'raf"* mean a rise in the ground.

Another poet said:

*"Every one firm of flesh, slender, like a banner raised above the heights."*

He means: every firm, slender one whose flesh is solid, and *al-kinaz* means solid.

Al-Suddi said: It was called A'raf because its people recognize (ya‘rifun) people. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is the Sirat (the bridge).

The scholars differed concerning the men whom God informed were upon the A'raf: who are they, and what was the reason they came to be there? Hudhayfah and Ibn ‘Abbas said: The companions of the A'raf are people whose good deeds and bad deeds were balanced equally, and their bad deeds kept them from the Garden, while their good deeds kept them from the Fire. So they stand there until God decides concerning them what He wills. Then He will admit them into the Garden by the bounty of His mercy. They are the last to enter the Garden. They recognize the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. When God wills to grant them well-being, He takes them to a river called the River of Life, whose two banks are of gold, adorned with pearls, and whose soil is musk. They bathe in it until their complexions are refined and a white mark appears on their necks by which they are known. Then they are brought, and God says to them: "Wish for whatever you want." They wish, until, when their wishes run out, He says to them: "For you is what you have wished, and the like of it, seventy times over." Then they enter the Garden, with a white mark on their necks by which they are known. They are called "the poor ones of the people of the Garden."

Ibn Mas‘ud said: God, Mighty and Majestic, will reckon people on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by even one, enters the Garden; and whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by even one, enters the Fire. Then he recited: ﴿Then those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. And those whose scales are light, they are those who have lost themselves﴾ [7:8–9]. Then he said:

*"The scale is made lighter by the weight of a mustard seed [and then it tips]."*

As for whoever's good and bad deeds are equal, he is among the companions of the A'raf. They stand upon the Sirat, and the light that was in their hands is not taken from them.

Yahya ibn [Shibl] narrated that a man from the Banu al-Nadir told him, on the authority of a man from the Banu Hilal, that his father told him that he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the companions of the A'raf. He said: "They are men who fought in the way of God while disobedient to their parents. They were killed, so they were spared from the Fire because of their being killed in the way of God, and they were held back from the Garden because of their parents' disobedience. So they are the last to [enter] the Garden." [183]

Shurahbil ibn Sa‘id said: They are a people who went out to fight without the permission of their parents. Mujahid said: They are righteous people, jurists and scholars. [Al-Tamimi] and Abu Majlaz said: They are angels who recognize the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire. It was said to Abu Majlaz: God says, ﴿And upon the A'raf are men﴾, and you claim they are angels? He said: "They are males, not females." Ibn ‘Abbas said: They are men who had many sins, and their being held back was by God's command. They stand upon the A'raf, ﴿recognizing each by their marks﴾ [7:46]. [Salih, the mawla of Kufa] narrated that Ibn ‘Abbas said: "The companions of the A'raf are the children of adultery." Abu al-‘Aliyah said: They are a people who hope to enter the Garden, and God did not place that hope in them except as an honor He intends for them.

‘Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid narrated from his father: They are a people whose fathers were pleased with them but whose mothers were not, or whose mothers were pleased with them but whose fathers were not. So God does not admit them into the Garden, because their fathers and mothers are not pleased with them, and He does not admit them into the Fire, because their fathers and mothers' pleasure with them has not ended. So they are held back upon the A'raf until God, Mighty and Majestic, judges among creation, and then He admits them into the Garden. ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Yahya [al-Kinani] said: They are those who died [in poverty] and did not change their religion. In the exegesis of al-Munjuni: They are the children of polytheists.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ab relate on the authority of some people that they are men who worked for God, Mighty and Majestic, but who saw [others] in their deeds. So they do not enter the Fire, because they did their deeds for God, and they do not enter the Garden, because they sought reward from other than God. So they are held back upon the A'raf until God judges among creation. This is His saying: ﴿recognizing each by their marks﴾.

Jawaybir ibn Sa‘id narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And upon the A'raf are men who recognize each by their marks﴾. He said: "The A'raf is an elevated place on the Sirat, upon which stand al-‘Abbas, Hamzah, ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ja‘far Dhu al-Janahayn. They recognize their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of their faces." [184]

As for His words, ﴿they recognize each by their marks﴾: meaning they recognize the people of the Garden by the whiteness of their faces and the radiance of bliss upon them, and they recognize the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes.

﴿And they call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you," they have not entered it, but they hope to﴾, meaning the people of the A'raf.

Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: "By God, God did not place that hope in their hearts except as an honor He intends for them, because God, Exalted, [ ... ] [an illegible word.] And the hypocrites, while on the Sirat, wish that one of them had remained and had not [ ... ] [an illegible word.]"

﴿And when their gaze is turned toward the [faces of the] people of the Fire, the companions of the Fire,﴾ and facing them, they seek refuge in God. They say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people,﴾ the disbelievers in the Fire. ﴿And the companions of the A'raf call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, who were the great ones of the people of the Fire, tyrants.﴾ They say: ﴿What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?﴾ — meaning the wealth and [children] you accumulated in the world, and what you were arrogant about regarding faith.

Al-Kalbi said: They will call out while standing upon the wall: "O Walid ibn al-Mughirah! O Abu Jahl ibn Hisham! O so-and-so!" Then they will look at the Garden and see in it the weak, the poor, and the needy, those whom they used to mock, such as Salman, Suhayb, Khabbab, and their followers. Then they will say: ﴿Are these the ones about whom you swore﴾, that you swore while in the world ﴿that God would not grant them mercy﴾, meaning the Garden. Then it will be said to the companions of the A'raf: ﴿Enter the Garden; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve.﴾ [7:49]

Muqatil said: The people of the Fire swore that the companions of the A'raf would not enter the Garden, but would enter the Fire with them. So the angels who held back the companions of the Sirat said: "These are the ones ﴿about whom you swore, O people of the Fire, that God would not grant them mercy﴾." Then the angels said to the companions of the A'raf: ﴿Enter the Garden.﴾

﴿And the companions of the Fire call out to the companions of the Garden: "Pour out [pour down] upon us, and spread [your favor] over us, some of the water, or of what God has provided you."﴾ — meaning from the food of the Garden. ﴿They say: "God has forbidden both of them,"﴾ meaning the water and the food, ﴿to the disbelievers.﴾

Abu al-Jawza' said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas: "Which charity is best?" He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is water. Have you not seen the people of the Fire, when they sought help from the people of the Garden, they said: ﴿Pour out upon us some of the water﴾?" [185] [Majma‘ al-Zawa'id: 3/131.]

﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾, and this is what Satan adorned for them: the prohibition of the *bahirah*, the *sa’ibah*, the *wasilah*, the *ham*, the whistling (*al-muka'*) and clapping (*al-tasdiyah*) around the House, and all the other vile and base qualities they practiced in their pre-Islamic ignorance. Religion is everything obeyed and adhered to, whether of truth or falsehood. Abu Rawq said: "Their religion" or "their creed." ﴿And the life of this world deceived them.﴾ ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, meaning We will leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs, and as they used to deny Our signs.﴾ [7:51]

So they are held back upon the A'raf until God, Mighty and Majestic, judges among creation, and then He admits them into the Garden. ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Yahya [al-Kinani] said: They are those who died [in poverty] and did not change their religion. In the exegesis of al-Munjuni: They are the children of polytheists.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ab relate on the authority of some people that they are men who worked for God, Mighty and Majestic, but who saw [others] in their deeds. So they do not enter the Fire, because they did their deeds for God, and they do not enter the Garden, because they sought reward from other than God. So they are held back upon the A'raf until God judges among creation. This is His saying: ﴿recognizing each by their marks﴾.

Jawaybir ibn Sa‘id narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning God's words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And upon the A'raf are men who recognize each by their marks﴾. He said: "The A'raf is an elevated place on the Sirat, upon which stand al-‘Abbas, Hamzah, ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ja‘far Dhu al-Janahayn. They recognize their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of their faces." [184]

As for His words, ﴿they recognize each by their marks﴾: meaning they recognize the people of the Garden by the whiteness of their faces and the radiance of bliss upon them, and they recognize the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes.

﴿And they call out to the companions of the Garden: "Peace be upon you," they have not entered it, but they hope to﴾, meaning the people of the A'raf.

Sa‘id ibn Jubayr said: "By God, God did not place that hope in their hearts except as an honor He intends for them, because God, Exalted, [ ... ] [an illegible word.] And the hypocrites, while on the Sirat, wish that one of them had remained and had not [ ... ] [an illegible word.]"

﴿And when their gaze is turned toward the [faces of the] people of the Fire, the companions of the Fire,﴾ and facing them, they seek refuge in God. They say: ﴿Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people,﴾ the disbelievers in the Fire. ﴿And the companions of the A'raf call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, who were the great ones of the people of the Fire, tyrants.﴾ They say: ﴿What did your gathering avail you, and your arrogance?﴾ — meaning the wealth and [children] you accumulated in the world, and what you were arrogant about regarding faith.

Al-Kalbi said: They will call out while standing upon the wall: "O Walid ibn al-Mughirah! O Abu Jahl ibn Hisham! O so-and-so!" Then they will look at the Garden and see in it the weak, the poor, and the needy, those whom they used to mock, such as Salman, Suhayb, Khabbab, and their followers. Then they will say: ﴿Are these the ones about whom you swore﴾, that you swore while in the world ﴿that God would not grant them mercy﴾, meaning the Garden. Then it will be said to the companions of the A'raf: ﴿Enter the Garden; no fear will be upon you, nor will you grieve.﴾ [7:49]

Muqatil said: The people of the Fire swore that the companions of the A'raf would not enter the Garden, but would enter the Fire with them. So the angels who held back the companions of the Sirat said: "These are the ones ﴿about whom you swore, O people of the Fire, that God would not grant them mercy﴾." Then the angels said to the companions of the A'raf: ﴿Enter the Garden.﴾

﴿And the companions of the Fire call out to the companions of the Garden: "Pour out [pour down] upon us, and spread [your favor] over us, some of the water, or of what God has provided you."﴾ — meaning from the food of the Garden. ﴿They say: "God has forbidden both of them,"﴾ meaning the water and the food, ﴿to the disbelievers.﴾

Abu al-Jawza' said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas: "Which charity is best?" He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is water. Have you not seen the people of the Fire, when they sought help from the people of the Garden, they said: ﴿Pour out upon us some of the water﴾?" [185] [Majma‘ al-Zawa'id: 3/131.]

﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play﴾, and this is what Satan adorned for them: the prohibition of the *bahirah*, the *sa’ibah*, the *wasilah*, the *ham*, the whistling (*al-muka'*) and clapping (*al-tasdiyah*) around the House, and all the other vile and base qualities they practiced in their pre-Islamic ignorance. Religion is everything obeyed and adhered to, whether of truth or falsehood. Abu Rawq said: "Their religion" or "their creed." ﴿And the life of this world deceived them.﴾ ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, meaning We will leave them in the Fire, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs, and as they used to deny Our signs.﴾ [7:51]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 7, verses 52–58**

﴿And We have certainly brought them a Book, which We have detailed upon knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.﴾ *Fassalnahu*: We made it clear and explained it, *'ala 'ilmin minna bidhalika* (with knowledge from Us of that). *Huda* (guidance) and *rahmah* (mercy) are in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*qat'*). ﴿Do they await anything but its ta'wil?﴾ *Yantadhirun* means "await." *Illa ta'wilahu* means: what their affair will come to, namely the punishment and the arrival at the Fire.

Qatadah said: *ta'wiluhu* means its reward. Mujahid said: its recompense. al-Suddi said: its consequence. Ibn Zayd said: its reality.

﴿On the day its ta'wil comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "Indeed the messengers of our Lord came with the truth. Do we have any intercessors now, who might intercede for us, or could we be sent back so that we might do other than what we used to do?"﴾ Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have lost their souls, and what they used to fabricate has vanished from them.﴾

﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Allah has the power over whoever is in the heavens and the earth in a glance and a blink; He created them in six days only to order His creation with gentleness and deliberation, as a matter of naming.

﴿Then He istawa upon the Throne.﴾ al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it means He settled (*istaqarra*). Abu Ubayd [said: He ascended (*fasa'ada*)]. Some said: He took control and prevailed (*istawla*). It was also said: He ruled and prevailed. All of these interpretations are flawed, and their weakness is not hidden. The sound and correct view is what al-Farra' and a group of the scholars of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: that the first thing created was the Throne, and then He made a covenant with His creation. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Then He istawa to the heaven﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:29], meaning: to the creation of the heaven.

The theologians (*mutakallimun*) of the people of truth (*ahl al-haqq*) said: Allah brought into being an act which He named *istiwa'*, and it is like coming, arriving and descending. These are attributes of His actions.

al-Hasan narrated from Umm Salamah concerning His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful istawa upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:5]. She said: "The how is not conceivable, the istiwa' is not unknown, descending with it is faith, and denying it is disbelief."

From Muhammad ibn Shuja' al-Balkhi, who said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿The Most Merciful istawa upon the Throne﴾, "How did He istawa?" He said: "The how is unknown, the istiwa' is not conceivable, faith in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation."

Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shabur narrated from his father that a man asked al-Awza'i about the saying: ﴿The Most Merciful istawa upon the Throne﴾. He said: "He is upon the Throne as He described Himself. I see you as a misguided man."

It reached me that a man asked Ishaq ibn al-Haytham al-Handhali, saying: "How did He istawa upon the Throne? Is He standing or sitting?" He said: "O man, only one who tires of standing sits, and only one who tires of sitting stands. Other than this is better for you: that you do not ask about it."

*Al-'arsh* (the Throne) in the language means a couch (*sarir*). Others said: it is whatever is elevated and provides shade, and from this comes *'arsh al-karm* (the trellis of the vine). It was also said: *al-'arsh* means kingship (*al-mulk*).

Zuhayr said:
"You two overtook the Ahlaf, when their throne had been shaken, and Dhibyan, whose sandals had slipped beneath its feet."

﴿He covers the night over the day, pursuing it swiftly﴾, *hathithan* meaning hastening. ﴿And the sun, the moon and the stars, subjected by His command﴾, *musakhkharat* meaning made subservient (*mudhallalat*) by His command. The people of Syria read *wa-l-shamsu* and so on in the nominative as a new sentence (*ibtida'*), with the predicate being: ﴿Surely His is the creation and the command﴾.

I heard Abu al-Qasim [al-Habibi] say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Nafi' the merchant of Herat, al-Shajari, say: I heard Abu Zayd Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Sami say: I heard 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' al-'Attar say: I asked Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah about His saying: ﴿Surely His is the creation and the command﴾. He said: "Allah has distinguished between the creation and the command, and whoever combines them has disbelieved."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not praise Allah for a righteous deed that he has done, and praises himself instead, his gratitude has become scant and his deed has been nullified. And whoever claims that Allah has given the servants a share of the command, has disbelieved in what Allah sent down upon His prophets, because of His saying: ﴿Surely His is the creation and the command﴾." [186] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/269.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan 'Isa ibn Zayd al-'Uqayli recited to us, saying: Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anbari recited to us from his father Mahmud ibn al-Hasan al-Warraq, who said:

"Surely to Allah belongs all the command over all His creation;
nothing of the command belongs to the created."

﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ al-Dahhak said: *tabaraka* means exalted (*ta'azzama*). al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: *tabaraka* means glorified (*tamajjada*). al-Qutaybi said: it is *tafa'ul* from *barakah* (blessing). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: He is blessed in His essence, and He blesses whom He wills of His creation.

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly (*tadarru'an*), in humility (*tadharru'*) and in secret (*khufyah*).﴾ *Tadarru'* means in submission and humbleness. *Khufyah* means in secret.

'Asim al-Ahwal narrated from Ibn 'Uthman al-Hindi, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was on a military expedition, and they came upon a valley. Some people began to shout *takbir* and *tahlil*, raising their voices. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people, lower your voices toward yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who is All-Hearing, Near, and He is with you." [187] [al-Musannaf li-Ibn Abi Shaybah: 2/372.]

al-Hasan said: Between the supplication in secret and the supplication in public there is a difference of seventy times. Then he said: A man may have memorized the Qur'an while his neighbour did not perceive it; a man may have understood much jurisprudence while people did not perceive it. A man may pray a long prayer in his house while those around him in the house do not perceive it. We have known people for whom no deed on earth was possible to do in secret that would ever become public.

The Muslims used to strive in supplication, and no sound of theirs was heard except a whisper between them and their Lord. That is because Allah said: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾. And Allah mentioned a righteous servant and approved his deed, saying, the Mighty, the Majestic: ﴿When he called upon his Lord with a secret call﴾ [Maryam 19:3].

﴿Surely He does not love the transgressors﴾ in supplication. Abu Majlaz said: they are those who ask for the ranks of the prophets. 'Ata al-'Awfi said: they are those who call upon Him for what is not permitted for believers, saying: "O Allah, disgrace them! O Allah, curse them!" Ibn Jurayj said: among transgression is raising the voice and the call in supplication, while they were ordered to be humble and submissive.

﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reform﴾, by associating partners with Allah, by disobedience, and by calling to other than the worship of Allah. *Ba'da islahiha*: after the reform by Allah of it, by sending the messengers, the command of what is lawful and the prohibition of what is wrong and unlawful. Every land before a prophet was sent to it was corrupt, until messengers were sent to it, and they reformed the land through obedience.

'Ata said: its meaning is: do not disobey on the earth, lest Allah withhold the rain and destroy the crops because of your sins. ﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope.﴾ al-Kalbi said: *khawfan* means fear of Him and His punishment, and *tama'an* means hope for what is with Him of forgiveness and reward. al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: *khawfan wa-tama'an* is like His saying: ﴿in desire and in fear﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:90]. It was also said: the fear of the outcome and the hope of mercy. Ibn Jurayj said: the fear of justice and the hope of grace. 'Ata said: fear of the Fire and hope for the Gardens. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: fear of separation and hope for meeting.

﴿Surely the mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers.﴾ The original form would have been *qaribatun* (feminine), but it is *qarib* (masculine). The grammarians differed concerning this and gave many views. I will mention the texts of what they said.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: *rahmah* here means reward. al-Akhfash said: it means rain, so *qarib* is a qualifier of the meaning rather than the wording, as in His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by the near of kin, and the orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:8]. He did not say "from it" (feminine), because by "division" he meant inheritance and wealth. And He said: ﴿So he began with their bags before the bag of his brother, then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾ [Yusuf 12:76]. The *sa'* (drinking-cup) is masculine because by it He meant the measure, and inheritance is like the *munshariyyah* and the *siqayah*.

al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: *qarib* and *ba'id* are used equally for masculine and feminine, singular and plural. A poet says:
"Enough sorrow for me that I stay in a town,
my friends being far from it, distant."

Another said:
"They were distant, so I hoped for them,
until when they drew near, they left."

Another said:
"The house is not distant from me,
but my soul has hardly been able to reach it."

[Sibawayh said:] when the feminine is attached to the masculine, he treated it in the way of the masculine. al-Kisa'i said: *inna rahmata Allahi qarib* means its place is near, like His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:63], meaning its coming is near.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: *rahmah* is a verbal noun (*masdar*), and the proper form of verbal nouns is masculine, as in His saying: ﴿So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:275]. A poet said:
"Surely generosity and nobility have made a grave in Marw, on the clear road."
He did not say "made" (feminine dual), because it is a verbal noun.

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: *qarib* in the language has two kinds: a near that is near in kinship, as the Arabs say: "This woman is near to you (*qaribah minka*)" when it means kinship, and "This woman is near to you (*qarib minka*)" when it means distance and place. Imru' al-Qays said:
"Woe to him if he should be left, when neither Umm Hashim
nor al-Basbasah, daughter of Yashkur, is near."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *qarib* and *ba'id* can be used for feminine and masculine. He argued with the words of 'Urwah ibn al-Ward:
"I feared, not 'Afra' near to you,
so that she might draw him near, nor 'Afra' distant from you."

Abu 'Ubaydah also said: when *qarib* and *ba'id* are nouns, masculine and feminine are equal in them; but if you form them from *qaruba* and *ba'uda*, then it is *qarIbah* and *ba'idah*.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings (*bushran*)﴾. 'Asim read *bushran* with a damma on the *ba'* and a sukun on the *shin*, meaning that they bring good news of rain, as indicated by His saying: ﴿the winds bearing good news﴾ [al-Rum 30:46].

It was narrated from him *bushuran* with a damma on the *ba'* and the *shin*, as the plural of *bashir*, like *nadhir* and *nidhar*. This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas.

Others among the people of Kufa read *nushran* with a fatha on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, meaning a good, gentle wind.

Imru' al-Qays said:
"It was as though wine, and the falling of clouds, and the scent of the *khuzama* flower, and the spreading of rain..."

This is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and Zirr ibn Hubaysh. Abu 'Ubayd preferred it, because of His saying: ﴿and by those that spread out spreading﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:3].

The people of Hijaz and Basra read *nushuran* with a damma on the *nun* and the *shin*. Abu Hatim preferred this, and said: it is the plural of *nashur*, like *sabur* and *sabir*, and *shakur* and *shakir*. These are the winds that blow from every direction and come from every side.

al-Hasan, Abu Raja', Abu 'Abd al-Rahman and Ibn 'Amir read *nushran* with a damma on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, by way of lightening.

Masruq read *nasaran* with two fathas, meaning *mansur* (spread), like *al-maqbud* and *al-qabd*.

﴿Before His mercy﴾, meaning before the rain. ﴿Until, when they carry heavy clouds﴾, *aqallat* meaning bear. *Sahaban thiqalan*: heavy clouds, the rain. ﴿We drive it﴾, *suqnahu*, the pronoun refers back to the word "clouds," ﴿to a dead land﴾, meaning to a land.

It was also said: its meaning is: for the sake of a land that has no vegetation. ﴿And We send down water thereby﴾, meaning the cloud. It was also said: the water was sent down on the land. ﴿The water﴾ means the rain.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said: not a drop falls from the sky until four things act upon it: the east wind stirs it, the north wind gathers it, the south wind makes it flow, and the west wind scatters it.

﴿Thus We bring out the dead﴾ alive. Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas said: when all people die at the first blast of the Trumpet, Allah will send down upon them rain for forty years. Men will be watered by water from beneath the Throne, called the water of life, and they will sprout in their graves by that rain, as they sprout in their mothers' wombs, and as plants grow from water. When their bodies are complete, the spirit will be breathed into them. Then a sleep will be cast upon them, and they will sleep in their graves. When the second blast is sounded, they will rise, and they will find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes, as the sleeper finds it when he wakes from his sleep. At that moment they will say: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:52]. Then the caller will call out to them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/274.]

﴿And the good land, its plants come forth by the permission of its Lord.﴾ This is a parable which Allah set forth for the believer and the disbeliever. The likeness of the believer is that of the good, pure land, whose plants come forth abundantly by the permission of Allah. The likeness of the disbeliever is that of the salty, wicked land, whose plants do not come forth except scanty, meaning with difficulty and hardship. [The text here is corrupt in the source.] Abu Ja'far read *nakadan* with a fatha on the *kaf*, meaning *al-nakad* (distress).

﴿Thus We vary the signs for a people who give thanks.﴾

nothing of the command belongs to the created."

"Enough sorrow for me that I stay in a town,

"They were distant, so I hoped for them,
until when they drew near, they left."

Another said:
"The house is not distant from me,
but my soul has hardly been able to reach it."

nor al-Basbasah, daughter of Yashkur, is near."

It was also said: its meaning is: for the sake of a land that has no vegetation. ﴿And We send down water thereby﴾, meaning the cloud. It was also said: the water was sent down on the land. ﴿The water﴾ means the rain.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said: not a drop falls from the sky until four things act upon it: the east wind stirs it, the north wind gathers it, the south wind makes it flow, and the west wind scatters it.

﴿Thus We bring out the dead﴾ alive. Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas said: when all people die at the first blast of the Trumpet, Allah will send down upon them rain for forty years. Men will be watered by water from beneath the Throne, called the water of life, and they will sprout in their graves by that rain, as they sprout in their mothers' wombs, and as plants grow from water. When their bodies are complete, the spirit will be breathed into them. Then a sleep will be cast upon them, and they will sleep in their graves. When the second blast is sounded, they will rise, and they will find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes, as the sleeper finds it when he wakes from his sleep. At that moment they will say: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:52]. Then the caller will call out to them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/274.]

﴿And the good land, its plants come forth by the permission of its Lord.﴾ This is a parable which Allah set forth for the believer and the disbeliever. The likeness of the believer is that of the good, pure land, whose plants come forth abundantly by the permission of Allah. The likeness of the disbeliever is that of the salty, wicked land, whose plants do not come forth except scanty, meaning with difficulty and hardship. [The text here is corrupt in the source.] Abu Ja'far read *nakadan* with a fatha on the *kaf*, meaning *al-nakad* (distress).

﴿Thus We vary the signs for a people who give thanks.﴾

Qatadah said: *ta'wiluhu* means its reward. Mujahid said: its recompense. al-Suddi said: its consequence. Ibn Zayd said: its reality.

Another said:
"They were distant, so I hoped for them,

Another said:
"The house is not distant from me,

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *qarib* and *ba'id* can be used for feminine and masculine. He argued with the words of 'Urwah ibn al-Ward:
"I feared, not 'Afra' near to you,

Abu 'Ubaydah also said: when *qarib* and *ba'id* are nouns, masculine and feminine are equal in them; but if you form them from *qaruba* and *ba'uda*, then it is *qarIbah* and *ba'idah*.

And He said: ﴿So he began with their bags before the bag of his brother, then he brought it out from his brother's bag﴾ [Yusuf 12:76]. The *sa'* (drinking-cup) is masculine because by it He meant the measure, and inheritance is like the *munshariyyah* and the *siqayah*.

al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: *qarib* and *ba'id* are used equally for masculine and feminine, singular and plural. A poet says:
"Enough sorrow for me that I stay in a town,
my friends being far from it, distant."

Another said:
"They were distant, so I hoped for them,
until when they drew near, they left."

Another said:
"The house is not distant from me,
but my soul has hardly been able to reach it."

[Sibawayh said:] when the feminine is attached to the masculine, he treated it in the way of the masculine. al-Kisa'i said: *inna rahmata Allahi qarib* means its place is near, like His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:63], meaning its coming is near.

al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: *rahmah* is a verbal noun (*masdar*), and the proper form of verbal nouns is masculine, as in His saying: ﴿So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:275]. A poet said:
"Surely generosity and nobility have made a grave in Marw, on the clear road."
He did not say "made" (feminine dual), because it is a verbal noun.

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: *qarib* in the language has two kinds: a near that is near in kinship, as the Arabs say: "This woman is near to you (*qaribah minka*)" when it means kinship, and "This woman is near to you (*qarib minka*)" when it means distance and place. Imru' al-Qays said:
"Woe to him if he should be left, when neither Umm Hashim
nor al-Basbasah, daughter of Yashkur, is near."

Abu 'Ubaydah said: *qarib* and *ba'id* can be used for feminine and masculine. He argued with the words of 'Urwah ibn al-Ward:
"I feared, not 'Afra' near to you,
so that she might draw him near, nor 'Afra' distant from you."

Abu 'Ubaydah also said: when *qarib* and *ba'id* are nouns, masculine and feminine are equal in them; but if you form them from *qaruba* and *ba'uda*, then it is *qarIbah* and *ba'idah*.

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings (*bushran*)﴾. 'Asim read *bushran* with a damma on the *ba'* and a sukun on the *shin*, meaning that they bring good news of rain, as indicated by His saying: ﴿the winds bearing good news﴾ [al-Rum 30:46].

It was narrated from him *bushuran* with a damma on the *ba'* and the *shin*, as the plural of *bashir*, like *nadhir* and *nidhar*. This is the reading of Ibn 'Abbas.

Others among the people of Kufa read *nushran* with a fatha on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, meaning a good, gentle wind.

Imru' al-Qays said:
"It was as though wine, and the falling of clouds, and the scent of the *khuzama* flower, and the spreading of rain..."

This is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas and Zirr ibn Hubaysh. Abu 'Ubayd preferred it, because of His saying: ﴿and by those that spread out spreading﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:3].

The people of Hijaz and Basra read *nushuran* with a damma on the *nun* and the *shin*. Abu Hatim preferred this, and said: it is the plural of *nashur*, like *sabur* and *sabir*, and *shakur* and *shakir*. These are the winds that blow from every direction and come from every side.

al-Hasan, Abu Raja', Abu 'Abd al-Rahman and Ibn 'Amir read *nushran* with a damma on the *nun* and a sukun on the *shin*, by way of lightening.

Masruq read *nasaran* with two fathas, meaning *mansur* (spread), like *al-maqbud* and *al-qabd*.

﴿Before His mercy﴾, meaning before the rain. ﴿Until, when they carry heavy clouds﴾, *aqallat* meaning bear. *Sahaban thiqalan*: heavy clouds, the rain. ﴿We drive it﴾, *suqnahu*, the pronoun refers back to the word "clouds," ﴿to a dead land﴾, meaning to a land.

It was also said: its meaning is: for the sake of a land that has no vegetation. ﴿And We send down water thereby﴾, meaning the cloud. It was also said: the water was sent down on the land. ﴿The water﴾ means the rain.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said: not a drop falls from the sky until four things act upon it: the east wind stirs it, the north wind gathers it, the south wind makes it flow, and the west wind scatters it.

﴿Thus We bring out the dead﴾ alive. Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas said: when all people die at the first blast of the Trumpet, Allah will send down upon them rain for forty years. Men will be watered by water from beneath the Throne, called the water of life, and they will sprout in their graves by that rain, as they sprout in their mothers' wombs, and as plants grow from water. When their bodies are complete, the spirit will be breathed into them. Then a sleep will be cast upon them, and they will sleep in their graves. When the second blast is sounded, they will rise, and they will find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes, as the sleeper finds it when he wakes from his sleep. At that moment they will say: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:52]. Then the caller will call out to them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/274.]

﴿And the good land, its plants come forth by the permission of its Lord.﴾ This is a parable which Allah set forth for the believer and the disbeliever. The likeness of the believer is that of the good, pure land, whose plants come forth abundantly by the permission of Allah. The likeness of the disbeliever is that of the salty, wicked land, whose plants do not come forth except scanty, meaning with difficulty and hardship. [The text here is corrupt in the source.] Abu Ja'far read *nakadan* with a fatha on the *kaf*, meaning *al-nakad* (distress).

﴿Thus We vary the signs for a people who give thanks.﴾

Surah 7, verses 59–64

Indeed, We sent Noah to his people. He is Noah son of Malik son of Mutawshalikh son of Akhnukh, who is Idris son of Mahla'il son of Yazid son of Qaythan son of Anush son of Shith son of Adam, peace be upon them. He was the first prophet after Idris. He was a carpenter, and God, Mighty and Majestic, sent him to his people when he was fifty years old. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him.﴾ Muhammad ibn al-Sumayda' recited ﴿ghayrahu﴾ with the accusative (ghayran).

Al-Farra' said: Some of the Banu Asad and Qada'a permitted the accusative of "ghayr" in every position where "illa" (except) could be used, when the preceding speech is complete or incomplete, so they say: "No polytheist came to me" and "No one came to me other than you." He cited al-Fadl:

"Nothing prevented them from drinking except that a dove spoke, in a [...] or said..."

Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative may have two aspects. One: it is an exception from a different category (istithna' min ghayr jinsihi). The second: it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from His saying ﴿u'budu Allah﴾, because "ghayruhu" is indefinite even though it is grammatically annexed to definite nouns.

Abu Ja'far, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿ma lakum min ilahin ghayrihi﴾ with a kasra on the ra', as an attribute (na't) of "ilah", and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this so that it would be one continuous utterance.

The rest recited ﴿ghayruhu﴾ with a damma, in two ways. One: anticipation (taqdim), even though it is postponed in wording; its estimated form is: "You have no other god besides Him." The second: to make it an attribute of the implied meaning of "ilah", because the sense is "you have no god other than Him."

﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day if you do not believe.﴾ ﴿The eminent ones of his people said﴾, meaning the nobles and leaders; al-Farra' said they were men with no women among them. ﴿Indeed, we see you in manifest error﴾, meaning deviation and departure from the truth, ﴿clear﴾, meaning evident.

﴿Noah said: O my people, there is no error in me,﴾ and he did not say "laysat" (feminine) because "al-dalala" means "the one who strays," and it may be understood in the sense of the verb's precedence. ﴿But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering to you﴾.

Abu 'Amr recited ﴿ublighukum﴾ with a light (unstressed) form throughout the Qur'an, for His saying: ﴿I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord﴾ and ﴿so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾, and because all the books of the prophets were revealed at once, including the Qur'an. The rest recited ﴿uballighukum﴾ with a doubled (shaddah) form, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it because it is the more eloquent of the two dialects. God says: ﴿Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ (5:67).

﴿And I advise you﴾; it is said [with the lightened form] "nasahtu lahu" and "shakartuhu" and "shakartu lahu". ﴿And I know from God what you do not know﴾, of His punishment, which does not turn back from the criminal people.

﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you, and so that you may be mindful of God, and that you may perhaps receive mercy?﴾ The alif is an interrogative particle entering upon the conjunctive waw, as if he said: "If you waste such and such..." ﴿A reminder from your Lord﴾, meaning prophethood and the message; it was also said: [a miracle and clear proof].

﴿Through a man from among you, so that he may warn you﴾ of God's punishment if they do not believe. ﴿And so that you may be mindful [and that they may be mindful]﴾ of God, ﴿and that you may perhaps receive mercy﴾, meaning that you may be shown mercy.

﴿But they denied him﴾, meaning Noah. ﴿So We saved him﴾ from the flood, ﴿and those with him﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: this means his three sons, Sam, Ham and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who had believed in him; and He carried them in the ark, which is the ship. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 12/48.)

Al-Kalbi said: they were eighty persons, forty men and forty women. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people﴾, ignorant of the truth and of God's command. Al-DDahhak said: ﴿'amiyin﴾ means disbelievers.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿'amiyin﴾ refers to insight; one says "a man 'amin 'an al-haqq" (blind to the truth) and "a'mа fi al-basar" (blind in sight). It was also said that al-'Ami and al-A'ma are one, like al-Khadir and al-Akhdar. Muqatil said: they were blind to the descent of the punishment upon them, and it is al-harth.

Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative may have two aspects. One: it is an exception from a different category (istithna' min ghayr jinsihi). The second: it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from His saying ﴿u'budu Allah﴾, because "ghayruhu" is indefinite even though it is grammatically annexed to definite nouns.

Abu Ja'far, Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿ma lakum min ilahin ghayrihi﴾ with a kasra on the ra', as an attribute (na't) of "ilah", and Abu 'Ubayd preferred this so that it would be one continuous utterance.

The rest recited ﴿ghayruhu﴾ with a damma, in two ways. One: anticipation (taqdim), even though it is postponed in wording; its estimated form is: "You have no other god besides Him." The second: to make it an attribute of the implied meaning of "ilah", because the sense is "you have no god other than Him."

﴿Noah said: O my people, there is no error in me,﴾ and he did not say "laysat" (feminine) because "al-dalala" means "the one who strays," and it may be understood in the sense of the verb's precedence. ﴿But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, delivering to you﴾.

Abu 'Amr recited ﴿ublighukum﴾ with a light (unstressed) form throughout the Qur'an, for His saying: ﴿I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord﴾ and ﴿so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾, and because all the books of the prophets were revealed at once, including the Qur'an. The rest recited ﴿uballighukum﴾ with a doubled (shaddah) form, and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred it because it is the more eloquent of the two dialects. God says: ﴿Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾ (5:67).

﴿And I advise you﴾; it is said [with the lightened form] "nasahtu lahu" and "shakartuhu" and "shakartu lahu". ﴿And I know from God what you do not know﴾, of His punishment, which does not turn back from the criminal people.

﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you, and so that you may be mindful of God, and that you may perhaps receive mercy?﴾ The alif is an interrogative particle entering upon the conjunctive waw, as if he said: "If you waste such and such..." ﴿A reminder from your Lord﴾, meaning prophethood and the message; it was also said: [a miracle and clear proof].

﴿Through a man from among you, so that he may warn you﴾ of God's punishment if they do not believe. ﴿And so that you may be mindful [and that they may be mindful]﴾ of God, ﴿and that you may perhaps receive mercy﴾, meaning that you may be shown mercy.

﴿But they denied him﴾, meaning Noah. ﴿So We saved him﴾ from the flood, ﴿and those with him﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: this means his three sons, Sam, Ham and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who had believed in him; and He carried them in the ark, which is the ship. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 12/48.)

Al-Kalbi said: they were eighty persons, forty men and forty women. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people﴾, ignorant of the truth and of God's command. Al-DDahhak said: ﴿'amiyin﴾ means disbelievers.
