Ibn Ishaq said: The nine's agreement to kill Salih (ﷺ) was only after they had hamstrung the she-camel and after Salih warned them of punishment. The nine who hamstrung the she-camel said: "Come, let us kill Salih; if he is truthful we will hasten his killing, and if he is lying we will send him to join his camel." They came to him at night to attack him in his household, but the angels repelled them with stones. When they were late returning to their companions, they came to Salih's house and found them crushed, struck with stones. They said to Salih: "You killed them." Then they resolved against him, but his clan stood between them and him and put on their weapons, and said to them: "By Allah, you will never kill him, and he has promised you that punishment will descend upon you in three days. If he is truthful, you will only increase your Lord's anger; and if he is lying, you will be free of what you intend." They turned away from them that night.

Al-Suddi and others said: The worst child, meaning Qudar, grew in a day what others grew in a week, and in a month what others grew in a year. When he grew up, he sat with people who drank wine. They wanted something to mix with their drink, and that day was the she-camel's turn to drink, and they found that the water had been drunk by the she-camel. That was hard for them, and they spoke about the she-camel and her hardship upon them: "We do not do anything with milk; if we took from this water the she-camel drinks, and gave it to our livestock and crops, it would be better for us." The son of the tenth said: "Shall I hamstring her for you?" They said: "Yes."

Ka'b said: The cause of their hamstringing the she-camel was that a woman called Malka had ruled Thamud. When people turned to Salih and leadership passed to him, she envied him; she said to a woman called Qatam, who was the beloved of Qudar ibn Salif, and to another woman called Qabal, who was the beloved of Mus'ad ibn Mahraj (also said ibn Wa'd), and Qudar and Mus'ad used to meet every night with them and drink wine. Malka said to them: "If Qudar and Mus'ad come to you tonight, do not obey them; tell them: 'The queen is sad because of the she-camel and because of Salih; we will not obey you until you hamstring the she-camel; if you hamstring her, we will obey you.'" When they came to them, the two women said this to them, and they said: [...]

Ibn Ishaq and others said: Qudar, Mus'ad and their seven companions set out, lay in wait for the she-camel when she came back from the water, and Qudar lay in wait for her at the base of a pit on her path, and Mus'ad lay in wait on another path. She passed by Mus'ad, who shot her with an arrow that struck the muscle of her leg, and Umm Ghanm and 'Unayza came out and ordered their daughter, who was among the most beautiful people, to show herself to Qudar; then she [Qudar] came to the she-camel and struck her with the sword, cutting her hamstring. She went out roaring one roar, then her young one ran off, and he thrust a spear into her chest and slaughtered her.

The people of the town came out and divided her meat and cooked it. When her young one (that is, her offspring) saw that, he went off until he reached a strong mountain called Sur; it was also said its name was Qara. He came to Salih and said: "Catch up with the she-camel, she has been hamstrung." They came out to meet him, apologizing to him: "O Prophet of Allah, it was only so-and-so and so-and-so who hamstrung her; we are not to blame." Salih (peace be upon him) said: "See whether you can catch up with her young one; if you catch him, perhaps the punishment will be lifted from you." They went out seeking him, and when they saw him on the mountain they went to seize him, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the mountain, and it rose up into the sky until no bird could reach it. Salih (peace be upon him) came, and when the young one saw him he wept until his tears flowed, then he faced Salih and cried out one cry, then another, then another.

Salih (peace be upon him) said: "For every cry there is a term. Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise not to be denied" [Hud 65].

Ibn Ishaq said: Four men followed the young camel (al-saqb) from among the nine who had hamstrung the she-camel, and among them were Mus'da' ibn Mahraj and his brother Dab ibn Mahraj. Mus'da' shot an arrow that pierced its heart, then dragged it by its leg and brought it down, and they threw its flesh together with the flesh of its mother. Salih said to them: "You have violated the sanctity of God the Exalted, so await the punishment and vengeance of God." They said to him, mocking him: "And when will that be, O Salih, and what is its sign?" They used to name the days: the first day was Ahad, Monday was Ahwan (Umayyin), Tuesday was Dabar, Wednesday was Jubar, Thursday was Mu'nis, Friday was Ghurubah, and Saturday was Shiyar. They had hamstrung the she-camel on Wednesday, so Salih (peace be upon him) said to them when they said that: "You will become (lit. you will awake) on the day of Mu'nis with your faces yellow; then you will awake on the day of Ghurubah with your faces red; then you will awake on the day of Shiyar with your faces black; then the punishment will overtake you on the day of the first (Ahad)." So they awoke on Thursday with their faces yellow, as if they had been smeared with saffron (khaluq), young and old, male and female alike. They became certain of the punishment and knew that Salih had spoken the truth, so they sought him in order to kill him. Salih went out fleeing until he took refuge with a clan of Thamud called Banu Ghanm. A man of theirs called Nufayl, whose kunya was Abu Hadab, and who was a polytheist, hosted him and hid him, so they could not reach him. They then sat with Salih's companions, torturing them so that they would point out his whereabouts.

A man among Salih's companions called Mubda' ibn Harim said: "O Prophet of God, they are torturing us so that we will point them to you; shall we point them out?" He said: "Yes." So Mida' (Mubda') pointed them to him, and they came to Abu Hadab and spoke with him about it. He said: "Yes, Salih is with me, and you have no way to reach him." So they turned away from him and left him alone, and what God the Mighty and Majestic had sent down upon them of His punishment occupied them. Some of them began informing others of what they saw in their faces. When they awoke, they all cried out: "Indeed, one day of the term has passed." When they awoke on the second day, their faces were red as if dyed with blood, so they shrieked, wailed and wept, and they recognised the sign of the punishment. When evening came, they all cried out: "Indeed, two days of the term have passed, and the punishment has come upon you." When the third day came, their faces were black as if smeared with fire, so they all cried out together: "The punishment has come upon you."

When it was the night of Sunday, Salih (peace be upon him) left among them, together with those who had believed with him, for Syria, and they settled in the sands of Palestine. When the people awoke, they wrapped themselves in shrouds and applied camphor/aloes-type perfume (hanut), their hanut being sabr and muqar, and their shrouds were [leather mats (anta')]. Then they threw themselves on the ground, turning their eyes: looking at the sky once and at the earth once, not knowing from where the punishment would come upon them.

When the forenoon grew intense on Sunday, a shriek came to them from the sky, containing the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything in the earth that has a sound, so their hearts were torn apart within their chests, and none of them, small or great, was left alive except that they perished, just as God the Exalted said: ﴿So they became prostrate corpses in their homes﴾. Except for a crippled girl among them called Dhari'a bint Salaq, who was a disbeliever and fiercely hostile to Salih (peace be upon him). God the Mighty and Majestic released her leg after she had witnessed the whole punishment, so she went out faster than anything has ever been seen to move, until she reached Qazah [Qazah: a valley in Muzdalifah], which is Wadi al-Qura, and she informed them of what she had witnessed of the punishment and what had befallen Thamud. Then she asked for water and was given some, and when she drank it she died.

Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered (the army) at the Hijr during the expedition of Tabuk, he said to his companions: "None of you should enter the town, nor drink from its water, nor enter upon these punished people unless you are weeping and fearful; and if you are not, then do not enter upon them, lest there befall you what befell them."

Then he said: "Now then, do not ask your Messenger for signs. These were the people of Salih, who asked their messenger for a sign, so God the Mighty and Majestic sent them the she-camel. She would come to them from this pass and depart by that pass, and she would drink their water on one day, while on the other day they would have water. When the camel's colt climbed up into the cave behind them, they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung her, so God destroyed from under the expanse of the sky all of them except one man, who was in the sanctuary of God."

It was said: "Who was he?" He said: "Abu Righal." [190]

When he came out, what had befallen his people befell him [and he was buried here], and a golden branch was buried with him. He showed them the grave of Abu Righal, so the people rushed toward it with their swords, dug around it and extracted that branch. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) lowered his head and hastened his pace until he passed the valley [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 12/85 and Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/159, with variation.]].

The people of knowledge said: Salih (peace be upon him) died in Mecca at the age of fifty-eight, and he remained among his people for twenty years.

From al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: "O Ali, do you know who is the most wretched of the first?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best."

He said: "The one who hamstrung the she-camel." 

He said: "Do you know who is the most wretched of the last?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best."

He said: "Your slayer." [191] [[al-Tabaqat al-Kubra: 3/35; Tarikh Baghdad: 1/146; Shawahid al-Tanzil: 2/444, no. 1108.]]

And (We sent) Lot. That is, "We sent Lot"; it is also said the meaning is: "Remember Lot." He was Lot son of [Haran], son of Terah, the brother of Abraham (peace be upon him), when he said to his people, who were the people of Sodom. The reason was that Lot had come out of the land of Babylon with his uncle Abraham (peace be upon him), believing in him, emigrating with him to the Levant. Abraham (peace be upon him) settled in Palestine, and he settled his nephew Lot in the Jordan region. God sent (a messenger) to the people of Sodom, and he said to them: ﴿Do you commit the abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in?﴾ That is, the coupling with males. ʿAmr ibn Dinar said: "Before the people of Lot, no male had ever committed fornication with a male in the world." ﴿Indeed you approach men with lust, instead of women.﴾ That is, the backsides of men are more appealing to you than the private parts of women. ﴿Rather, you are a people who exceed the limits﴾, polytheists [who alter] the lawful into the unlawful.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They had fruits and villages the like of which were not found anywhere on earth, so people came to them and harmed them. Iblis appeared to them in the form of an old man and said: "If you [fight] them all, I will save you from them." They refused. When the people pressed upon them, they committed sodomy with them, and they took boys in the morning and became corrupt, and this practice became entrenched among them.

Al-Hasan said: "They would not marry except men." Al-Kalbi said: "The first to practise the deeds of the people of Lot was the wicked Iblis, because their lands became fertile and the people of other regions came to them seeking provision. Iblis appeared to them in the form of a young man, then invited [someone] to his back passage and had intercourse in his back passage. Then they became arrogant through that deed, and it spread greatly among them. So the earth cried out to its Lord, the heavens heard and cried out to their Lord, the Throne heard and cried out to its Lord. God then commanded the heaven to pelt them with stones and commanded the earth to swallow them up." ﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said﴾ when he said this to them, ﴿Among themselves: "Expel them [Lot and his followers] from your town. Indeed they are people who keep themselves pure"﴾, meaning they seek to be pure and refrain from anal intercourse with men and women. ﴿So We saved him﴾, meaning Lot, ﴿and his family﴾, the believers in him. It is also said: his family was his two daughters, Nu'adha and Dithaʾ.

﴿Except his wife, who was of those who remained behind﴾, meaning those who remained in the punishment. It is also said the meaning is: she was among those who remained and lingered before the destruction, those who had lived a long life, grown old among the aged people. She perished with those of the people of Lot who perished when the punishment came upon them. He said "al-ghabirin" (those who remain) and not "al-ghabirat" (feminine plural) because he meant that she was among those who remained with the men, so when her mention was joined to the men's, it was said "al-ghabirin." It is also said: the verb is "ghabara, yaghbaru, ghaburan," and "ghabara" means "to remain." The poet said:

"My father, who conquered the lands with his sword, and humbled them for the sons of Aban, the remaining one."

meaning the one who remains.

Abu Dhu'ayb said:

"And I remained after them in a toilsome life, and an entering in, for I am a follower who will be overtaken."

﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾, meaning stones of sijjil, ﴿so see how was the end of the criminals.﴾ We will mention the full story in its proper place, God willing.

Abu al-Yaman ibn al-Hakam ibn Nafi' al-Himsi narrated from Safwan ibn 'Amr: "ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Ibn Habib, the judge of Homs, asking him what the punishment of the sodomite is. He wrote that he should be stoned as the people of Lot were stoned, for God the Exalted said: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾, and He said: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [Surah al-Hijr: 74]. ʿAbd al-Malik accepted this from him and approved of it."

ʿIkrimah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever you find doing the deed of the people of Lot, kill the doer and the one to whom it is done."

And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. That is, We sent to the people of Madyan, son of Ibrahim the Friend of Allah, and they are the People of the Thicket (Ashab al-Aykah).

Qatadah said: He was sent twice, to Madyan and to the People of the Thicket. [He was] their brother Shu'ayb. Qatadah said: He is Shu'ayb ibn [Nuwayb]. 'Ata' said: He is Shu'ayb ibn Tawbah ibn Madyan ibn Ibrahim. Ibn Ishaq said: He is Shu'ayb ibn Mikil ibn Ishaq ibn Madyan ibn Ibrahim; his name in Syriac is Yathrub, and his mother was Mikil, daughter of Lut. Shu'ayb was blind.

It is said that he was the "orator of the prophets" because of the excellence of his dialogue with his people. His people were a disbelieving people who denied Allah and cheated in measure and weight. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ [That is, Shu'ayb has come.] ﴿So give full measure and weight﴾: complete them. ﴿And do not deprive people of their things﴾: do not wrong people of their rights, and do not diminish them [from them]. ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ The earth, before Shu'ayb was sent to it as a messenger, was one in which they committed sins, made lawful what was forbidden, and shed blood without right; that was its corruption. When he was sent to it and called them to Allah, the earth was set right. Every prophet who was sent to his people calls them to the reformation that I have mentioned to you and ordered you to.

﴿That is better for you, if you are believers﴾: believing (ṣaddiqīn) in what I say. ﴿And do not sit at every path﴾ [that is, on this road], as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [Al-Fajr 89:14].

﴿Threatening﴾: intimidating. ﴿And turning away from the way of Allah﴾, the religion of Allah, ﴿those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked﴾: deviation. That is because they used to sit on the roads and inform whoever intended to go to Shu'ayb in order to believe in him that Shu'ayb is a liar.

﴿So do not let [that] tempt you.﴾ They used to threaten the believers with killing and frighten them.

Al-Suddi and Abu Rawq said: They were [tyrants]. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: They used to cut the road.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw a post on the road; no garment passed by it without being torn, and nothing without being ripped. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is the likeness of people from your community who sit on the road and cut it off.'" Then he recited: ﴿And do not sit at every path, threatening.﴾ [al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/103.]

﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you [and multiplied among you]. And look at how was the end of the corrupters﴾: that is, the last of the people of Lut. ﴿And if a group among you [believed]...﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said...﴾

That is, the leaders who exalted themselves above believing in him: ﴿We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion﴾: you will return to our religion which we are upon and abandon your religion.

Shu'ayb said: ﴿Even though we were unwilling?﴾ That is, even if we were unwilling, you would compel us to it. The interrogative alif was placed before "even if" (walaw). ﴿We would have invented against Allah a lie if we returned to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will it.﴾ Meaning: unless it has already preceded for us in the knowledge and will of Allah that we return to it, so that His decree concerning us would then take effect, and His judgment and knowledge upon us would be executed. ﴿Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: His knowledge encompasses everything, so nothing is hidden from Him, whether what has existed or what will exist. ﴿Upon Allah we have relied﴾ in what you threaten us with.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾ and His saying ﴿it is not for us to return to it﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is "or you will enter into it," and "we will not enter it unless Allah, our Lord, wills, so that He would send us astray after He has guided us."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Habibi say: I heard Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say there: ﴿If we return to your religion﴾ means: if we became [in it], not that we would return; it is an beginning and a return.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"Those noble deeds, not two bowls of milk... mixed with water, and they became, after being, urine."

That is, the milk has now become such that it was never urine.

I heard [al-Husayn ibn al-Habibi] say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: its meaning is: ﴿after Allah has saved us from it﴾ in His prior knowledge and in the Preserved Tablet and the Pen.

Some of them said: Shu'ayb and those who believed with him had at the beginning of their affair been concealing themselves, then they made their affair public. Their people only said to them ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾ because they thought they were upon their religion. [It is said: whoever is with him] [[As in the manuscript.]] on the companions of Shu'ayb rather than Shu'ayb, because they had been disbelievers and then believed; the address was to them, and Shu'ayb's answer was on their behalf, not on his own, since Shu'ayb had never been a disbeliever; he was only addressing, in the terms of those who had left their religion, the matter of coming to him.

I have seen in some tafsir that "the millah" here means the sharia, which he followed before his prophethood; when he was [made a prophet], he separated from them.

Then Shu'ayb invoked against his people when he perceived what was in them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾: that is, judge.

And [the historian] said: decide.

Ibn 'Abbas said: I did not know what His saying ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾ meant until I heard the daughter of Dhu Yazan say to her husband: "Come, let me fatah you" — that is, let me judge between us.

Al-Farra' said: The people of Oman call the judge the "fatih" and "fattah." Others mentioned that it is a dialect of Mahad. He recited for someone:

"Alā ablugh banī ʿIṣm rasūlan... bi-annī ʿan fatāḥatikum ghaniyy"
("Oh, let me convey to the Banu Isma a message: that I am independent of your judgment.")

That is, of your judgment. ﴿And You are the best of those who decide﴾: the best of judges.

﴿And the chiefs of those of his people who disbelieved said: If you follow Shu'ayb and abandon your religion, indeed you would then be losers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: deceived. 'Ata' said: ignorant. al-Dahhak said: wicked.

﴿So the earthquake seized them.﴾ al-Kalbi said: the earthquake.

Ibn 'Abbas and other exegetes said: Allah opened for them a gate of the gates of Hell, so He sent upon them a wind and intense heat, which seized their breaths. They entered the interiors of their houses, but neither shade nor water benefited them, and the heat cooked them. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a cloud in which was a pleasant wind; they found the coolness of the wind with its pleasantness and the shade of the cloud. They called to one another: "Come under it!" They went out into the open, and when they gathered beneath the cloud, men, women, and children, Allah set it ablaze upon them as fire; the earth quaked beneath them, and they were burned as locusts are burned when roasted, and they became ashes. That was the punishment of the Day of the Shade, and that is His saying: ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾: dead. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "their homes" (diyarihim) are their dwellings. Muhammad ibn Marwan said: everything in the Qur'an as "darihim" is [their place of humiliation], and everything as "diyarihim" is their armies.

"Kalamun, his death demolished my pillar, in the midst of the encampment, the lord of the people; death came to him as fire in the midst of the cloud. Fire made their homes over them like the extinguished."

Hatim said:

His people were a disbelieving people who denied Allah and cheated in measure and weight. So he said to them: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ [That is, Shu'ayb has come.] ﴿So give full measure and weight﴾: complete them. ﴿And do not deprive people of their things﴾: do not wrong people of their rights, and do not diminish them [from them]. ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation.﴾ The earth, before Shu'ayb was sent to it as a messenger, was one in which they committed sins, made lawful what was forbidden, and shed blood without right; that was its corruption. When he was sent to it and called them to Allah, the earth was set right. Every prophet who was sent to his people calls them to the reformation that I have mentioned to you and ordered you to.

﴿That is better for you, if you are believers﴾: believing (ṣaddiqīn) in what I say. ﴿And do not sit at every path﴾ [that is, on this road], as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [Al-Fajr 89:14].

﴿Threatening﴾: intimidating. ﴿And turning away from the way of Allah﴾, the religion of Allah, ﴿those who believe in Him, and seeking to make it crooked﴾: deviation. That is because they used to sit on the roads and inform whoever intended to go to Shu'ayb in order to believe in him that Shu'ayb is a liar.

﴿So do not let [that] tempt you.﴾ They used to threaten the believers with killing and frighten them.

Al-Suddi and Abu Rawq said: They were [tyrants]. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: They used to cut the road.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw a post on the road; no garment passed by it without being torn, and nothing without being ripped. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'This is the likeness of people from your community who sit on the road and cut it off.'" Then he recited: ﴿And do not sit at every path, threatening.﴾ [al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/103.]

﴿And remember when you were few, and He multiplied you [and multiplied among you]. And look at how was the end of the corrupters﴾: that is, the last of the people of Lut. ﴿And if a group among you [believed]...﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said...﴾

That is, the leaders who exalted themselves above believing in him: ﴿We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion﴾: you will return to our religion which we are upon and abandon your religion.

Shu'ayb said: ﴿Even though we were unwilling?﴾ That is, even if we were unwilling, you would compel us to it. The interrogative alif was placed before "even if" (walaw). ﴿We would have invented against Allah a lie if we returned to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. And it is not for us to return to it unless Allah, our Lord, should will it.﴾ Meaning: unless it has already preceded for us in the knowledge and will of Allah that we return to it, so that His decree concerning us would then take effect, and His judgment and knowledge upon us would be executed. ﴿Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: His knowledge encompasses everything, so nothing is hidden from Him, whether what has existed or what will exist. ﴿Upon Allah we have relied﴾ in what you threaten us with.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾ and His saying ﴿it is not for us to return to it﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is "or you will enter into it," and "we will not enter it unless Allah, our Lord, wills, so that He would send us astray after He has guided us."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Habibi say: I heard Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say there: ﴿If we return to your religion﴾ means: if we became [in it], not that we would return; it is an beginning and a return.

Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"Those noble deeds, not two bowls of milk... mixed with water, and they became, after being, urine."

That is, the milk has now become such that it was never urine.

I heard [al-Husayn ibn al-Habibi] say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: its meaning is: ﴿after Allah has saved us from it﴾ in His prior knowledge and in the Preserved Tablet and the Pen.

Some of them said: Shu'ayb and those who believed with him had at the beginning of their affair been concealing themselves, then they made their affair public. Their people only said to them ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾ because they thought they were upon their religion. [It is said: whoever is with him] [[As in the manuscript.]] on the companions of Shu'ayb rather than Shu'ayb, because they had been disbelievers and then believed; the address was to them, and Shu'ayb's answer was on their behalf, not on his own, since Shu'ayb had never been a disbeliever; he was only addressing, in the terms of those who had left their religion, the matter of coming to him.

I have seen in some tafsir that "the millah" here means the sharia, which he followed before his prophethood; when he was [made a prophet], he separated from them.

Then Shu'ayb invoked against his people when he perceived what was in them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾: that is, judge.

And [the historian] said: decide.

Ibn 'Abbas said: I did not know what His saying ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾ meant until I heard the daughter of Dhu Yazan say to her husband: "Come, let me fatah you" — that is, let me judge between us.

Al-Farra' said: The people of Oman call the judge the "fatih" and "fattah." Others mentioned that it is a dialect of Mahad. He recited for someone:

"Alā ablugh banī ʿIṣm rasūlan... bi-annī ʿan fatāḥatikum ghaniyy"
("Oh, let me convey to the Banu Isma a message: that I am independent of your judgment.")

That is, of your judgment. ﴿And You are the best of those who decide﴾: the best of judges.

﴿And the chiefs of those of his people who disbelieved said: If you follow Shu'ayb and abandon your religion, indeed you would then be losers.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: deceived. 'Ata' said: ignorant. al-Dahhak said: wicked.

﴿So the earthquake seized them.﴾ al-Kalbi said: the earthquake.

Ibn 'Abbas and other exegetes said: Allah opened for them a gate of the gates of Hell, so He sent upon them a wind and intense heat, which seized their breaths. They entered the interiors of their houses, but neither shade nor water benefited them, and the heat cooked them. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a cloud in which was a pleasant wind; they found the coolness of the wind with its pleasantness and the shade of the cloud. They called to one another: "Come under it!" They went out into the open, and when they gathered beneath the cloud, men, women, and children, Allah set it ablaze upon them as fire; the earth quaked beneath them, and they were burned as locusts are burned when roasted, and they became ashes. That was the punishment of the Day of the Shade, and that is His saying: ﴿So they became in their homes prostrate﴾: dead. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "their homes" (diyarihim) are their dwellings. Muhammad ibn Marwan said: everything in the Qur'an as "darihim" is [their place of humiliation], and everything as "diyarihim" is their armies.

Ibn Ishaq said: It reached me that a man of Madyan named 'Umar ibn [Jalha'] when he saw the cloud, in which was wrath, said: "O people, Shu'ayb is truly a messenger. Leave aside Sumayr or 'Imran ibn Shaddad. Indeed I see a cloud, O people, that has risen. Call out with a voice over the rocky ridge of the valley, for if you see in it the morning of tomorrow except the Raqim walking between the hills..." Sumayr and 'Imran were two soothsayers/shepherds, and the Raqim was their dog. [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/7, with variation.]

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bajali said: Abjad, Hawwaz, Huti, Kalaman, Sa'fas, and Qarashat are names of kings, and their king on the day of the Cloud was in the time of Shu'ayb. The sister of Kalamun wept for him, saying:

"Kalamun, his death demolished my pillar, in the midst of the encampment, the lord of the people; death came to him as fire in the midst of the cloud. Fire made their homes over them like the extinguished."

﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb, as if they had never prospered therein﴾: that is, they had not lived, nor dwelt, nor resided, nor enjoyed comfort. Its root is from their saying "ghaniya bil-makan" when you stay in a place; al-maghani are the dwellings, and its singular is maghan. Labid said:

"And I dwelt six [years] before the course of Dahis, if the stubborn soul had immortality."

Hatim said:

"We dwelt a time in poverty and wealth, but time gave us both to drink from its two cups."

﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb—they were the losers﴾, not the believers as they claimed. ﴿So he turned away from them﴾: Shu'ayb [ibn Shamikh], from among them, when the punishment came upon them, and said: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you; so how should I grieve [sorrow] over a disbelieving people?﴾ — when they were being punished. It is said: "asaytum, I grieve, asan." The poet said:

"I grieved over Zayd and I did not know what had happened."

And al-Asa is grief, and [al-Asa] is patience.

And We did not send a prophet to any town without [its people denying him], and We seized its people with **al-ba'sa'** (hardship), meaning misery and hardship of living, and **al-darra'** (adversity), meaning harm, which is a state of affliction. It was said that it means sickness and disability. Al-Suddi said: al-ba'sa' means poverty and hunger, so that they might humble themselves (﴿la'allahum yadarra'un﴾), that is, so that they would submit humbly, [repent] and turn back. Then We replaced the evil (the hardship, the hunger and the want) with good, meaning blessing, abundance, ease and plenty, until they multiplied (﴿'afaw﴾), meaning they increased, prospered, and their wealth and children grew in number. Ibn 'Abbas said: (﴿'afaw﴾) means [they exerted themselves]. Ibn Zayd said: it means they multiplied as plants and feathers multiply.

Qatada said: (﴿hatta 'afaw﴾) means they were pleased with that. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: (﴿'afaw﴾) means until they multiplied and left [their possessions] without counting them, and its root is abundance.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Trim the moustaches and let the beards grow." [Musnad Abi Ya'la: 10/105, no. 5738.]

A poet said:

"He says, after your forefathers, there were fathers who came for a time, and it was not long ago."

Another said:

"But we bite the sword with it, with thick-fleshed, well-fed calves, a heap..."

And they said, out of their ignorance and heedlessness: "Hardship and ease have already touched our forefathers, and so we are like them." So Allah said: ﴿Then We seized them suddenly, while they did not perceive﴾, [suddenly, as a lesson] for those after them. ﴿While they did not perceive﴾ the descent of the punishment.

﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah﴾, meaning had affirmed Allah's oneness and obeyed Him, ﴿We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven﴾, meaning rain, ﴿and from the earth﴾, meaning vegetation. The root of barakah (blessing) is persistence in a thing; one says: "Barak fulan 'ala fulan" when he responded to him. [The blessings of the earth, meaning] We would have followed up on them with rain, vegetation and plenty, and removed drought and famine. ﴿But they denied, so We seized them﴾, meaning We inflicted punishments upon them ﴿for what they used to earn﴾ of disbelief, disobedience and wicked deeds.

﴿Then are the people of the towns secure, those who disbelieved and denied, that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping?﴾ meaning, safe.

﴿Or are the people of the towns secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the forenoon while they are playing?﴾ meaning in the daytime, while they are heedless.

﴿Then are they secure from the plan of Allah? But none feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ The meaning of (makr) is luring the people by what He showed them in their worldly life.

Qatada said: the plan of Allah is His luring them by prolonging their health and the continuous flow of blessings. 'Atiyya said: it means His seizing and His punishment. It is related that al-Shibli was asked about the plan of Allah, and he answered with the verse:

"Your love is not for part of me but for all of me, even if your love leaves me without movement.

And [one who] disgraces, from [those who] are born, to do my custom, and does it beautifully."

The questioner said: "Ask him about a verse from the Book of Allah, and he answers me with poetry." Al-Shibli realised that he had not grasped what he meant, and said: "O you, [...] [unreadable word] them in what they are in."

﴿Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth after its [former] people﴾ — (﴿yahdi﴾) is recited by Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Qatada and Ya'qub in one narration of Zayd as (﴿nahdi﴾) with nun, for glorification, while the rest recite it with ya' for singularity — ﴿that had We willed, We could have struck them for their sins﴾, meaning destroyed them as We destroyed those before them, ﴿and We seal over their hearts so they do not hear﴾ guidance and do not accept admonition. ﴿These are the towns﴾, meaning these towns which I have mentioned to you and which We destroyed, and they are the towns of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lot and Shu'ayb. ﴿We relate to you some of their news﴾, meaning We inform you of their stories. ﴿Their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs [with signs, indications and evidences], but they were not to believe in what they had denied before.﴾ The interpretation of this has been disputed.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: its meaning is that they were not going to believe when the messengers came in what had already been known by Allah's knowledge, that they would deny it on the day they affirmed His covenant, when He brought them out of the loins of Adam.

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: meaning these disbelievers whom We destroyed were not going to believe, when the messengers were sent, in what they had denied before, on the day their covenant was taken, until He brought them out of the back of Adam, and they believed unwillingly, affirmed with the tongue and displayed denial.

Mujahid said: its meaning is that they would not, even if We brought them back to life after their destruction and returned them to the world, believe in what they had denied before their destruction, as in His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 28]. Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: this is the meaning that every prophet who punished his people with punishment, they were not going to believe in what their predecessors among the disbelieving nations had denied, but rather they denied as they had denied. A parallel to His saying: ﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them except that they said, "A magician or a madman." Have they advised one another concerning it?﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 52–53].

It was also said: its meaning is: ﴿Their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with miracles and wonders which they asked of them, ﴿but they were not to believe﴾ after they saw the signs and wonders, ﴿in what they had denied before﴾ seeing those wonders. A poet said:

Another said:

And they said, out of their ignorance and heedlessness: "Hardship and ease have already touched our forefathers, and so we are like them." The questioner said: "Ask him about a verse from the Book of Allah, and he answers me with poetry." Al-Shibli realised that he had not grasped what he meant, and said: "O you, [...] [unreadable word] them in what they are in."

Shayba and Nafi' read it as *haqiqqun* with a doubled yā', meaning: it is a binding truth upon me to abandon saying anything about God, the Mighty and Majestic, except the truth.

﴿I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord﴾: that is, the staff. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard 'Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say: it is an allusion (ta'rid); he says: "Indeed, [I am] worthy," turning the address around. *Haqiq* is on the pattern *fa'il* from *haqq* and may be in the sense of the agent.

﴿So send with me the Children of Israel﴾: that is, release them and let them go to return to the Holy Land.

Wahb said: The reason Pharaoh enslaved the Children of Israel was that Pharaoh disputed with [Moses]. [He was stronger than] Pharaoh... Yusuf [...] [[unreadable word.]] in Yusuf [and the tribes (al-asbat) were wiped out], upon whom Pharaoh imposed, so he enslaved them, and God rescued them through Moses.

He said: The time between the day Yusuf entered Egypt and the day Moses came as a messenger was four hundred years.

Pharaoh said, replying to Moses: ﴿If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are among the truthful.﴾ Then he threw down his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent (thu'ban mubin).

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: It was [great in size among] the serpents. When it opened its mouth, its jaw became eighty [cubits], and it filled the space between the two rows of Pharaoh's guards, placing its lower jaw on the ground and its upper jaw on the wall of the palace, until some of those outside the city of Egypt saw its head.

Then it advanced toward Pharaoh to swallow him, and Pharaoh leapt from his throne and fled from it, and he defecated, which he had not done before. The people fled and shouted, and it charged upon the people, and they scattered from it, and twenty-five thousand of them died, some killing others. Pharaoh entered the house and cried: "O Moses, take it! I believe in you, and I will send the Children of Israel with you." Moses took it, and it returned to being a staff as it had been.

Then Pharaoh said to him: "Do you have another sign?" He said: "Yes." He put his hand into his garment (jayb), then drew it out, and it was white like snow, with a radiance that overcame the light of the sun. Moses was dark-complexioned (adam). Then he put it back into his garment, and it became a hand as it had been.

﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: "Indeed this is a knowing sorcerer."﴾ They meant that he takes the eyes of the people by his deception, until the staff appears to them as a serpent and the dark hand appears white, [showing a thing] contrary to what it is. As it is said, "The rain has bewitched the land (sahara al-matar al-ard)" when it reaches it and cuts off its plants from the root and turns the earth over onto its belly; so it bewitches it with a bewitching, and the land is bewitched (masura). Thus the sorcery of the sorcerer is likened to it, because it makes the one he bewitches imagine that the thing is other than it is. From this is the statement of Dhu al-Rumma describing the mirage:

"A bewitcher of eyes from the desert wastes, whose high ground dances in its ridges."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/22.]]

﴿He wants to drive you out of your land﴾: that is, [the Copts] from your land, Egypt. ﴿So what do you advise?﴾ This is from Pharaoh's speech to the chiefs, and Pharaoh is not mentioned in it, like His saying: ﴿Now the truth has come to light; it was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful. That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:51–52]. This is the speech of Yusuf, and he is not mentioned.

They said: ﴿Put him off﴾, that is, imprison him, ﴿and his brother﴾ Aaron, and do not kill them, and they will not believe in them. 'Ata' said: imprison him. This is more pleasing to me, because he knew that he could not imprison him after seeing the signs of the staff and the hand.

﴿And send to the cities gatherers﴾: that is, the police (al-shurta). He had cities in which there were many sorcerers for various matters; when a matter afflicted him, he would send for them.

﴿They will bring you every knowing sorcerer.﴾ The people of Kufa read it with the intensive form (*kulli sahir*, emphatic plural sense), while the common readers read *bi-kulli sahir*. The difference between *sahir* (sorcerer) and *sahhar* (expert sorcerer) is that the *sahir* is one who lacks knowledge, while the *sahhar* is one who has knowledge and yet does not. The historian said:

"The sahir is one who bewitches at one time and not another; the sahhar is one long practiced in sorcery."

He said: If Moses overcomes them, we will affirm that, and we will know that he is a sorcerer.

Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi said: When Pharaoh saw what he saw of God's power in the staff, he said: "We cannot overcome Moses except with someone like him." So he took the boys of the Children of Israel and sent them to a village called al-Farqa', where they would teach them sorcery as children are taught writing in a school. They taught them much sorcery. Pharaoh arranged a appointment with Moses. Pharaoh sent for the sorcerers and brought them, together with their teacher, and said to him: "What have you done?"

He said: "I have taught them a sorcery that the sorcerers of the earth cannot withstand, unless it is a command from heaven, for they have no power against it." Then Pharaoh sent the police throughout his realm, and he left no sorcerer in his dominion without bringing him. They differed about the number of sorcerers whom Pharaoh gathered.

Muqatil said: the sorcerers were seventy-two, two of them from the Copts and they were the leaders of the people, and seventy from the Children of Israel.

al-Kalbi said: They were seventy sorcerers besides their chief, and those who taught them sorcery were two Magians from the people of Nineveh. Ka'b said: They were twelve thousand. al-Suddi said: They were some thirty-odd. 'Ikrima said: seventy thousand. Ibn al-Munkadir said: eighty thousand. He chose from them seven thousand, none of whom was other than a skilled sorcerer; then he chose from them seven hundred, then from them he chose seventy of their notables and scholars. Ibn Jurayj also said this.

When the sorcerers assembled, they said to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed for us there will surely be a reward﴾, that is, a payment and a recompense.

﴿If we are the victors.﴾ Pharaoh said: "Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near," that is, in rank with me.

al-Kalbi said: [You will be] the first to enter upon me and the last to leave. They said, that is, the sorcerers:

﴿O Moses, either you throw first, or we will be the throwers﴾, with our staves [and ropes].

Moses said: ﴿Throw﴾. ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and frightened them﴾, that is, terrified and alarmed them, ﴿and they brought a great sorcery.﴾ That was because they threw ropes, bones and long pieces of wood, and behold, they were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, [devouring] one another.

Then We sent Moses after them, after the peoples of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot and Shu'ayb, with Our signs, meaning Our proof and evidence, to Pharaoh (Fir'awn) and his chiefs. But they wronged them, that is, they denied them and disbelieved in them. So look at how the end of the corrupters was. That is, how We dealt with them. Moses said when he entered upon Pharaoh, whose name was Qabus according to the People of the Book.

Wahb said: His name was al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan. He was from the Copts and lived more than four hundred years. Moses said: "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, sent to you." Pharaoh said: "You are lying." Moses said: "It is incumbent upon me that I should not say anything about God except the truth." That is, I am worthy of not saying anything about God except the truth. ﴿I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord﴾: that is, the staff. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard 'Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say: it is an allusion (ta'rid); he says: "Indeed, [I am] worthy," turning the address around. *Haqiq* is on the pattern *fa'il* from *haqq* and may be in the sense of the agent.

﴿So send with me the Children of Israel﴾: that is, release them and let them go to return to the Holy Land.

Wahb said: The reason Pharaoh enslaved the Children of Israel was that Pharaoh disputed with [Moses]. [He was stronger than] Pharaoh... Yusuf [...] [[unreadable word.]] in Yusuf [and the tribes (al-asbat) were wiped out], upon whom Pharaoh imposed, so he enslaved them, and God rescued them through Moses.

Then he put it back into his garment, and it became a hand as it had been.

﴿If we are the victors.﴾ Pharaoh said: "Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near," that is, in rank with me.

al-Kalbi said: [You will be] the first to enter upon me and the last to leave. They said, that is, the sorcerers:

﴿O Moses, either you throw first, or we will be the throwers﴾, with our staves [and ropes].

Moses said: ﴿Throw﴾. ﴿When they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and frightened them﴾, that is, terrified and alarmed them, ﴿and they brought a great sorcery.﴾ That was because they threw ropes, bones and long pieces of wood, and behold, they were serpents like mountains, filling the valley, [devouring] one another.

And We revealed to Musa: "Throw down your staff." So he threw it, and behold, it swallowed up (تبتلع) what they had fabricated. Whoever reads تَلْقَفُ (talqafu) with a sukun on the lam and a light qaf is deriving it from لقف يلقف (laqafa yalqafu). Its evidence is the reading of Sa'id ibn Jubayr: تلقم من لقم يلقم (talqamu, from laqama yalqamu).

﴿What they had fabricated﴾ means what they were lying about (يكذّبون). It was also said: what they were turning and falsifying upon the people (يقلبون ويزوّرون على الناس). So it swallowed all of their sorcery. The sorcerers said: "If this were sorcery, our ropes would have remained and we would have disobeyed." This is His saying: ﴿So the truth took effect﴾, that is, it became manifest.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: ﴿the truth took effect﴾ means it struck fear into them and terrified them [like the striking of the striking-blow]. ﴿And what they had been doing was nullified﴾ of the sorcery. ﴿So they were overcome there and were turned back humbled﴾, that is, abased and subdued.

﴿And the sorcerers were cast down prostrating﴾ before God, because they recognized that this was a heavenly matter and not sorcery. It was also said that God inspired them to do so. Al-Akhfash said: from the speed with which they prostrated, it was as if they had been thrown down. They said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds﴾. Pharaoh said: "Is it me you mean?" They said: ﴿The Lord of Musa and Harun﴾.

Ata' said: the chief of the sorcerers was at the farthest of the cities of Egypt, and they were two brothers. When Pharaoh's messenger came to them, they said to their mother: "Show us the grave of our father," and she showed it to them. They came to it and called out his name, and he answered them. They said: "The king has sent a messenger to us, asking us to come to him, because he came to him as a man with no men or weapons with him, while they have [might and protection], and the king has become exceedingly distressed by their might. With them is a staff which, when they throw it, nothing can stand before them; it swallows iron, stone and wood." Their father answered them: "Look: when they sleep, if you are able to take the staff, then take it, for a sorcerer does not work his sorcery while asleep. If the staff acts while they are asleep, that is the command of the Lord of the worlds, and neither you nor the king nor all the people of the world have any power against it." So Pharaoh's man came to them secretly while they were asleep to seize the staff, and the staff went for them. This was said by Muqatil.

Musa said to the chief sorcerer: "Will you believe in me if I overcome you?" He said: "I will certainly bring sorcery that no sorcery can overcome. And if you overcome me, I will indeed believe in you," while Pharaoh was watching. Pharaoh said to them when they believed: ﴿Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Indeed this is a scheme, a contrivance that you have devised﴾, a deception that you and Musa have contrived ﴿in the city﴾, that is, in Egypt, before your departure to this place.

﴿That you may expel its people from it by your sorcery; but you will soon know what I will do to you.﴾

﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on alternate sides﴾, which means cutting off one side's hand and the opposite side's foot. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the first to cut on alternate sides was Pharaoh. ﴿Then I will crucify you all﴾ on the bank of the river of Egypt. They said, meaning the sorcerers to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾, that is, returning in the Hereafter. ﴿And you resent us only for﴾ the reading of the common people is with a kasra on the qaf: وَما تَنْقِمُ مِنَّا (wa ma tanqimu minna).

Al-Hasan and Ibn al-Muhaysin read it with a fatha on the qaf. Both are dialects: نقم ينقم and نقم ينقم.

The poet said:

"They resented nothing of the Banu Umayya
except that they are forbearing when they are angered."

Al-Dahhak and others said: it means, "and they do not find fault with us." Ata' said: "We have no wrongdoing toward you, and we have committed no offence against you for which you punish us, except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us." Then [they turned] to God, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, pour upon us patience at the time of the cutting and the crucifixion, so that we do not return as disbelievers ﴿and let us die as Muslims﴾, take us to You upon the religion of Musa. Thus they were disbelieving sorcerers at the beginning of the day, and righteous martyrs at its end.

﴿And the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said: Will you leave Musa and his people to cause corruption in the land﴾ in the land of Egypt, ﴿and to forsake you and your gods?﴾ That is, so that they may turn your kingdom and your servants against you ﴿and [He] forsakes you﴾, meaning: and that he may forsake you.

Sulayman al-Taymi reported from Anas ibn Malik that he read وَنَذَرُكَ (wa nadhuruka) with a raised ending and a nun, [they reported] about themselves that they would abandon His worship if Musa were left alive, and so he would turn them away from us.

Al-Hasan read (وَيَذَرُكَ) with a raised ending, taking it as an implied subject: that is, "and He forsakes you." ﴿Your gods﴾, so that we do not worship you and do not worship them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had a cow that he worshipped, and whenever they saw a beautiful cow he ordered them to worship it; for this reason al-Samiri produced for them a calf.

'Amr reported from al-Husayn who said: Pharaoh had a small hanging idol on his chest which he worshipped and prostrated to, as if it were an idol whose worshipper longed for it.

It was also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Pharaoh used to make small idols for his people and command them to worship them, and he would say to them: "I am the lord of these idols." This is His saying: ﴿I am your most high lord﴾.

Abu 'Ubayd said: It reached me from al-Hasan that he was asked: "Did Pharaoh worship anything?" He said: "Yes, he worshipped a male goat."

إلهتك (ilahatika) with a kasra on the alif, meaning [your god], so that he would not be worshipped as you are worshipped. They said: "Because Pharaoh used to be worshipped but did not worship."

so our gods [the sun] were kept from returning."

meaning the sun.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the first to cut on alternate sides was Pharaoh. ﴿Then I will crucify you all﴾ on the bank of the river of Egypt. They said, meaning the sorcerers to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we are returning﴾, that is, returning in the Hereafter. ﴿And you resent us only for﴾ the reading of the common people is with a kasra on the qaf: وَما تَنْقِمُ مِنَّا (wa ma tanqimu minna).

Al-Hasan and Ibn al-Muhaysin read it with a fatha on the qaf. Both are dialects: نقم ينقم and نقم ينقم.

The poet said:

"They resented nothing of the Banu Umayya
except that they are forbearing when they are angered."

Al-Dahhak and others said: it means, "and they do not find fault with us." Ata' said: "We have no wrongdoing toward you, and we have committed no offence against you for which you punish us, except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us." Then [they turned] to God, Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿Our Lord, pour upon us patience﴾, pour upon us patience at the time of the cutting and the crucifixion, so that we do not return as disbelievers ﴿and let us die as Muslims﴾, take us to You upon the religion of Musa. Thus they were disbelieving sorcerers at the beginning of the day, and righteous martyrs at its end.

﴿And the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said: Will you leave Musa and his people to cause corruption in the land﴾ in the land of Egypt, ﴿and to forsake you and your gods?﴾ That is, so that they may turn your kingdom and your servants against you ﴿and [He] forsakes you﴾, meaning: and that he may forsake you.

Sulayman al-Taymi reported from Anas ibn Malik that he read وَنَذَرُكَ (wa nadhuruka) with a raised ending and a nun, [they reported] about themselves that they would abandon His worship if Musa were left alive, and so he would turn them away from us.

Al-Hasan read (وَيَذَرُكَ) with a raised ending, taking it as an implied subject: that is, "and He forsakes you." ﴿Your gods﴾, so that we do not worship you and do not worship them. Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh had a cow that he worshipped, and whenever they saw a beautiful cow he ordered them to worship it; for this reason al-Samiri produced for them a calf.

'Amr reported from al-Husayn who said: Pharaoh had a small hanging idol on his chest which he worshipped and prostrated to, as if it were an idol whose worshipper longed for it.

It was also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: Pharaoh used to make small idols for his people and command them to worship them, and he would say to them: "I am the lord of these idols." This is His saying: ﴿I am your most high lord﴾.

Abu 'Ubayd said: It reached me from al-Hasan that he was asked: "Did Pharaoh worship anything?" He said: "Yes, he worshipped a male goat."

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah [al-Sha'bi], al-Dahhak and Ibn Abi Ishaq read:

إلهتك (ilahatika) with a kasra on the alif, meaning [your god], so that he would not be worshipped as you are worshipped. They said: "Because Pharaoh used to be worshipped but did not worship."

It was also said that by the gods he meant the sun, which they used to worship.

[Uyayna] ibn [Shihab] said:

"We were turned away from the nobles in the afternoon,
so our gods [the sun] were kept from returning."

meaning the sun.

﴿He said﴾, meaning Pharaoh: ﴿We will kill their sons﴾ with the emphatic form for multiplicity. The people of the Hijaz read it with the light form. ﴿And we will spare their women, and indeed we are above them, dominant.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh used to kill the Children of Israel in the year in which he had been told that a boy would be born who would take away his kingdom. He kept killing them until Musa (peace be upon him) came to them with the message. When what happened with Musa happened, he ordered the killing to be resumed against them, and the Children of Israel complained to Musa (peace be upon him). At that, ﴿Musa said to his people: Seek help in God and be patient. Indeed the earth belongs to God; He gives it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants﴾, meaning the land of Egypt. Al-Hasan read يُوَرِّثُها (yuwarrithuha) with the emphatic form, but the preferred reading is the light form, because of His saying: ﴿And We caused the people to inherit the land﴾. ﴿And the final outcome is for the righteous﴾, meaning victory and triumph. It was also said: happiness and martyrdom. It was also said: Paradise.

Ikrimah reported from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When the sorcerers believed, six hundred thousand of the Children of Israel followed Musa. ﴿They said: We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us﴾, meaning the people of Musa said: we were harmed by the killing of the sons, the enslaving of the women and the forced labour, before you brought us the message, and after you brought us the message, by the renewed killing, torture, seizure of wealth and exhausting labour.

Wahb said: They were of various kinds in Pharaoh's works. As for the strong among them, they would strip the high mountains... and their necks, shoulders and hands, and their backs were lacerated from carrying that and from being killed for it. Another group had been [worn raw] by the weight of the stones and the [night] journeys made for it; another group made bricks and laid the bricks in tiers; some were carpenters and blacksmiths; and the weak among them were subject to the tax, a levy that they had to pay, which the sun was said to have struck. It was said: if one failed to pay his levy, his hand would be chained to his neck for a month. As for the women, they were made to spin and weave.

Musa (peace be upon him) said to them: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy, Pharaoh, and will make you successors in the land﴾, and will settle you in Egypt after them, by means of the forced labour and enslavement, and they are the Children of Israel.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 137–141:

the eastern and western parts of the earth (مَشارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغارِبَهَا): he means Egypt and Syria, "which We had blessed" (الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها) with water, trees and fruits. He used the expression [ ... ] [[A lacuna near the top of the page.]].

[ ... ] So He made them inherit that land after destroying its people, the Amalekites and the Pharaohs. "And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled" (وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنى): that is, the word of Allah was fulfilled, which is His promise to them of victory and establishment in the land. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land" (وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ), up to His saying "what they had been fearing" (ما كانُوا يَحْذَرُونَ).

It has also been said: its meaning is that the good blessing of your Lord [was fulfilled] upon the Children of Israel, meaning that they would be recompensed with the good (al-husna) on the Day of Resurrection "for their patience" (بِما صَبَرُوا), in their religion. "And We destroyed" (وَدَمَّرْنا), meaning We destroyed [and so We destroyed] "what Pharaoh and his people had been making" (ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ) in the land of Egypt, of the [buildings and] caves, "and what they had been erecting" (وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ).

Al-Hasan said: "what they had been erecting" (وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ) refers to fruits and plants.

Mujahid said: it means they built houses, palaces and dwellings, and [their wealthy ones] had [buildings] that were not raised on supports.

Ibn 'Amir and Ibn 'Abbas recited يَعْرُشُونَ with a damma on the ra'. Both are eloquent dialects: 'arasha yaʿrishu and ʿarasha yaʿrushu.

Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah recited يعرِّشون with shaddah on the kasrah.

"And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea" (وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ), that is, We made them cross it, after the signs they had seen and the sea they had witnessed.

Al-Kalbi said: Moses took them across on the day they were rescued after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, and he fasted that day out of gratitude to Allah, may He be exalted.

"Then they came upon a people who were devoted to" (فَأَتَوْا عَلى قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ), that is, praying. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited يَعْكِفُونَ with a kasrah on the kaf, while the rest recited it with a damma. Both are dialects. "Idols" (عَلى أَصْنامٍ), that is, idols they had, which they worshipped besides Allah, may He be exalted.

Ibn Juraij said: they were images of cows, and that was the beginning of the affair of the calf.

Qatadah said: those people were from Lakhm, and these [Israelites] were at al-Rammah. It has also been said that they were of the Canaanites, whom Moses had been ordered to fight. So when the Children of Israel saw that, they said to him: "O Moses, make for us a god, just as they have gods" (قالُوا يا مُوسَى اجْعَلْ لَنا إِلهاً كَما لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ). Moses said: "Indeed you are a people who are ignorant" (إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ), that is, ignorant of the greatness of Allah, His blessing and His sanctity.

Ma'mar narrated from al-Zuhri, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before Hunayn, and we passed by a great green tree. We said: "O Messenger of Allah, make for us this one a Dhat Anwat, as they have a Dhat Anwat." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Moses (peace be upon him): 'Make for us a god, as they have gods' (اجْعَلْ لَنا إِلهاً كَما لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ). By Him in whose hand my soul is, you will certainly follow the ways of those who were before you." [193] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/218. And Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 9/61.]]

It was also narrated from him (peace be upon him) that he said: "The Hour will not come until my nation takes the path of the nations before it, span by span and cubit by cubit, as Persia and Byzantium did." [194] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 8/151.]]

"Indeed, these people, what they are in is destroyed" (إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ), meaning doomed, ruined and lost, "and what they have been doing is in vain" (وَباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ), meaning vanished and perished. He said: "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah" (قالَ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِيكُمْ), that is, seek and desire for you. The preposition was omitted, as in His saying: "And Moses chose his people" (وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ), ... [a god], "while He has preferred you over the worlds" (وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ), that is, over the people of your time.

"And when We rescued you" (وَإِذْ نَجَّيْناكُمْ): the people of Madinah recited أَنْجَيْناكُمْ, while the people of Syria recited وإذ أنجاكم, and so it is in their codices without the nun.

"From the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, slaughtering your sons" (مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ).

Nafi' recited يَقْتُلُونَ with a light pronunciation, from killing in a small quantity, while the rest recited it with the shaddah, indicating killing in large quantity. "And they spared your women" (وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِساءَكُمْ). "And in that was a great trial from your Lord" (وَفِي ذلِكُمْ بَلاءٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ).

the eastern and western parts of the earth (مَشارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغارِبَهَا): he means Egypt and Syria, "which We had blessed" (الَّتِي بارَكْنا فِيها) with water, trees and fruits. He used the expression [ ... ] [[A lacuna near the top of the page.]].

[ ... ] So He made them inherit that land after destroying its people, the Amalekites and the Pharaohs. "And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled" (وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ الْحُسْنى): that is, the word of Allah was fulfilled, which is His promise to them of victory and establishment in the land. This is His saying, may He be exalted: "And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land" (وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ), up to His saying "what they had been fearing" (ما كانُوا يَحْذَرُونَ).

It has also been said: its meaning is that the good blessing of your Lord [was fulfilled] upon the Children of Israel, meaning that they would be recompensed with the good (al-husna) on the Day of Resurrection "for their patience" (بِما صَبَرُوا), in their religion. "And We destroyed" (وَدَمَّرْنا), meaning We destroyed [and so We destroyed] "what Pharaoh and his people had been making" (ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ) in the land of Egypt, of the [buildings and] caves, "and what they had been erecting" (وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ).

Al-Hasan said: "what they had been erecting" (وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ) refers to fruits and plants.

Mujahid said: it means they built houses, palaces and dwellings, and [their wealthy ones] had [buildings] that were not raised on supports.

Ibn 'Amir and Ibn 'Abbas recited يَعْرُشُونَ with a damma on the ra'. Both are eloquent dialects: 'arasha yaʿrishu and ʿarasha yaʿrushu.

Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah recited يعرِّشون with shaddah on the kasrah.

"And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea" (وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ الْبَحْرَ), that is, We made them cross it, after the signs they had seen and the sea they had witnessed.

Al-Kalbi said: Moses took them across on the day they were rescued after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, and he fasted that day out of gratitude to Allah, may He be exalted.

"Then they came upon a people who were devoted to" (فَأَتَوْا عَلى قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ), that is, praying. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited يَعْكِفُونَ with a kasrah on the kaf, while the rest recited it with a damma. Both are dialects. "Idols" (عَلى أَصْنامٍ), that is, idols they had, which they worshipped besides Allah, may He be exalted.

Ibn Juraij said: they were images of cows, and that was the beginning of the affair of the calf.

Qatadah said: those people were from Lakhm, and these [Israelites] were at al-Rammah. It has also been said that they were of the Canaanites, whom Moses had been ordered to fight. So when the Children of Israel saw that, they said to him: "O Moses, make for us a god, just as they have gods" (قالُوا يا مُوسَى اجْعَلْ لَنا إِلهاً كَما لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ). We said: "O Messenger of Allah, make for us this one a Dhat Anwat, as they have a Dhat Anwat." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar! This is just as the Children of Israel said to Moses (peace be upon him): 'Make for us a god, as they have gods' (اجْعَلْ لَنا إِلهاً كَما لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ). "Indeed, these people, what they are in is destroyed" (إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ مُتَبَّرٌ), meaning doomed, ruined and lost, "and what they have been doing is in vain" (وَباطِلٌ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ), meaning vanished and perished. Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 7, verses 142–147 (part 1 of 2):

﴿We appointed for Moses thirty nights, and We completed them with ten more, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete at forty nights.﴾ When he set out, he said to his brother Harun: ﴿Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.﴾ That is, set them right by leading them to obedience to God, ﴿and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾, meaning do not take the path of the disobedient, and do not be a helper of the wrongdoers.

The reason is that Moses had promised the Children of Israel, while they were in Egypt, that once God destroyed their enemy and rescued them from his hands, he would bring them a book containing what they should do and what they should avoid. When God did that for them, Moses asked his Lord for the book, and God commanded him to fast for thirty days, which was the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the thirty nights were complete, he noticed that the smell of his mouth had changed (khuluq: smell). So he cleaned his teeth with a twig of [ḍarnub]. The angels said to him: "We used to smell the scent of musk from your mouth, and you spoiled it with the siwak (tooth-stick)." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/274.]]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "He ate from the bark of a tree, so God commanded him to fast ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah." He (God) said: "Do you not know that the smell of the mouth of one who fasts is more fragrant to Me than the scent of musk?" So their trial was in the ten days which God added.

﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time﴾, that is, at the set time, when he asked Him to speak to him. The word mīqāt (appointed time) is on the pattern mif'āl, derived from waqt (time), like mī'ād (appointment) and bilād (lands). The waw was changed into yā' because it was sukūn (unvowelled) and the letter before it was kasrah (vowelled with i).

The commentators (mufassirun) said: Moses (peace be upon him) purified himself and purified his garments for the appointment with his Lord. When he came to Mount Sinai, ﴿his Lord spoke to him﴾, communicated with him, and brought him near, until he heard the sounds of the pen, so he longed for His speech, yearned for His vision and desired it. ﴿He said: "My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Give me [the ability] that I may look at You." ﴿God said: "You will not see Me."﴾ And a human being cannot bear to look at Me in this world; whoever looks at Me dies. Then Moses said: "I heard Your speech and I longed to look upon You. So if I look upon You and die, that is dearer to me than living without seeing You." Then God said: ﴿But look at the mountain.﴾ It was the greatest mountain in Madyan, called Zubayr. When the mountains heard that, they became proud, hoping that God would manifest Himself to them. Zubayr began to humble itself from its place, and when God saw its humility, He raised it up between them and specially favoured it with the manifestation.

Al-Suddi said: When God spoke to Moses, the wicked Iblis (Satan) plunged into the earth until he emerged between Moses' feet. He whispered to him and said: "The one who speaks to you is Satan." At that moment Moses asked for the vision, and God said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾ [...] [[Unreadable word.]] the vision is connected with this verse, but they have no proof from it, because the particle lan (never) here does not imply perpetuity; it is for a limited time, as God says, quoting the Jews: ﴿They will never wish for death﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 95.]], meaning death itself. Then He mentions that they say: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us﴾ [[Surat al-Zukhruf: 77.]], and ﴿Would that it had been the end!﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqah: 27.]], meaning death. And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿You will never attain righteousness﴾, meaning Paradise, ﴿until you spend of what you love﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 92]; yet one may enter Paradise without spending of what [he knows]. So the meaning of the verse is: "You will not see Me in this world, but you will see Me in the Hereafter."

'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: His saying ﴿You will not see Me﴾ is the answer to Moses' words ﴿Show me that I may look upon You﴾, and it does not refer to the Hereafter, because Moses did not say "Show me that I may look at You in the Hereafter"; he asked for the vision in this world, so he was answered regarding what he asked. There is no proof in it for those who deny the vision.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿You will not see Me﴾ is: you are not able to see Me. It was said: its meaning is: you will not see Me with a mortal eye, but you will see Me with an eternal eye. It was said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾ before Muhammad and his community, but you will see Me after Muhammad and his community. It was said: its meaning is: you will not see Me by asking and supplicating, but you will see Me by bounty and gift; for if He gave it to him by his request, the vision would be a recompense for the request, whereas it is permissible for His act to be a recompense for the act of His servant, but it is not permissible for Him to be the recompense for the act of His servant.

It was also said: its meaning is: you will not see Me with the eye with which you saw My enemy, for Satan appeared to him and whispered to him. God said: "O Moses, do you not know that the seeing of the wicked and the seeing of God cannot coincide in one state, one place and one time?"

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard 'Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say: "If Moses' request had been impossible, the Prophet of God Moses (peace be upon him) would not have made it, with his knowledge and his understanding of God, may His name be exalted, just as it would not be permissible for him to ask for a consort or a son for Him."

God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.﴾ Its remaining (istiqrar) means its being in place and steady.

The speakers of theology (mutakallimun) from the people of Syria said: When God made the vision conditional upon the mountain's remaining in place, this indicates that the vision is permissible, because the mountain's remaining in place is not impossible; so this indicates that what the vision is made conditional upon is likewise not impossible. Do you not see that when the entry of the disbelievers into Paradise was impossible, He made it conditional upon something impossible, namely His saying: ﴿They will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ [[Surat al-A'raf: 40.]].

The people of wisdom and allusion (ahl al-hikmah wa al-ishārah) said: When the Speaker (al-Kalim) wished to go out to the appointed time, he placed an intermediary between his people and his Lord. He said to his brother Harun: ﴿Take my place among my people.﴾ When he asked for the vision, God placed between him and it an intermediary, which is the mountain, as God says: ﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain.﴾ It is as if He were saying: "If I am not fit to be your successor without your brother, then you too are not fit to see Me without the mountain's remaining in place." ﴿Then when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾.

Wahb said: When Moses asked for the vision, God sent upon him the mist, the thunderbolts, the darkness, the thunder and the lightning, and they surrounded the mountain on which Moses was. God commanded the angels of the heavens to line up around Moses at four farsakhs (leagues) from every side. There passed by him a great multitude of the angels of the first heaven, whose mouths were glorifying and sanctifying with voices like the loud sound of thunder. Then God commanded the angels of the second heaven to descend upon Moses, and they descended upon him like lions, roaring with glorification and sanctification, and the weak servant, the son of 'Imran, was terrified by what he saw and heard, and every hair on his head and body stood on end.

Then he said: "I regret my request. Will anything save me from the place I am in?" The chief and head of the angels said to him: "O Moses, be patient in what you asked for; what you have seen is a little of much." Then the angels of the third heaven descended, like eagles, with crashing, trembling and a mighty roar, their mouths glorifying and sanctifying like the marching of a great army and the blaze of fire.

Then the angels of the fourth heaven descended upon him, none of them resembling those who had passed by him before; their colours were like the blaze of fire, the rest of their form was like white snow, their voices were loud in glorification and sanctification, and none of the voices of those who had passed by him before came close to theirs.

Then the angels of the fifth heaven descended upon them, of seven colours, and his eye could not follow them; he had never seen their like nor heard voices like theirs. His inside was filled with fear, his grief intensified and his weeping increased. The chief and head of the angels said to him: "Son of 'Imran, stay where you are until you see what you cannot endure." Then God, may He be exalted, commanded the angels of the sixth heaven: "Descend upon My servant, who desired to see Me," so they stood around him and descended upon him, each angel holding in his hand something like a tall great palm tree of fire, brighter than the sun, and their garments were like the blaze of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, all the angels of the heavens before them responded to them, shouting with the strength of their voices: "Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of Might, Who never dies." On the head of each of them were four faces. When Moses saw them, he raised his voice to glorify with them when they glorified, weeping and saying: "Lord, remember me and do not forget Your servant. I do not know whether I will return from what I am in or not. If I go out, I will be burned, and if I remain, I will die." The chief and leader of the angels said to him: "O son of 'Imran, your inside is about to be filled and your heart about to be torn out; be patient for what you have sat down for."

Then God, may He be exalted, commanded that His Throne be carried by the angels of the seventh heaven, and He said: "Show it to him." When the light of the Throne appeared, the mountain split apart from the greatness of the Lord, the angels of the heavens raised their voices altogether, the mountain shook, and every tree in it was uprooted. The weak servant Moses fell down in a swoon on his face, his soul not with him.
