'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya said: His saying ﴿You will not see Me﴾ is the answer to Moses' words ﴿Show me that I may look upon You﴾, and it does not refer to the Hereafter, because Moses did not say "Show me that I may look at You in the Hereafter"; he asked for the vision in this world, so he was answered regarding what he asked. There is no proof in it for those who deny the vision.

It was also said: The meaning of ﴿You will not see Me﴾ is: you are not able to see Me. It was said: its meaning is: you will not see Me with a mortal eye, but you will see Me with an eternal eye. It was said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾ before Muhammad and his community, but you will see Me after Muhammad and his community. It was said: its meaning is: you will not see Me by asking and supplicating, but you will see Me by bounty and gift; for if He gave it to him by his request, the vision would be a recompense for the request, whereas it is permissible for His act to be a recompense for the act of His servant, but it is not permissible for Him to be the recompense for the act of His servant.

It was also said: its meaning is: you will not see Me with the eye with which you saw My enemy, for Satan appeared to him and whispered to him. God said: "O Moses, do you not know that the seeing of the wicked and the seeing of God cannot coincide in one state, one place and one time?"

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard 'Ali ibn Mahdi al-Tabari say: "If Moses' request had been impossible, the Prophet of God Moses (peace be upon him) would not have made it, with his knowledge and his understanding of God, may His name be exalted, just as it would not be permissible for him to ask for a consort or a son for Him."

God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me.﴾ Its remaining (istiqrar) means its being in place and steady.

The speakers of theology (mutakallimun) from the people of Syria said: When God made the vision conditional upon the mountain's remaining in place, this indicates that the vision is permissible, because the mountain's remaining in place is not impossible; so this indicates that what the vision is made conditional upon is likewise not impossible. Do you not see that when the entry of the disbelievers into Paradise was impossible, He made it conditional upon something impossible, namely His saying: ﴿They will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ [[Surat al-A'raf: 40.]].

The people of wisdom and allusion (ahl al-hikmah wa al-ishārah) said: When the Speaker (al-Kalim) wished to go out to the appointed time, he placed an intermediary between his people and his Lord. He said to his brother Harun: ﴿Take my place among my people.﴾ When he asked for the vision, God placed between him and it an intermediary, which is the mountain, as God says: ﴿You will not see Me, but look at the mountain.﴾ It is as if He were saying: "If I am not fit to be your successor without your brother, then you too are not fit to see Me without the mountain's remaining in place." ﴿Then when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾.

Wahb said: When Moses asked for the vision, God sent upon him the mist, the thunderbolts, the darkness, the thunder and the lightning, and they surrounded the mountain on which Moses was. God commanded the angels of the heavens to line up around Moses at four farsakhs (leagues) from every side. There passed by him a great multitude of the angels of the first heaven, whose mouths were glorifying and sanctifying with voices like the loud sound of thunder. Then God commanded the angels of the second heaven to descend upon Moses, and they descended upon him like lions, roaring with glorification and sanctification, and the weak servant, the son of 'Imran, was terrified by what he saw and heard, and every hair on his head and body stood on end.

Then he said: "I regret my request. Will anything save me from the place I am in?" The chief and head of the angels said to him: "O Moses, be patient in what you asked for; what you have seen is a little of much." Then the angels of the third heaven descended, like eagles, with crashing, trembling and a mighty roar, their mouths glorifying and sanctifying like the marching of a great army and the blaze of fire.

Then the angels of the fourth heaven descended upon him, none of them resembling those who had passed by him before; their colours were like the blaze of fire, the rest of their form was like white snow, their voices were loud in glorification and sanctification, and none of the voices of those who had passed by him before came close to theirs.

Then the angels of the fifth heaven descended upon them, of seven colours, and his eye could not follow them; he had never seen their like nor heard voices like theirs. His inside was filled with fear, his grief intensified and his weeping increased. The chief and head of the angels said to him: "Son of 'Imran, stay where you are until you see what you cannot endure." Then God, may He be exalted, commanded the angels of the sixth heaven: "Descend upon My servant, who desired to see Me," so they stood around him and descended upon him, each angel holding in his hand something like a tall great palm tree of fire, brighter than the sun, and their garments were like the blaze of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, all the angels of the heavens before them responded to them, shouting with the strength of their voices: "Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of Might, Who never dies." On the head of each of them were four faces. When Moses saw them, he raised his voice to glorify with them when they glorified, weeping and saying: "Lord, remember me and do not forget Your servant. I do not know whether I will return from what I am in or not. If I go out, I will be burned, and if I remain, I will die." The chief and leader of the angels said to him: "O son of 'Imran, your inside is about to be filled and your heart about to be torn out; be patient for what you have sat down for."

Then God, may He be exalted, commanded that His Throne be carried by the angels of the seventh heaven, and He said: "Show it to him." When the light of the Throne appeared, the mountain split apart from the greatness of the Lord, the angels of the heavens raised their voices altogether, the mountain shook, and every tree in it was uprooted. The weak servant Moses fell down in a swoon on his face, his soul not with him. God then turned the stone on which Moses was into something like a hollow, shaped like a dome, so that Moses would not be burned. Then God sent to him the spirit of life, and Moses rose, glorifying God and saying: "I have believed that You are my Lord, and I have confirmed that no one sees You and remains alive. Whoever looks at Your angels, his heart is torn out. How great You are, and how great Your angels are! You are the Lord of lords, the God of gods, the King of kings; nothing equals You and nothing stands up to You. Lord, I repent to You. Praise be to God, there is no partner for You, Lord of the worlds." [[In full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/70, with variation and addition.]]

Al-Suddi said: The mountain was surrounded by angels, the angels were surrounded by fire, the fire was surrounded by angels, and the angels were surrounded by fire; then your Lord manifested Himself to the mountain.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The light of His Lord appeared to the mountain, the mountain Zubayr. [[Zad al-Masir: 3/174.]] Al-Dahhak said: God brought forth for it from the light of the veils something like the nostril of a bull.

'Abd Allah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar said: What manifested of God's majesty to the mountain was only like the eye of a needle, meaning it became dust (dakk).

Al-Suddi said: What manifested of Him was only the size of the little finger. This is shown by what was narrated from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited this verse and said: "Like this," and he placed the thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, and the mountain collapsed.

Sufyan said: The mountain sank into the earth until it reached the sea, and it still moves with it.

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali said: It split and went under the earth, and it will not appear until the Day of Resurrection.

'Ata' al-'Awfi said: ﴿He made it dakk﴾, that is, a vast sand. Al-Kalbi said: ﴿He made it dakk﴾, that is, shattered into small mountains. Al-Hasan said: ﴿He made it dakk﴾, that is, utterly gone. Masruq said: It became small, [like a hillock] [[See Fath al-Qadir: 2/243.]].

Al-Hasan: God revealed to the mountain: "Can you bear My vision?" So the mountain was split and sank into the earth while Moses watched, until it was gone entirely.

Qutrub said: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾ means: his Lord's command came to the mountain, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town in which we were﴾ [[Surat Yusuf: 82.]].

Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is: ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself﴾ as a sign to the mountain; he made it a transitive verb, [like al-takhallus (escaping), al-tabaddul (changing) and al-tawa'uud (threatening)].

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: It was related to me from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that God manifested, from behind seventy thousand veils, light the size of a dirham, and so the mountain became dakk.

Abu Bakr said: At that time every water became sweet, every madman recovered, every sick person was healed, the thorns were removed from the trees, the earth became fertile and blossomed, and the fires of the Magians went out, and the idols fell on their faces. ﴿He made it dakk﴾, levelled and flat with the ground. Ibn 'Abbas said: He made it dust.

It is narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His saying ﴿When his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it dakk﴾: "Six mountains flew away from its greatness: three fell in Madinah, Uhud, Warqan and Radwa, and three fell in Makkah: Thawr, Thabirah and Hira'." [195] [[Tarikh Baghdad: 10/440, and Fath al-Bari: 6/307.]]

The recitations differed on this word. 'Asim read dakkan with a short vowel and tanwin, and the one in al-Kahf with a long vowel. Others among the people of Kufa and Himyar read (dakka') with the long vowel, not subject to tanwin. The rest read it short with a raised ending and tanwin. This is the preference of Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd. Whoever reads it short, its meaning is "made crushed" (madkuk). Dakk and daqq have the same meaning, because the kaf and qaf interchange, as in their saying kalam raqiq and rakik (delicate and weak speech). It may also mean: God crushed it to dust, that is, God reduced it to powder, as in His saying ﴿When the earth is levelled to dakk﴾ and His saying ﴿and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with one crushing﴾ [[Surat al-Haqqah: 14.]].

Hamid said:
"He crushes the pillars of the mountains, his assault... strutting with white swords, his troops."

Whoever reads it long, it is from the Arabs' saying "a she-camel dakka'" when she has no hump. Then its meaning is: He also made it dakka', that is, level, with nothing on it, because the mountain is masculine. This is the view of the people of Kufa.

The grammarians of Basra said: Its meaning is: He made it like dakk, and the word "like" was omitted, so it was treated as if it were ﴿and ask the town﴾. Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads it long says in the plural dakka'at, like hamra'at and hamrah. Whoever says "ard dakk" says in the plural dukuk.

﴿And Moses fell down﴾, that is, he collapsed. ﴿Senseless﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he fainted. Qatadah said: dead.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿Moses fell down senseless﴾ on the day of Thursday, the day of 'Arafah, and he was given the Torah on Friday [the day of sacrifice].

Al-Waqidi said: When Moses fell down senseless, the angels of the heavens said: "What is it with the son of 'Imran and his request for the vision?!" It is related in some books that the angels of the heavens came to Moses while he was in a swoon, and they began to kick him with their feet and say: "Son of the menstruating women, did you aspire to see the Lord of might?"

﴿When he recovered from his swoon﴾ and his mind returned, he knew that he had done something that ought not to be done. ﴿He said: "Glory be to You, I repent to You from my request for the vision, and I am the first of the believers﴾ that You cannot be seen in this world." [Al-Suddi said] and Mujahid said: "And I am the first of those among the Children of Israel who believed in You."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Nasrabadhi relate from al-Junayd [that he said:] "I came to You from the tribes in a matter which my intention does not attach to. So I am the first of the believers that You cannot be seen in this world, because the first to ask You for the vision [...]" [[Unreadable word.]].

Ibn 'Abbas said: When Moses set out for Mount Sinai for the appointment, his Lord said to him: "What do you seek?" He said: "I came seeking guidance." He said: "You have found it, O Moses." Moses said: "O Lord, which of Your servants is dearest to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is most distant?" He said: "The one who judges by truth and does not follow desire." He said: "Which of Your servants is most knowing?" He said: "The one who seeks to bring the knowledge of people to his knowledge, who hears a word that guides him to guidance, and who turns back a bad custom."

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: When God brought Moses near at Mount Sinai, he saw a servant sitting in the shade of the Throne, and he said: "What is this?" He said: "This is a servant who does not envy people for what God has given them of His bounty, who is good to his parents, and who does not walk about with tale-bearing."

Moses said: "O Lord, forgive me my past sins, what has passed, what lies between that, and what You know better than I do. I seek refuge with You from the whispering of my soul and from the evil of my deeds." He said: "You have been spared that, O Moses." He said: "O Lord, which deed is dearest to You that I should do?" He said: "Remember Me and do not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants has the best deeds?" He said: "The one whose tongue does not lie, whose heart does not sin, and whose private parts do not commit adultery, [and who has good character]." He said: "Which of Your servants has the worst deeds?" He said: "The wicked one with bad character, [a corpse by night], idle by day." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 61/133.]]

﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech, so take what I have given you, and be among the grateful﴾, to God, glory be to Him, for His blessings.

Abu 'Amr Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdun al-Furati informed us. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bukayr al-Razi informed us, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yahya ibn Salam, the imam, informed us, Ahmad ibn Hassan ibn Musa al-Balkhi informed us, Abu 'Asim Isma'il ibn 'Ata' ibn Qays [al-Umawi] informed us, from Abu Hazim al-Madani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God gave Moses the tablets and he looked into them, he said: 'O Lord, You have honoured me with an honour You have not given to anyone before me.' He said: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech, so take what I have given you, and be among the grateful﴾, with diligence, preservation, and death upon love of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Moses said: "O Lord, who is Muhammad?" He said: "Ahmad the Prophet, whose name I inscribed upon My Throne two thousand years before I created the heavens. He is My prophet, My chosen one, My beloved, and the best of My creation, and he is dearer to Me than all My creation and all My angels."

Moses said: "O Lord, if Muhammad is dearer to You than all Your creation, then have You created a nation more honoured by You than my nation?" He said: "O Moses, the excellence of the nation of Muhammad over all other creation is like My excellence over all My creation." He said:

"O Lord, I wish I had seen them." He said: "O Moses, you will not see them. If you wish to hear their speech, I will let you hear it." He said:

"O Lord, I wish to hear their speech." Allah, exalted is He, said: "O nation of Aḥmad" — and they answered us, all of them, from the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers: "Here we are, O Allah, here we are. Verily the praise and the blessing are Yours, and the dominion; You have no partner. Here we are." Allah, exalted is He, said: "O nation of Aḥmad, My mercy has preceded My wrath, and My pardon has preceded My reckoning. I have given you before you ask Me, I have answered you before you call upon Me, and I have forgiven you before you disobey Me. Whoever comes to Me on the Day of Resurrection bearing the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is My servant and My messenger, will enter Paradise, even if his sins are more than the foam of the sea." And this is His saying, mighty and majestic be He: [196]

﴿And you were not at the side of the mount when We called...﴾ up to His saying ﴿...among the witnesses.﴾

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAli ibn Nusayr al-Muzakki informed us; Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Isḥaq al-Sarraj informed us; Qutayba ibn Saʿid narrated to us; Rushd ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Maʿafiri, from his father, that Kaʿb al-Aḥbar saw a rabbi of the Jews weeping. He said: "What makes you weep?"

He said: "I remembered some matters."

Kaʿb said to him: "I adjure you by Allah, if I tell you what made you weep, will you believe me?"

He said: "Yes."

He said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed [Book] that Moses (peace be upon him) looked into the Torah and said:
'I find a nation, the best of nations brought forth for mankind, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, who believe in Allah, the Messenger and the other Book, and who fight the people of misguidance until they fight the one-eyed Dajjal.' Moses said: 'Lord, make them my nation.' He said: 'They are the nation of Muhammad, O Moses.'" The rabbi said: "Yes."

He said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed Book of Allah that Moses looked into the Torah and said: 'Lord, I find a nation who eat their expiations and their charities, whereas the earlier ones used to burn their charities with fire. Moses used to gather the charities of the Children of Israel, and he would not find a slave, male or female, except that he bought him with those charities and then freed him; what remained, he dug for it a deep pit and cast it in and buried it, lest they return to it. They are the ones who respond, and those for whom intercession is granted, the intercessors and those for whom intercession is made.'" Moses said: "Make them my nation?" He said: "They are the nation of Aḥmad, O Moses." The rabbi said: "Yes."

Kaʿb said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed Book of Allah that Moses looked into the Torah and said: 'I find a nation that, when one of them ascends a height, glorifies Allah, and when he descends a valley, praises Allah; the dust is purifying for them and the earth a place of prayer wherever they are; they purify themselves from major impurity; their purification with dust is like their purification with water when they do not find water; they are not marked by the traces of ablution.' Make them my nation?" He said: "They are the nation of Aḥmad, O Moses." The rabbi said: "Yes."

Kaʿb said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed Book of Allah that Moses looked into the Torah and said: 'Lord, I find a nation that, when one of them intends a good deed and does not do it, a good deed like it is recorded for him; and if he does it, it is recorded as ten to seven hundred times its like. When one of them intends an evil deed and does not do it, nothing is recorded against him; and if he does it, one like it is recorded.'" He said: "Make them my nation?" He said: "They are the nation of Aḥmad, O Moses." The rabbi said: "Yes."

Kaʿb said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed Book of Allah that Moses looked into the Torah and said: 'Lord, I find a merciful nation, weak, who inherit the Book which We have chosen [for Our servants]; among them is one who wrongs himself, among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds,' so I find none of them except that he is shown mercy. Make them my nation?" He said: "They are the nation of Aḥmad, O Moses." The rabbi said: "Yes."

Kaʿb said: "I adjure you by Allah, do you find in the revealed Book of Allah that Moses looked into the Torah and said: 'Lord, I find in the Torah a nation whose Qur'ans are in their chests, who wear the colours of the garments of the people of Paradise, who form their rows in prayer like the rows of the angels, whose voices in their mosques are like the humming of bees, and none of them enters the Fire except one who sees the reckoning as one sees the stone from behind the tree.' Moses said: 'Then make them my nation?' He said: 'They are the nation of Aḥmad, O Moses.' The rabbi said: 'Yes.'"

When Moses was amazed at the good that Allah, blessed and exalted, had given Muhammad (ﷺ), he said: "Would that I were among the companions of Muhammad." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed to him three verses to satisfy him with them: ﴿O Moses, I have chosen you above the people...﴾ up to His saying ﴿...the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾ And ﴿Among the people of Moses is a nation who guide by the truth and by it act justly.﴾ He said: So Moses was fully content. [[At length in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/125.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We wrote for him﴾ — meaning for Moses — ﴿on the tablets.﴾

Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: The tablets of Moses (peace be upon him) were of *burd* (a green gemstone). [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/89.]] Ibn Jurayj said: They were of emerald, which Allah commanded Jibril to bring from Eden, and he wrote on them with the pen with which he had written the Reminder, drawing ink from the sea of light, and he wrote the tablets for him.

Al-Kalbi said: The tablets were of green chrysolite and red ruby; Allah wrote in them eighteen verses concerning the Children of Israel, and they are ten verses in the Torah. Wahb said: Allah commanded him to cut the tablets from a solid rock, which Allah softened for him; he cut them with his hand, then split them with his fingers, and Moses heard the scratching of the pen with the Ten Words. That was the first day of Dhu al-Qaʿda, and the tablets were ten, the length of Moses (peace be upon him).

Muqatil and Kaʿb said: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets﴾ like the engraving of a seal, and in them was written: "I am Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Do not associate anything with Me, of the inhabitants of heaven or of the inhabitants of earth, for all of that is My creation. Do not cut off the roads, do not swear falsely by My name, for whoever swears falsely by My name, I will not purify him. Do not kill, do not commit adultery, and do not disobey your parents."

Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: The Torah was revealed in seventy camel-loads; a portion of it could be read in a year, and only four men read it in full: Moses, Yusha', ʿUzayr and ʿIsa (peace be upon them). He said: "This verse is a thousand verses," meaning His saying ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything an admonition and a detailed explanation of everything﴾, of commands and prohibitions, the lawful and the unlawful, the limits and the rulings.

﴿So take hold of them with strength.﴾ Muqatil said: with earnestness and perseverance. Al-Dahhak said: with obedience. ﴿And command your people, they will take the best of them.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, in a narration of al-Kalbi, said: the best of what they were commanded in the land, so that they might make lawful its lawful things and unlawful its unlawful things; and Moses was more hostile to his people, so he was commanded with what they were not commanded. Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Jarir said: the best of them are the obligations, since there were commands and prohibitions in them; so Allah commanded them to act upon what He commanded them and to abandon what He forbade them, for acting upon what is commanded is better than acting upon what is forbidden.

It was also said: its meaning is that they should take hold of them and do their best in acting upon them. Qutrub said: ﴿they will take the best of them﴾ means "by their goodness," and "all of it is good," like His saying ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾. [[Surah al-ʿAnkabut: 45.]] Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the meaning of "the best of them" is that one imagines for a word two or three meanings and turns it toward the resemblance of truth. It was also said: there were obligations with no excess in them, and virtues recommended, and the best is to combine the obligations and the virtues.

﴿I will show you the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾ The people of meanings said: this is like a speaker saying to one he addresses, "I will show you tomorrow," in a threat and warning to whoever opposes My command.

Mujahid said: ﴿I will show you the abode of the wrongdoers﴾ — their destination in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan said: Jahannam. Qatadah and others said: "I will cause you to enter the Fire, and I will show you the dwellings of the disbelievers, who are its inhabitants, of the tyrants and the ʿAmalaqa."

ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfi said: its meaning is "I will show you the abode of Pharaoh and his people," which is Egypt.

Ibn ʿAbbas and Qasama ibn Zuhayr recited: "I will bequeath to you the abode of the wrongdoers." Al-Kalbi said: "the abode of the wrongdoers" is what they passed by when they travelled, the dwellings of ʿAd and Thamud and the generations who were destroyed. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿I will show you the abode of the wrongdoers﴾ is where their settlement ends up in [the land].

Ibn Zayd said: it means the ways of the earlier ones. It was also said: "the abode" means destruction, and its plural is *adwar*. This is because when Allah drowned Pharaoh, He revealed to the sea that it should cast their bodies onto the shore, and it did so; the Children of Israel looked at them, and He showed them the destruction of the wrongdoers.

Yaman said: it means the dwelling of Pharaoh.

﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant in the land without right.﴾ Some people said: the ruling of this verse is specific to the people of Egypt, meaning by "My signs" the nine signs which Allah, glorified is He, gave to Moses (peace be upon him).

Others said: it is general. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: it means concerning the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, of the sun, the moon, the stars, the seas, the trees, the plants and others: I turn them away from reflecting upon them and taking lessons from them. Al-Farra' — that is, al-Gharbani — said: "I prevent their hearts from reflecting upon My affair."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Saʿid Muhammad ibn Nafiʿ al-Sijzi say in Herat: I heard Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami say: I heard ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn al-ʿAla' al-ʿAttar say: I heard Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, when he was asked about this verse, say: "I will prevent them from understanding the Qur'an."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Saʿid al-Razi say: I heard al-ʿAbbas ibn Hamza say: I heard Dhu al-Nun al-Misri say: "Allah refuses to honour the hearts of the wrongdoers" — written: "the wisdom of the Qur'an."

﴿And if they see﴾ — meaning these arrogant ones —

Malik ibn Dinar recited: ﴿if they are shown﴾ with a *dammah* on the *ya'*, meaning: Allah will do so to them. ﴿The way of rectitude﴾ — the path of guidance and uprightness — ﴿they will not take it as a way for themselves﴾; ﴿and if they see the way of error﴾ — meaning misguidance and destruction — ﴿they will take it as a way.﴾

Mujahid, Humayd, Talha, al-A'mash, Hamza, Yahya and al-Kisa'i recited: "al-Rashad" with a *fatha* on the *ra'* and the *shin*, and they are two dialects, like *al-saqam* and *al-saqam*, *al-huzn* and *al-huzn*, *al-bukhl* and *al-bukhl*. Abu ʿAmr used to distinguish between them, saying: *al-Rushd* with a *damma* means righteousness and soundness in an affair, as in His saying: ﴿If you perceive in them rushd (maturity)﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 6.]]; and *al-Rashad* with two *fathas* means uprightness in religion. Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman recited *al-Rashad* with an *alif*, which is a verbal noun like *al-ʿafaf* and *al-salah*.

﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ — heedless, amused, inattentive, not reflecting upon them nor taking admonition from them. ﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾ — and the vision of the Resurrection; it was also said: the high station in the Hereafter — ﴿their deeds have become void. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ — meaning in the Hereafter, the recompense for what they used to do in the world.

And the people of Musa (Moses) took, after him, that is, after his departure to the mountain, a calf from their ornaments, which they had borrowed from the people of Pharaoh.

The Children of Israel had been among the Copts in the position of the protected people (ahl al-jizya) in Islam. They had a day of festivity on which they would adorn themselves, and they would borrow ornaments from the Copts for it. That festival coincided with the time when they had to return the ornaments to the Copts. When God brought them out of Egypt and drowned Pharaoh, those ornaments remained in their hands. Then the Samiri (al-Samiri) made from them a calf ('ijl), which is a young cow, a body (jasadan), an embodied form with no spirit in it.

Wahb said: "jasadan" means flesh and blood. "Lahu khuwar" means it had a lowing, and khuwar is the sound of a cow, which lows once and then does not repeat it.

Wahb also said: they would hear the lowing from it, but it did not move.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, recited it as "jiwar" with a jim and a hamza, and that also means the sound.

The readers differed over His words "ḥulliyyihim." Ya'qub read it with a fatha on the ha', a sukun on the lam, and a light ya' (ḥalyihim, in the singular). Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "ḥilliyyihim" with a kasra on the ha' and a shadda on the ya'. The rest read it with a damma on the ha'. These are two dialects, like "ṣalā," "juthā," and "bakā," and in such forms both kasra and damma are permitted.

"Did they not see" refers to those who worshipped the calf instead of God, "that it does not speak to them and does not guide them to a way?" God said: They took it, that is, worshipped it, and took it as a god. "And they were wrongdoers," that is, disbelievers.

"And when they regretted (sut fi aydihim)," that is, they repented of worshipping the calf. This is one of the most eloquent expressions of the Qur'an.

The Arabs say of everyone who regrets or is unable to do something: "suqita fi yadihi" and "usqita," and they are two dialects. Its origin is from al-istis'ar, which is when a man strikes another man or throws him down, so that he casts him from his hands to the ground in order to subdue him and bind him; the one thrown is "maswut fi yad," and the one who falls is "saqit" [Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/84].

"And they saw that they had gone astray, they said: If our Lord does not have mercy on us, and forgive us, He will turn to us in repentance and pardon us and overlook us, we will certainly be among the losers," through the punishment.

"And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved," Abu al-Darda' said: "Grief (asaf) is a station beyond anger, more severe than it." Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "He returned sorrowful over the action of his people" [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/286]. al-Hasan ibn Ghadban said: "Sorrowful."

He said: "Evil is what you have done as my successors after me," that is, evil is the deed you committed after my departure. It is said: "khalafahu bi-khayr aw sharr" when one speaks to him, regarding his family or people, after one has left them, of good or evil.

"Did you hasten the command of your Lord?" meaning, did you outrun it?

"And he threw down the tablets," in anger at his people when they worshipped the calf. Qatadah said: He threw them only when he heard of the virtues of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). In the Tablets he said: "O Lord, make me of the community of Muhammad."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on my brother Musa. The one who is told is not like the one who sees. Allah had informed him of his people's trial, so he knew that what Allah had told him was true, and that he was holding firmly to what was in his hands. Then he returned to his people, saw them, became angry, and threw down the tablets." [Tarikh Baghdad: 3/418].

The narrators said: The Torah was in seven parts. When he threw the tablets they broke, six parts fell out and one part remained. In what fell was the writing of Musa, and in what remained was guidance and mercy.

"And he seized his brother by the head," that is, his beard and chin, "dragging him towards himself." Harun was three years older than Musa and was more beloved to the Children of Israel than Musa, because he was gentle in anger.

Harun said at that moment: "O son of my mother" (ya ibna umma). The people of Kufa read the mim with a kasra here and in Ta-Ha. He meant "ya ibn ummi," so he dropped the ya' of possession, since the vocative is built on deletion, and kept the kasra on the mim to indicate the possession, like His saying "ya 'ibad" which indicates it. The reading of Ibn al-Sumayfa'": "ya ibna ummi," with the ya' kept according to the original form. The rest read it with a fatha on the mim, and both are with the meaning "ya ibna ummah," the two words being made as one noun and built on fatha, like the expressions "ḥaḍramawt" and "khamsata 'ashar" and similar. [See al-Qurtubi's Tafsir, where this is explained in detail: 7/291.]

"Indeed the people have oppressed me," through their worship of the calf, "and they nearly killed me," meaning they intended and came close to it. "So do not let the enemies gloat over me," with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the mim, and the enemies in the accusative, is the reading of the common readers. Malik ibn Dinar read: "fa-la tashmat bi al-a'da'" with a fatha on the ta' and the mim, and al-a'da' in the nominative. "And do not place me among the wrongdoing people," that is, the people of the calf.

Musa said, when the excuse of his brother became clear to him: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us both into Your mercy, and You are the most merciful of the merciful."

"Indeed those who took the calf will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord in the Hereafter, and humiliation in the life of this world."

Abu al-'Aliyah said: It is what they were commanded, namely killing themselves.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said: He meant that their children, the grown ones, who were adults in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would be overtaken by wrath... "and humiliation in the life of this world," and that is what befell Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir of killing and exile for their having sided with the worshippers of the calf and approved of it. Ibn Abbas said: it is the jizya.

"Thus do We recompense the fabricators," the liars. Abu Qilabah said: "By Allah, it is the recompense of every fabricator until the Day of Resurrection. He will be humiliated by Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

I heard Abu 'Amr al-Furati, who heard Abu Sa'id Bakr ibn Abi 'Uthman al-Khayri, who heard al-Siraj, who heard Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ghazzi, who heard his father say: Malik ibn Anas said: "There is no innovator except that humiliation is found above his head," then he recited, "Indeed those who took the calf..." meaning the innovators.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on Surah 7, verses 153–156:

﴿Those who committed evil deeds and then repented﴾ up to His words ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses﴾. That is, it subsided from Moses. Evidence for this is the reading of Mu'awiya ibn Mughira: "wa lamma sakana" (وَلَمَّا سَكَنَ), with a nun.

Abu al-Najm said:

*The viper was about to slither,*
*and the whistling bird fell silent from crying out.*

The root meaning of *sakt* is refraining from something, and from it comes *al-sakit* (the one who is silent from speech).

﴿And when he took up the Tablets, in whose inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord﴾: he took up the Tablets that he had thrown down, and six-sevenths of them had been lost. "And in their inscription" means what was copied from them, that is, what remained of them.

Ata' said: this means what remained of them, and nothing of the legal limits or the rulings was lost. Ibn Abbas and Amr ibn Dinar said: Moses fasted forty days. When he threw down the Tablets and they shattered, he fasted the same number of days, and they were returned to him and rewritten for him on two tablets in place of the broken ones, without losing anything from them. ﴿Guidance and mercy﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿guidance﴾ from error, and ﴿mercy﴾ from punishment, ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾ [who are cautious]. The rajaz poet said:

*The hollow of the pitch... they make it, or they seek it,*
*water gurgling in its hollows.*

That is, from the source of the *jaza'*.

﴿And Moses chose from his people﴾, that is, from among his people. When the preposition is dropped, the noun is put in the accusative, as in the verse of al-Farazdaq:

*Among us is the one chosen among men for generosity,*
*and for piety when the stormy winds blow.*

Another poet said:

*I have chosen you for the people when their characters have decayed,*
*and the one from whom hope was sought has become weak.*

That is, from among the people. They differed about the reason for Moses' choosing the seventy.

Al-Suddi said: God commanded that He would come to Moses with some men of the Children of Israel who would apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, and He promised an appointment. Moses chose from his people ﴿seventy men﴾, then went with them to apologize. When they reached that place they said: ﴿We will not believe you until we see God openly﴾, and since you have spoken to Him, show Him to us. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them and they died﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: he chose them so that they might repent to Him for what they had done and ask Him to forgive those they had left behind among their people.

Mujahid said: he chose them for the completion of the appointment.

Wahb said: the Children of Israel said to Moses (peace be upon him): "Some people claim that God does not speak to you, and that if He did speak to you, you would have stood for His speech. Did you not see that some of us asked Him to see Him and died? So do not ask Him to make a group of us [descend] until He speaks to you and they hear His speech and believe, and the suspicion is removed." God revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): choose seventy men from their best, then ascend with them to the mountain, you and Aaron. He appointed Joshua son of Nun as his successor over the Children of Israel. He speaks as God commanded: ﴿And Moses chose seventy men﴾.

Al-Minhal reported from al-Rabi' ibn Habib, who said: We heard Abu Sa'id al-Raqashi, and he recited this verse, and said: The seventy were young men, except for twenty, and none of them had exceeded forty. That is because a man of twenty has lost his beauty and youth, and whoever has not exceeded forty has nothing left of his intellect. Others said: they were elders.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿Moses chose seventy men﴾ to go up to the mountain, but only sixty elders were found. God revealed to him that he should choose ten of the young men, and he chose them, and they became elders. So he chose six men from each tribe, and they became seventy-two.

Moses said: "I was only commanded to take seventy men," so he appointed two of you as deputies, and they disputed about that. He said: "Whoever remains seated has the same reward as the one who went out." So two men remained seated, one of them Kaleb ibn Yuqiya and the other Joshua ibn Nun.

Moses commanded the seventy to fast and purify themselves, and to purify their garments. Then he took them out to Mount Sinai for the appointment with his Lord. He would not come to Him except by His permission. This is His saying, ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. Then, when the earthquake seized them﴾. The commentators differed about the manner of this earthquake and the cause of its seizing them.

Ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi said: when they reached that place they said to Moses: "Ask for us, so that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." Atiyya al-'Awfi said: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, but it is answered only for those who are God-fearing. That is because the disbeliever is provided for and protected through the believer, owing to the vastness of God's mercy toward the believer, in which he lives. When he goes to the Hereafter, it becomes specifically for the believers, like one who sees by the light of another's fire when the owner of the lamp takes his lamp away.

Abu Rawq said: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, meaning the mercy which He has distributed among the creatures, by which some of them incline toward others. Ibn Zayd said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ is repentance. Others said: its wording is general but its meaning is specific to this community.

Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ibn Jarir and Abu Bakr al-Hudhali said: when this verse was revealed, ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾, Iblis said: "I am part of that thing." God withdrew it from Iblis, and said: ﴿So I will ordain it for those who are God-fearing and pay the zakat, and those who believe in Our signs﴾. Then the Jews and Christians said: "We are God-fearing, we pay the zakat, and we believe in the signs of our Lord." So God withdrew it from them and made it for this community.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on Surah 7, verses 153–156:

﴿Those who committed evil deeds and then repented﴾ up to His words ﴿And when the anger subsided from Moses﴾. That is, it subsided from Moses. Evidence for this is the reading of Mu'awiya ibn Mughira: "wa lamma sakana" (وَلَمَّا سَكَنَ), with a nun.

Abu al-Najm said:

*The viper was about to slither,*
*and the whistling bird fell silent from crying out.*

The root meaning of *sakt* is refraining from something, and from it comes *al-sakit* (the one who is silent from speech).

﴿And when he took up the Tablets, in whose inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord﴾: he took up the Tablets that he had thrown down, and six-sevenths of them had been lost. "And in their inscription" means what was copied from them, that is, what remained of them.

Ata' said: this means what remained of them, and nothing of the legal limits or the rulings was lost. Ibn Abbas and Amr ibn Dinar said: Moses fasted forty days. When he threw down the Tablets and they shattered, he fasted the same number of days, and they were returned to him and rewritten for him on two tablets in place of the broken ones, without losing anything from them. ﴿Guidance and mercy﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿guidance﴾ from error, and ﴿mercy﴾ from punishment, ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾ [who are cautious]. The rajaz poet said:

*The hollow of the pitch... they make it, or they seek it,*
*water gurgling in its hollows.*

That is, from the source of the *jaza'*.

﴿And Moses chose from his people﴾, that is, from among his people. When the preposition is dropped, the noun is put in the accusative, as in the verse of al-Farazdaq:

*Among us is the one chosen among men for generosity,*
*and for piety when the stormy winds blow.*

Another poet said:

*I have chosen you for the people when their characters have decayed,*
*and the one from whom hope was sought has become weak.*

That is, from among the people. They differed about the reason for Moses' choosing the seventy.

Al-Suddi said: God commanded that He would come to Moses with some men of the Children of Israel who would apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, and He promised an appointment. Moses chose from his people ﴿seventy men﴾, then went with them to apologize. When they reached that place they said: ﴿We will not believe you until we see God openly﴾, and since you have spoken to Him, show Him to us. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them and they died﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: he chose them so that they might repent to Him for what they had done and ask Him to forgive those they had left behind among their people.

Mujahid said: he chose them for the completion of the appointment.

Wahb said: the Children of Israel said to Moses (peace be upon him): "Some people claim that God does not speak to you, and that if He did speak to you, you would have stood for His speech. Did you not see that some of us asked Him to see Him and died? So do not ask Him to make a group of us [descend] until He speaks to you and they hear His speech and believe, and the suspicion is removed." God revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): choose seventy men from their best, then ascend with them to the mountain, you and Aaron. He appointed Joshua son of Nun as his successor over the Children of Israel. He speaks as God commanded: ﴿And Moses chose seventy men﴾.

Al-Minhal reported from al-Rabi' ibn Habib, who said: We heard Abu Sa'id al-Raqashi, and he recited this verse, and said: The seventy were young men, except for twenty, and none of them had exceeded forty. That is because a man of twenty has lost his beauty and youth, and whoever has not exceeded forty has nothing left of his intellect. Others said: they were elders.

Al-Kalbi said: ﴿Moses chose seventy men﴾ to go up to the mountain, but only sixty elders were found. God revealed to him that he should choose ten of the young men, and he chose them, and they became elders. So he chose six men from each tribe, and they became seventy-two.

Moses said: "I was only commanded to take seventy men," so he appointed two of you as deputies, and they disputed about that. He said: "Whoever remains seated has the same reward as the one who went out." So two men remained seated, one of them Kaleb ibn Yuqiya and the other Joshua ibn Nun.

Moses commanded the seventy to fast and purify themselves, and to purify their garments. Then he took them out to Mount Sinai for the appointment with his Lord. He would not come to Him except by His permission. This is His saying, ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. Then, when the earthquake seized them﴾. The commentators differed about the manner of this earthquake and the cause of its seizing them.

Ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi said: when they reached that place they said to Moses: "Ask for us, so that we may hear the speech of our Lord." He said: "I will do so." When Moses drew near the mountain, a column of cloud descended upon it and covered the whole mountain. Moses approached and entered it and said to the people: "Draw near." Whenever his Lord spoke to him, a bright light would fall upon his forehead, so that none of the Children of Israel could look at it. A veil was placed between him and them. The people drew near until they entered the cloud, which was a pillar, and they heard Him speaking to Moses, commanding him in it: "Do this, do not do that." When He finished, the cloud withdrew from Moses, and he came to them. They said: "O Moses, ﴿we will not believe you until we see God openly﴾." Then ﴿the thunderbolt seized them and they all died﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: the seventy who said ﴿We will not believe you until we see God openly﴾ and whom ﴿the thunderbolt seized﴾ were before the seventy whom ﴿the earthquake seized﴾. God commanded Moses to choose seventy men from his people, and he chose them and brought them out to supplicate their Lord. Among what they supplicated was: "O God, give us what You have given no one before us, and do not give it to anyone after us." God disliked this supplication of theirs, so ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, said: ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾ only because of their claim against Moses, before Aaron. That is because Moses, Aaron, Shabbar and Shabbir (peace be upon them) set out to the foot of a mountain. Aaron slept on a bed, and God took his soul. When he died, Moses buried him. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said to him: "Where is Aaron?" He said: "God took his soul." They said: "Rather, you killed him, out of envy for his gentleness and his character." He said: "Choose whom you wish." They chose seventy men, and he took them away. When they reached the grave, Moses said: "O Aaron, were you killed, or did you die?" Aaron said: "No one killed me, but God took me to Himself." They said: "O Moses, you will never tell this story again." ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, and they were struck and died. Moses said: "O Lord, what shall I say to the Children of Israel when I return to them? They will say, 'You killed them.'" So God revived them and made them all prophets.

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾ only because they did not approve of the calf, and did not forbid it. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾ because they did not separate themselves from their people when they worshipped the calf, and did not enjoin the good nor forbid the evil.

Wahb said: that earthquake was not death, but when the people saw that awe, ﴿the earthquake seized them﴾ and they fell down, and they trembled until their joints nearly came apart and their backs nearly broke. When Moses (peace be upon him) saw this, he had mercy on them and feared for them death, and their loss weighed heavily on him, for they had been to him like children in goodness, listening and obedient. At that point he supplicated, wept, and pleaded with his Lord. God removed from them that earthquake and trembling, so they calmed and were at peace, and they heard the speech of their Lord. This is His saying: ﴿He said﴾, that is, Moses: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me﴾, by the killing of the Copt. ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾, that is, the worshippers of the calf. Moses thought that they had been punished for the Children of Israel's taking of the calf.

Al-Suddi said: God revealed to Moses that these seventy were among those who had taken the calf, and Moses did not know this. So Moses said: "O Lord, how shall I return to the Children of Israel, when You have destroyed their best, and I have not a single man with me? What will they accept from me, and entrust to me, after this?" So God revived them.

Al-Mubarrad said: His saying ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾ is a request for information and a plea for compassion, meaning: do not destroy us. Moses knew that God is too just to punish one person for the crime of another, but it is like the saying of Jesus: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants﴾, the verse [Qur'an 5:118].

﴿It is only Your trial﴾, that is, Your testing.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Rabi' said: Your ordeal. Ibn Abbas said: Your punishment, by which You afflict whom You will and turn it away from whom You will. ﴿You send astray thereby whom You will, and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers. And ordain for us﴾, that is, ensure, [and grant us success in righteous deeds]. It is said: God has ordained safety for you. ﴿In this world, good, and in the Hereafter﴾, that is, righteous deeds in this world, and forgiveness and Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾. Abu Ruzza al-Sa'di, who was a reliable reciter and a poet, recited "hidna" with a kasra on the ha'. It is said: "hada yahidu and yahudu," when one returns and moves [then the inclination guides him]. A poet said:

*Salma has known a man, that I among people am one who turns to her.*

God said: ﴿My punishment: I afflict with it whom I will﴾ from My creation. Al-Hasan and Ibn al-Sumayqa recited "man ashā'" with the verb from *al-ishā'a* (causing to be struck). ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, that is, it has generalized to everything. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: His mercy in this world encompasses the righteous and the wicked, but on the Day of Resurrection it is specifically for the God-fearing.

Atiyya al-'Awfi said: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, but it is answered only for those who are God-fearing. That is because the disbeliever is provided for and protected through the believer, owing to the vastness of God's mercy toward the believer, in which he lives. When he goes to the Hereafter, it becomes specifically for the believers, like one who sees by the light of another's fire when the owner of the lamp takes his lamp away.

Abu Rawq said: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾, meaning the mercy which He has distributed among the creatures, by which some of them incline toward others. Ibn Zayd said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾ is repentance. Others said: its wording is general but its meaning is specific to this community.

Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ibn Jarir and Abu Bakr al-Hudhali said: when this verse was revealed, ﴿My mercy encompasses all things﴾, Iblis said: "I am part of that thing." God withdrew it from Iblis, and said: ﴿So I will ordain it for those who are God-fearing and pay the zakat, and those who believe in Our signs﴾. Then the Jews and Christians said: "We are God-fearing, we pay the zakat, and we believe in the signs of our Lord." So God withdrew it from them and made it for this community.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 157–159:

﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ﴾ [the verse, to the end]. Nawf al-Bakali al-Himyari said: When Musa (Moses) chose seventy men from his people for the appointed time with his Lord, Allah the Exalted said to Musa: "I will make for you the earth a place of prayer (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur), so that you may pray wherever the prayer reaches you, except at a latrine, a bath, or a grave. And I will place tranquillity (sakinah) in your hearts, and I will make you recite the Torah from the backs of your hearts. Every one of you will recite it, man and woman, free and slave, young and old."

Musa told his people this, and they said: "We do not want to pray in churches. We cannot bear the tranquillity in our hearts. We want it to be as it was in the ark (tabut). We cannot recite the Torah from the backs of our hearts, and we do not want to recite it except by looking at it." Then Allah said: ﴿فَسَأَكْتُبُها لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ [So I will prescribe it for those who fear Me], up to His words ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [the successful]. So Allah gave it to this community (umma). Musa said: "My Lord, make me their prophet." He said: "Their prophet is from among them." He said: "My Lord, make me one of them." He said: "You will not reach them." Musa said: "O my Lord, I came to You with a delegation of the Children of Israel, and You made our delegation for others." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿وَمِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسَى أُمَّةٌ يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ [And among the people of Musa is a community that guides by the truth and by it acts justly], and Musa was content. Nawf said: "Will you not praise your Lord, who preserved your errors (ghayy), gave you your share generously, and made the Children of Israel's delegation yours?" [Its completion is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/112, with slight variation.]

The scholars differed about the meaning of al-ummi (the unlettered).

Ibn 'Abbas said: it means one of you who was unlettered, who could not write, read or calculate. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ تَتْلُوا مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مِنْ كِتابٍ وَلا تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ﴾ [You did not recite any scripture before it, nor did you write it with your right hand]. [Al-'Ankabut: 48.]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We are an unlettered community: we do not write and we do not calculate." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/43, no. 129, where it reads "nahsub" (we do not reckon).]

It was said: it is a nisba (relative adjective) to his umma, as if the original was ummati, and the taa' was dropped in the nisba, as it was dropped in "al-yaki" and "al-mada."

It was said: it is a nisba to Umm al-Qura, which is Makkah. ﴿الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ﴾ [whom they find], i.e., his description, his prophethood, his attributes and his matter, ﴿مَكْتُوباً عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ﴾ [written with them in the Torah and the Gospel].

'Ata' ibn Yasar said: I met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and said: "Tell me about the description of the Messenger of Allah in the Torah." He said: "Yes, by Allah, he is described in the Torah as he is described in the Qur'an: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِنَّا أَرْسَلْناكَ شاهِداً وَمُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً وَحِرْزاً لِلْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ [O Prophet, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, a warner, and a safeguard for the unlettered]. You are My servant and My messenger; I have named you al-Mutawakkil (the one who relies upon Allah). He is not harsh, nor coarse, nor clamorous (sakhkhab) in the markets (in some sources: sakhab), and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. I will not take him until he sets straight the crooked religion, by people saying: 'There is no god but Allah,' and by it opening hearts that are sealed, ears that are deaf, and eyes that are blind."" [Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/21; Dala'il al-Nubuwwa of Abu Nu'aym: 151.]

'Ata' said: Then he met Ka'b and asked him about this. They did not differ in a single letter, except that Ka'b said: "[It reads as] ghulufiyyan (sealed) hearts, sumumiyyan (deaf) ears, and 'umumiyyan (blind) eyes." [The addition is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/113.]

Ka'b also related about the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said: "His birth is in Makkah, his migration is to Taba (Madinah), and his kingdom is in al-Sham (Syria). His community are the praisers (al-hammadun), who praise Allah in every condition and every station. They wash their limbs (for ablution) and purify themselves for jihad. Among them are those who watch the sun (for times of prayer), and they pray the prayer wherever it reaches them, even upon the dung-heap. Their description in speech is like their description in prayer." Then he recited: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِهِ صَفًّا﴾ [Those who fight in His cause in ranks]. [Surah al-Saff: 4.]

al-Waqidi said: 'Uthman ibn al-Dahhak related to me, from Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from Tha'laba ibn Malik, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he asked Abu Malik, who was one of the Jewish scholars, about the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Torah. He said:

"His description is in the book of the sons of Harun, which no one among the descendants of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim has changed or altered, and he is among the last of the prophets. He is the Arab prophet who comes with the religion of Ibrahim, the upright (hanif). He wears his waist-wrap (izar) on his middle, and he washes his extremities, and in his eyes there is redness, and between his shoulders is the seal of prophethood, like the button of a bridal canopy (hajlah). He is neither short nor tall. He wears the shamla (a cloak), rides a donkey, and walks in the markets. With him are war, killing and captivity; his sword is on his shoulder, and he does not care whom he meets among people. With him is a prayer which, if it had been among the people of Nuh, they would not have been destroyed by the flood; if it had been among 'Ad, they would not have been destroyed by the wind; and if it had been among Thamud, they would not have been destroyed by the cry."

"His birth is in Makkah, his upbringing is there, the beginning of his prophethood is there, and the abode of his migration is Yathrib, between a stone-hill (jarrah) and palm trees and a salt-flat (sabkha). He is unlettered and does not write with his hand. He is one of jihad; he praises Allah in every hardship and every ease. His dominion is al-Sham. His companion among the angels is Jibril. He suffers severe harm from his people, and they love him intensely. Then he will prevail over his people and besiege them with a siege like that of the threshing floor (al-jarin). He will have engagements in Yathrib, some in his favour and some against him, and then the final outcome will be his. With him will be people who hasten to death faster than water from the top of a mountain to its base. Their hearts are their Gospel, their sacrifice is their blood, they are lions by day and monks by night. His enemy is terrified of him from a month's distance. He personally engages in fighting until he goes out and speaks, with no police (shurta) or guards protecting him." [See the description of the Prophet and his community in Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/134.]

﴿يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ [He commands them to do what is good], i.e., with faith, ﴿وَيَنْهاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ﴾ [and forbids them from what is wrong], meaning polytheism (shirk). It was said: al-ma'ruf is the Law (shari'a) and the Sunna, and al-munkar is what is not known in the Law or the Sunna.

'Ata' said: ﴿يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ [He commands them to do what is good] means to renounce rivals (andad) and to practise noble character and maintaining ties of kinship. ﴿يَنْهاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ﴾ [He forbids them from what is wrong] means worshipping idols and severing ties of kinship. ﴿وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّباتِ﴾ [He makes lawful for them the good things] means the lawful things that the people of jahiliyya (pre-Islamic ignorance) had forbidden: the bahira, the sa'iba, the wasila and the hami. ﴿وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبائِثَ﴾ [and forbids them the foul things] means pork, blood, carrion, usury and other prohibitions. ﴿وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ﴾ [and relieves them of their burden]: Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Mujahid said: it means the hardship imposed upon the Children of Israel by acting on what is in the Torah. Ibn Zayd and Qatada said: it means the hardships that were upon them in religion. ﴿وَالْأَغْلالَ الَّتِي كانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [and the shackles that were upon them] means the burdens that they were commanded to carry out in the Torah, such as killing oneself and cutting off the (sinful) parts of the body; it is likened to shackles, as the poet said:

"There is no longer any trace of the abode's pledge, O Umm Malik,
but the chains have encircled the necks."

"The youth has become like the elderly man who speaks nothing
but justice, and the blamers have rested."

So the limits of Islam and its prohibitions that prevent one from crossing into forbidden matters are likened to chains encircling the necks. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/466; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/301.]

﴿فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ﴾ [So those who believed in him and honoured him], i.e., helped him and revered him, ﴿وَنَصَرُوهُ﴾ [and supported him], ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾ [and followed the light that was sent down with him], meaning the Qur'an, ﴿أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [those are the successful]. ﴿قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾ [Say: O people, I am the messenger of Allah to all of you], ﴿الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth], up to His words, Exalted is He: ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَكَلِماتِهِ﴾ [in Allah and His words].

Qatada said: "and His signs (ayatihi)." Miqatil and al-Suddi said: it means 'Isa ibn Maryam. ﴿وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ [Follow him that you may be guided].

﴿وَمِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسَى﴾ [And among the people of Musa] means the Children of Israel. ﴿أُمَّةٌ﴾ [a community] means a group. ﴿يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [who guide by the truth], i.e., who direct to the truth. It was said: they are successors (khulafa'), who are guided and remain upright upon it, and act by it. ﴿وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ [and by it act justly], i.e., they are fair towards themselves and are praised.

al-Suddi said: They are a people between you and them ... from Sahl [the text is unclear here].

Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached me that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disavowed what they had done, made excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel in the earth, and they travelled through it for a year and a half until they emerged from behind China. They are there, truly Muslims, facing our qibla.

al-Kalbi, al-Rabi' and al-Dahhak and 'Ata' said: They are a people in the far west, behind China, on a river of sand called the river of Awdaq. None of them has more wealth than another. They receive rain at night and wake to daylight; they cultivate, and none of us reaches them nor any of them reaches us. They are upon the truth.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Jibril went to them on the night of the Isra' (night journey), and spoke to them. Jibril said to them: "Do you know whom you are speaking to?"

They said: "No."

He said: "This is Muhammad, the Prophet. Believe in him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Musa instructed us that whoever among you reaches Ahmad, let him convey my greeting to him."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned the greeting to Musa: "And upon him be peace." Then he recited to them ten surahs of the Qur'an that were revealed in Makkah, and no obligation had yet been revealed except the prayer and zakat. So he commanded them to pray and to give zakat, and commanded them to establish worship where they were. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ﴾ [So those who believed in him and honoured him], i.e., helped him and revered him, ﴿وَنَصَرُوهُ﴾ [and supported him], ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ﴾ [and followed the light that was sent down with him], meaning the Qur'an, ﴿أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [those are the successful]. ﴿قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾ [Say: O people, I am the messenger of Allah to all of you], ﴿الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ [to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth], up to His words, Exalted is He: ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَكَلِماتِهِ﴾ [in Allah and His words].

Qatada said: "and His signs (ayatihi)." Miqatil and al-Suddi said: it means 'Isa ibn Maryam. ﴿وَاتَّبِعُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ [Follow him that you may be guided].

﴿وَمِنْ قَوْمِ مُوسَى﴾ [And among the people of Musa] means the Children of Israel. ﴿أُمَّةٌ﴾ [a community] means a group. ﴿يَهْدُونَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [who guide by the truth], i.e., who direct to the truth. It was said: they are successors (khulafa'), who are guided and remain upright upon it, and act by it. ﴿وَبِهِ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ [and by it act justly], i.e., they are fair towards themselves and are praised.

al-Suddi said: They are a people between you and them ... from Sahl [the text is unclear here].

Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached me that when the Children of Israel killed their prophets and disbelieved, and they were twelve tribes (asbat), one tribe disavowed what they had done, made excuse, and asked Allah to separate them from them. So Allah opened for them a tunnel in the earth, and they travelled through it for a year and a half until they emerged from behind China. They are there, truly Muslims, facing our qibla.

al-Kalbi, al-Rabi' and al-Dahhak and 'Ata' said: They are a people in the far west, behind China, on a river of sand called the river of Awdaq. None of them has more wealth than another. They receive rain at night and wake to daylight; they cultivate, and none of us reaches them nor any of them reaches us. They are upon the truth.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Jibril went to them on the night of the Isra' (night journey), and spoke to them. Jibril said to them: "Do you know whom you are speaking to?"

They said: "No."

He said: "This is Muhammad, the Prophet. Believe in him." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Musa instructed us that whoever among you reaches Ahmad, let him convey my greeting to him."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned the greeting to Musa: "And upon him be peace." Then he recited to them ten surahs of the Qur'an that were revealed in Makkah, and no obligation had yet been revealed except the prayer and zakat. So he commanded them to pray and to give zakat, and commanded them to establish worship where they were. They used to observe the Sabbath, so he commanded them to gather together and to abandon the Sabbath.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 7, verses 160–162:

﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes, as nations﴾, meaning the Children of Israel. Abān ibn Yazīd al-ʿAṭṭār reported from ʿĀṣim that he read *waqaṭṭaʿnāhum* with the letter *ṭāʾ* lightened (*wa-qaṭaʿnāhum*), and he meant by *asbāṭ* (tribes, sing. *sibṭ*) the clans and divisions. For this reason the number is given in the form it takes, since *asbāṭ* is a masculine plural.

The poet said:

"Indeed Quraysh, all of it, are ten bellies (sub-clans),
and you are innocent of its ten clans."

[In al-Ṭabarī's *Jāmiʿ al-Bayān* 9/119 and *Lisān al-ʿArab* 1/722, the line reads: "Indeed Kullāb, these are ten bellies."]

He used *baṭn* (belly, sub-clan) to mean a clan and a division, which is why *al-baṭn* is masculine. He said *asbāṭan umamā* in the plural, and one does not say *atānī ithnā ʿashara rajulan* ("twelve men came to me"), because he intended the numbers and the collective nouns, and so he placed each number in the position of a single unit. It was also said that the meaning is: "We divided them into tribes, as nations, twelve."

﴿And We revealed to Mūsā (Moses), when his people asked him for water, "Strike the rock with your staff."﴾ ʿAṭāʾ said: The rock had four faces, and each face had three eyes; each tribe had its own eye, which no other tribe shared. ﴿So there gushed forth﴾, that is, flowed abundantly and burst out.

The people of *tafsīr* (Qur'anic exegesis) said: *inbajasat* and *infajarat* have the same meaning. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, however, distinguished between them, saying: *inbajasat* means "it became known," and *infajarat* means "it flowed" [and ran].

ʿAṭāʾ said: On every spot of the rock that Mūsā (peace be upon him) struck there appeared something like a woman's breast, which first sweated and then flowed. ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾, from each tribe, and no tribe encroached on another's share of water. Each tribe came from one father.

﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾ in the wilderness, to shield them from the sun, ﴿and We sent down upon them manna and quails﴾, up to His words: ﴿"Your sins will be forgiven for you"﴾.

The people of Madīna read *yughfar* with a *yāʾ* and a *ḍamma*, and *khaṭāyākum* in the nominative. Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a *tāʾ* and a *ḍamma* (*tughfar*).
