On that day they all acknowledged it, some willingly and obediently, and some under compulsion, out of taqiyyah (fear). They thereby took their pledges, and their terms of life, their provisions and their accounts were determined. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I wished to be thanked." [See Tarikh Dimashq: 7/398.]

They said: Among them, on that day, were the prophets, like lamps. Adam saw a shining light and said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is Dawud, a prophet from your descendants." He said: "How old is he?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "My Lord, increase him."

He said: The pen had run with the terms of the children of Adam. He said: "My Lord, increase him by forty years from my life." So forty years were recorded for Dawud, and Adam's life was a thousand years. When Adam completed nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came, and when Adam saw him he said: "What is it with you?" He said: "You have completed your term." Adam said to him: "Forty years remain of my life." He said: "Did you not grant them to Dawud?" He said: "No," and Adam denied it. So his descendants denied it, and Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot, and he erred, so his descendants erred. The angel returned to his Lord and said: "Adam claims that forty years of his life remain." He said: "Inform Adam that he granted them to his son Dawud." The pens were slow, so they recorded them for Dawud.

When He had made them confess His Oneness and had preferred some of them over others, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not be established until every one whose pledge was taken is born, and nothing will be added to them or taken from them. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾. The construction of the verse (nazm al-ayah) is: "And when your Lord took from the backs of the Children of Adam their descendants." The matter of Adam is not mentioned, because they were brought out on the Day of the Covenant from his back. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam, some from the backs of others, in the way children are born from their fathers. So He dispensed with mentioning the back of Adam by saying "from the Children of Adam." When it became known that they were all his sons and had come out from his back, the mention of Adam's back was dropped and the mention of the backs of his sons was retained.

As for His words, ﴿their descendants﴾: the people of Makkah and Kufah read ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ without an alif, as a singular, while the rest read it in the plural with an alif. ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves﴾, and said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, a question for confirmation. ﴿They said: "Yes, we bear witness."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr read ﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ with the ya' (يقولوا), while the rest read it with the ta' (تقولوا), as in His saying ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾.

They differed about His words ﴿We bear witness﴾. Al-Suddi said: It is an announcement from Allah, speaking of Himself and of His angels, that they bore witness to the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam. Others said: Rather, it is about the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam, when some of them were made to bear witness against others, lest they say ﴿on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾, meaning, lest they should not say it. ﴿Or [lest] you say: "Our fathers only associated [others with Allah] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾, meaning the polytheists. We only followed them, and we were heedless of the Oneness. ﴿Thus We detail the verses﴾, O Muhammad, to your people, ﴿so that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾. They differed about him.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: He is Bal'am ibn Abirah. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ura. Mujahid said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ir. Muqatil said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ur ibn Mathh ibn Lut. 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas: He is from the Children of Israel.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: He was from the Canaanites, from the city of the giants. Muqatil said: He was from the city of Balqa', and it was named Balqa' because its king was a man called Baliq. His testament, as related by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi and others, was this: When Musa (ﷺ) intended to fight the giants and settled in the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of al-Sham, the people of Bal'am came to Bal'am, and he had the Greatest Name of Allah.

They said: "Musa is a fierce man, and he has large armies, and he has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us and give them to the Children of Israel. We are your people and your cousins, and we have no say. You are a man whose supplication is answered. Go out and ask Allah, Exalted is He, to turn Musa and his people away from us." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah has with him the angels and the believers. How can I curse them, when I know what I know from Allah? If I do this, my worldly life and my hereafter are lost." They said: "We have no [other] recourse," and they kept urging him about it. He said: "Until I consult my Lord." He would not supplicate until he saw in a dream what he was commanded, and he would be commanded to curse them.

In a dream it was said to him: "Do not curse them." He said to his people: "I have consulted my Lord about cursing them, and I have been forbidden." They gave him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: "Curse them!" He said: "Until I am commanded." When he was commanded, nothing came to him. He said: "I was commanded, but nothing came to me." They said: "If your Lord disliked your cursing them, He would have forbidden you as He did the first time." They kept at him, soothing him and pleading with him, until they seduced him, and he was seduced. He mounted his she-ass and set out toward a mountain overlooking the army of the Children of Israel, called Jasban.

When she had gone but a short distance, she lay down with him, so he dismounted and beat her until she was made to stand. He mounted her again, and she did not go far before she lay down, so he did the same to her, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far before she lay down, so he beat her until she was made to suffer, and then Allah gave her permission to speak, and she spoke as a proof against him. She said: "Woe to you, O Bal'am! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me from this way, so that we might go to the Prophet of Allah and to the believers whom you curse?" He did not desist, so Allah released her, and she went on until she brought him up over the mountain of Jasban. He began to curse them, but he cursed them with nothing without his tongue being turned toward his own people, and he prayed for his people for no good without his request being turned to the Children of Israel.

His people said to him: "Do you know what you are doing, O Bal'am? You are praying for them and cursing us." He said: "This is something I do not control; it is a matter in which Allah has prevailed." His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest, and he said to them: "Now this world and the hereafter are gone from me. Nothing remains but scheming and trickery. I will devise for you and contrive. Adorn your women and perfume them and give them goods, then send them to the army to mingle with them, and command them not to refuse any man who desires them, for if a single man of them commits fornication, they will be led into temptation." They did so.

When the women entered the army, a woman passed among the Canaanites, named Bashti, daughter of Sur, by a man of the notables of the Children of Israel called Zimri ibn Shalum, chief of the tribe of Shim'un ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim (ﷺ). He stood up to her and took her hand, for her beauty had tempted him. Then he came and stood before Musa and said: "I think you will say, 'This is forbidden to you.'" He said: "Indeed she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and lay with her, so Allah sent the plague (ta'un) upon the Children of Israel at once.

Fanhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, was a man who had been given physical stature and strength in grasping. He had been absent when Zimri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel and was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was made entirely of iron, and entered the tent upon them while they were lying together. He pierced them both with his spear and lifted them up toward the sky, with the spear in his arm, leaning with his elbow on his side and resting the spear against his beard.

He had been [disliking 'Izar], and he kept saying: "O Allah, this is what we do to those who disobey You." Then the plague was lifted. Those of the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the time Zimri had the woman until Fanhas killed him, were counted, and seventy thousand had perished in one hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel give the descendants of Fanhas the cheek, the foreleg and the jaw of every animal they slaughter, because he leaned on the spear with his arm and rested it against his beard; and the firstborn of all their wealth and their persons, because he was the firstborn of 'Izar ibn Harun. And concerning Bal'am, Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [At length in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/169.]

Muqatil said: The king of al-Balqa' said to Bal'am: "Curse Musa." He said: "He is of my religion; I will not curse him." So a wooden cross was set up for him to be crucified on. When he saw that, he set out on his she-ass to curse them. When he saw their army, the she-ass stood still and halted. He beat her, and she said: "Why do you beat me? I am commanded; do not wrong me. And there is a fire before me that has prevented me from walking." He returned and informed the king. The king said: "You must curse him, or I will crucify you." So he cursed Musa by the Greatest Name, that he should not enter the city, and it was answered for him. Musa and the Children of Israel fell into the wilderness (tih) because of his supplication. Musa said: "O Lord, for what sin have we fallen into the wilderness?" He said: "Because of the supplication of the scholar (al-'alim)." He said: "Just as You heard his supplication against me, hear my supplication against him." Musa prayed that He strip him of the Greatest Name and of faith. So Allah stripped him of what he had and removed knowledge from him, and it came out of his chest like a white dove. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he withdrew from them﴾ (fa-insalakha minha). Then Allah revealed this verse concerning him.

'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Rawq said: This verse was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi. His story was that at the beginning of his affair he read the books and knew that Allah would send a messenger at that time, and he hoped that he himself would be that messenger. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, he envied him. He had intended to go to some kings, but when he returned he passed by the slain of Badr and asked about them. It was said: "Muhammad killed them." He said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have killed his own kin." When Umayyah died, his sister Farida came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her about her brother's death. She said: "While he was with us, he slept on my couch, and two birds came and landed; one sat by his foot and the other by his head. The one by his foot said to the one by his head: 'Shall I strike?' He said: 'Strike.' He said: 'Shall I cut open?' He said: 'No.'" She said: "I asked him about that, and he said: 'Good, my sister.' Then they flew off from me, and he fainted. When he came round, he said:"

"Every life, however long it lasts, ends in the end of its matter / I wish I had been, before what has appeared to me, grazing the wild goats on the mountain crags."

"On the Day of Reckoning, a great day, in which the young grow old with heavy sleep."

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Recite to me your brother's poetry." She recited to him:

"To You is the praise, the bounty and the grace, our Lord, and nothing is higher than You in majesty and glory, / King over the throne of the heavens, Guardian, before whose might faces are humbled and bow down."

It was a long poem, until she came to its end. She recited to him his poem:

"The people stood for the reckoning, all of them, so the wretched one is punished and the happy one is blessed."

Then she recited to him his poem in which he says:

"Before the Lord of the Throne they are presented to Him, / He knows the open and the secret, the hidden. / The Day when the Merciful comes, and He is compassionate; / Indeed His promise is ever to be fulfilled. / The Day when there comes to him what he said, a single one, / then he will be surely guided or astray, / or happy with a happiness I hope for, / or humiliated, wretched for what he has earned. / If I am called to account for what I have committed, / I shall surely be cast into strong punishment. / And my Lord, if You pardon, then pardon is my hope, / or if You punish, You do not punish one who is innocent."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved."

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [al-Isabah: 8/261, abridged. See also the story and the verses in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 2/285.]

Some said: It was revealed concerning al-Busus.

He was a man who had been given three answered supplications. He had a wife, and he had a child by her. She said to him: "Make one of them for me." He said: "One of them is yours. What do you want?" She said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel." He prayed for her, and she became the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was none like her among them, she turned away from him, and the man was angry. He prayed against her, and she became a barking bitch. Two of the supplications were used up. Her sons came and said: "We have no peace over this. You prayed against our mother, and she became a barking bitch, and the people taunt us. Pray to Allah that He returns her to the state she was in." He prayed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and she returned as she was, and the supplications were all used up.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning Abu 'Amir ibn al-Nu'man ibn Sayfi, the monk, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) named "the Wicked" (al-Fasiq). He had been a monk in the Jahiliyyah and wore woollen garments. He came to Madinah and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is this that you have brought?" He said: "I have brought the Hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." He said: "I am the one who brought it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You are not upon it, but you have introduced Iblis into it." Abu 'Amir said: "May Allah cause the liar among us to die, a stranger, alone." He went out to al-Sham and sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare strength and weapons, and build me a mosque." Then he went to the monk, Caesar, and came with troops to expel the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions from Madinah. This is His saying: ﴿and in ambush for those who had fought against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning waiting for his coming. He died in al-Sham, a stranger, alone.

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: It was revealed concerning the Quraysh. Allah brought them the signs, but they withdrew from them and did not accept them.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites of the People of the Book, who used to recognise the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿as they recognise their own sons﴾.

'Amr ibn Dinar said: 'Ikrimah was asked about this verse, and he said: "This and that are not specific to one matter."

Qatadah said: This is a parable that Allah struck for one to whom guidance was presented but who did not accept it. This is His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: It is the Greatest Name of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: He would ask Allah for nothing without being given it.

Ibn 'Abbas, in another narration, said: It is greater in that it is a book of the books of Allah. Mujahid said: He was a prophet from the Children of Israel called Bal'am. He was given prophethood, but his people bribed him to keep silent, so he did, and left them as they were. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

﴿So he withdrew [went out] from them﴾, as the snake sheds its skin. ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he overtook him and caught up with him, ﴿and he became of the misguided.﴾ ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾, meaning We would have favoured him, honoured him and raised his station by the signs.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We would have raised him by them.

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: Meaning, We would have lifted disbelief from him through the signs and protected him.

﴿But he inclined to the earth﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He leaned toward the earth. Mujahid said: He settled. Muqatil said: He was content with the world. Abu 'Ubaydah said: He clung to it and was slow. The one who is "mukhallad" among men is one whose white hair is slow to appear, and among animals, one whose incisors remain until the molars come out. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

Al-Zajjaj said: Khalada and akhlada are one, and it is derived from khuld, which means lasting and dwelling. One says "khalada fulan bi al-maqam" when he stays in a place. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"To whom do these dwellings belong, which you have passed through in al-Gharqad, / like the writing in the hollow of the watercourse, long-lasting."

Meaning: remaining.

Malik ibn Nuwayrah said:

"Then no tidings of a tribe from the tribes of Malik / and 'Amr ibn Yarbu' who stayed and clung to the land."

[Lisan al-'Arab: 3/164.] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

﴿And followed his desire.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: He follows base affairs and abandons the lofty ones. Abu Rawq said: He chose the world over the hereafter. Ibn Zayd said: His desire was with [the ancient ones]. 'Ata' said: He wanted the world and obeyed his Satan. Yaman said: ﴿and followed his desire﴾, meaning his wife, because she drove him to betrayal.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verse 172–179 (part 2 of 2):

So his likeness is like the likeness of the dog: if you chase it, it pants; or if you leave it, it pants. Mujahid said: "It is the likeness of one who reads the Book but does not act by it." Ibn Jurayj said: "The dog is one whose heart is cut off, having no heart; if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. This is the likeness of one who abandons guidance, having no heart; rather, his heart is cut off."

Ma'mar narrated from some of them, who said: "It is the disbeliever who is astray, whether you admonish him or do not admonish him."

Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning, "if you chase it [with wisdom], it will not take it up; and if you leave it, it will not be guided to any good, like the dog: if it is lying down it pants, and if it is driven away it pants."

Al-Hasan said: "It is the hypocrite, who does not turn back to the truth, whether he is called or not called, admonished or not admonished. [Like the dog], it pants whether it is driven away or left alone." 'Ata' said: "It barks whether it is chased or not chased." Al-Qutabi said: "Every creature pants from exhaustion or thirst except the dog, for it pants in a state of fatigue and in a state of rest, in health and in sickness, in hunger and in thirst." So God struck this as a likeness for one who denies His signs.

He said: whether you admonish him, he is astray; and whether you leave him, he is astray, like the dog: if you drive it, it pants, and if you leave it, it pants. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 193]. ﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Salim [Abu al-Khadr], who said: he means the likeness of the Children of Israel, i.e., if you bring them news of what was among them, which you did not witness (﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾).

They would know that no one brings this news of the past among them except a prophet, one who is informed by heaven. ﴿Evil is the likeness﴾, i.e., "evil is the likeness" as a circumstantial clause from the implied noun (al-mathal). As Jarir said:

"How excellent is the provision of your father's provision, a provision."

This is when you make "sa'a" (evil) a verb of the likeness and take "al-qawm" (the people) as a substitute for the pronoun within it. If you transfer its verb to "the people" and make them its agent, it becomes a specification (tamyiz), meaning: "I shall liken the people," and when you transfer it to them, the likeness becomes explanatory, as one says: "qarrabahu 'aynan" and "daqa dharʿan," whenever the tanwin falls from the specified noun that is genitive by annexation. Its evidence is the recitation of al-Jahdari and al-A'mash: "sa-umaththil al-qawm" (with annexation). Abu Hatim said: they mean by it "mithl" (the likeness), i.e., "the likeness of the people," so "mithl" was omitted.

"The people" were placed in a position with "ummah," so he raised them, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾.

﴿And themselves they were wronging﴾, up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾. He said this only because of His complete knowledge concerning them, that they would arrive at it through their disbelief in their Lord. Some scholars of meanings call this the "lam of becoming" (lam al-sayrurah), as in His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 8]. And they recited:

"Our wealth we gather for the heirs of inheritance, and our houses we build for the ruin of time."

And another said:

"For death the mothers bear their young, just as houses are built for the ruin of time."

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr narrated from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this verse, he said: "Just as God, Exalted is He, created for Hell what He created, the child of fornication was among those created for Hell."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, i.e., they do not comprehend good and guidance; ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾, i.e., the path of truth and right guidance; ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾, i.e., the admonitions of God and the Qur'an, so that they might reflect and take heed, thereby knowing the oneness of God, then acting upon the realization of prophethood. Then He struck for them a likeness in ignorance and in limiting themselves to eating and drinking, and their distance from the requirements of action. The Mighty One said: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray﴾, because livestock know their Lord and remember Him and obey Him, while the disbelievers do not know their Lord nor obey Him.

And in a report: "Every creature is more obedient to God than the son of Adam" [al-Mu'jam al-Saghir: 2/51].

﴿Those are the heedless.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 172–179 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.﴾

The commentators (mufassirun) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it all his descendants, and they are the offspring. They differed about the place of the covenant (mithaq).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was in the valley of Nu'man, beside 'Arafah. It is also related from him that it was [Barhaba], a land in India, and it is the place where Allah caused Adam (ﷺ) to descend. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/316. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/55.]

Al-Kalbi said: Between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Al-Suddi said: Allah had brought Adam out of the Garden and he had not descended from the heavens. Then He wiped over his back and brought forth his descendants. They said: He brought forth from the left side of his back black offspring, and said to them: "Enter the Fire, and I do not mind." That is when the people of the right and the people of the left are spoken of. And the people of al-Manamah.

And He said to them all: "Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord; you have no lord other than Me. So do not associate anything with Me, for I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you a Book." They said: "We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God, and we have no lord other than You." On that day they all acknowledged it, some willingly and obediently, and some under compulsion, out of taqiyyah (fear). They thereby took their pledges, and their terms of life, their provisions and their accounts were determined. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I wished to be thanked." [See Tarikh Dimashq: 7/398.]

They said: Among them, on that day, were the prophets, like lamps. Adam saw a shining light and said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is Dawud, a prophet from your descendants." He said: "How old is he?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "My Lord, increase him."

He said: The pen had run with the terms of the children of Adam. He said: "My Lord, increase him by forty years from my life." So forty years were recorded for Dawud, and Adam's life was a thousand years. When Adam completed nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came, and when Adam saw him he said: "What is it with you?" He said: "You have completed your term." Adam said to him: "Forty years remain of my life." He said: "Did you not grant them to Dawud?" He said: "No," and Adam denied it. So his descendants denied it, and Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot, and he erred, so his descendants erred. The angel returned to his Lord and said: "Adam claims that forty years of his life remain." He said: "Inform Adam that he granted them to his son Dawud." The pens were slow, so they recorded them for Dawud.

When He had made them confess His Oneness and had preferred some of them over others, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not be established until every one whose pledge was taken is born, and nothing will be added to them or taken from them. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾. The construction of the verse (nazm al-ayah) is: "And when your Lord took from the backs of the Children of Adam their descendants." The matter of Adam is not mentioned, because they were brought out on the Day of the Covenant from his back. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam, some from the backs of others, in the way children are born from their fathers. So He dispensed with mentioning the back of Adam by saying "from the Children of Adam." When it became known that they were all his sons and had come out from his back, the mention of Adam's back was dropped and the mention of the backs of his sons was retained.

As for His words, ﴿their descendants﴾: the people of Makkah and Kufah read ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ without an alif, as a singular, while the rest read it in the plural with an alif. ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves﴾, and said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, a question for confirmation. ﴿They said: "Yes, we bear witness."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr read ﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ with the ya' (يقولوا), while the rest read it with the ta' (تقولوا), as in His saying ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾.

They differed about His words ﴿We bear witness﴾. Al-Suddi said: It is an announcement from Allah, speaking of Himself and of His angels, that they bore witness to the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam. Others said: Rather, it is about the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam, when some of them were made to bear witness against others, lest they say ﴿on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾, meaning, lest they should not say it. ﴿Or [lest] you say: "Our fathers only associated [others with Allah] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾, meaning the polytheists. We only followed them, and we were heedless of the Oneness. ﴿Thus We detail the verses﴾, O Muhammad, to your people, ﴿so that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾. They differed about him.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: He is Bal'am ibn Abirah. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ura. Mujahid said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ir. Muqatil said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ur ibn Mathh ibn Lut. 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas: He is from the Children of Israel.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: He was from the Canaanites, from the city of the giants. Muqatil said: He was from the city of Balqa', and it was named Balqa' because its king was a man called Baliq. His testament, as related by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi and others, was this: When Musa (ﷺ) intended to fight the giants and settled in the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of al-Sham, the people of Bal'am came to Bal'am, and he had the Greatest Name of Allah.

They said: "Musa is a fierce man, and he has large armies, and he has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us and give them to the Children of Israel. We are your people and your cousins, and we have no say. You are a man whose supplication is answered. Go out and ask Allah, Exalted is He, to turn Musa and his people away from us." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah has with him the angels and the believers. How can I curse them, when I know what I know from Allah? If I do this, my worldly life and my hereafter are lost." They said: "We have no [other] recourse," and they kept urging him about it. He said: "Until I consult my Lord." He would not supplicate until he saw in a dream what he was commanded, and he would be commanded to curse them.

In a dream it was said to him: "Do not curse them." He said to his people: "I have consulted my Lord about cursing them, and I have been forbidden." They gave him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: "Curse them!" He said: "Until I am commanded." When he was commanded, nothing came to him. He said: "I was commanded, but nothing came to me." They said: "If your Lord disliked your cursing them, He would have forbidden you as He did the first time." They kept at him, soothing him and pleading with him, until they seduced him, and he was seduced. He mounted his she-ass and set out toward a mountain overlooking the army of the Children of Israel, called Jasban.

When she had gone but a short distance, she lay down with him, so he dismounted and beat her until she was made to stand. He mounted her again, and she did not go far before she lay down, so he did the same to her, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far before she lay down, so he beat her until she was made to suffer, and then Allah gave her permission to speak, and she spoke as a proof against him. She said: "Woe to you, O Bal'am! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me from this way, so that we might go to the Prophet of Allah and to the believers whom you curse?" He did not desist, so Allah released her, and she went on until she brought him up over the mountain of Jasban. He began to curse them, but he cursed them with nothing without his tongue being turned toward his own people, and he prayed for his people for no good without his request being turned to the Children of Israel.

His people said to him: "Do you know what you are doing, O Bal'am? You are praying for them and cursing us." He said: "This is something I do not control; it is a matter in which Allah has prevailed." His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest, and he said to them: "Now this world and the hereafter are gone from me. Nothing remains but scheming and trickery. I will devise for you and contrive. Adorn your women and perfume them and give them goods, then send them to the army to mingle with them, and command them not to refuse any man who desires them, for if a single man of them commits fornication, they will be led into temptation." They did so.

When the women entered the army, a woman passed among the Canaanites, named Bashti, daughter of Sur, by a man of the notables of the Children of Israel called Zimri ibn Shalum, chief of the tribe of Shim'un ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim (ﷺ). He stood up to her and took her hand, for her beauty had tempted him. Then he came and stood before Musa and said: "I think you will say, 'This is forbidden to you.'" He said: "Indeed she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and lay with her, so Allah sent the plague (ta'un) upon the Children of Israel at once.

Fanhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, was a man who had been given physical stature and strength in grasping. He had been absent when Zimri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel and was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was made entirely of iron, and entered the tent upon them while they were lying together. He pierced them both with his spear and lifted them up toward the sky, with the spear in his arm, leaning with his elbow on his side and resting the spear against his beard.

He had been [disliking 'Izar], and he kept saying: "O Allah, this is what we do to those who disobey You." Then the plague was lifted. Those of the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the time Zimri had the woman until Fanhas killed him, were counted, and seventy thousand had perished in one hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel give the descendants of Fanhas the cheek, the foreleg and the jaw of every animal they slaughter, because he leaned on the spear with his arm and rested it against his beard; and the firstborn of all their wealth and their persons, because he was the firstborn of 'Izar ibn Harun. And concerning Bal'am, Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [At length in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/169.]

Muqatil said: The king of al-Balqa' said to Bal'am: "Curse Musa." He said: "He is of my religion; I will not curse him." So a wooden cross was set up for him to be crucified on. When he saw that, he set out on his she-ass to curse them. When he saw their army, the she-ass stood still and halted. He beat her, and she said: "Why do you beat me? I am commanded; do not wrong me. And there is a fire before me that has prevented me from walking." He returned and informed the king. The king said: "You must curse him, or I will crucify you." So he cursed Musa by the Greatest Name, that he should not enter the city, and it was answered for him. Musa and the Children of Israel fell into the wilderness (tih) because of his supplication. Musa said: "O Lord, for what sin have we fallen into the wilderness?" He said: "Because of the supplication of the scholar (al-'alim)." He said: "Just as You heard his supplication against me, hear my supplication against him." Musa prayed that He strip him of the Greatest Name and of faith. So Allah stripped him of what he had and removed knowledge from him, and it came out of his chest like a white dove. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he withdrew from them﴾ (fa-insalakha minha). Then Allah revealed this verse concerning him.

'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Rawq said: This verse was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi. His story was that at the beginning of his affair he read the books and knew that Allah would send a messenger at that time, and he hoped that he himself would be that messenger. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, he envied him. He had intended to go to some kings, but when he returned he passed by the slain of Badr and asked about them. It was said: "Muhammad killed them." He said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have killed his own kin." When Umayyah died, his sister Farida came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her about her brother's death. She said: "While he was with us, he slept on my couch, and two birds came and landed; one sat by his foot and the other by his head. The one by his foot said to the one by his head: 'Shall I strike?' He said: 'Strike.' He said: 'Shall I cut open?' He said: 'No.'" She said: "I asked him about that, and he said: 'Good, my sister.' Then they flew off from me, and he fainted. When he came round, he said:"

"Every life, however long it lasts, ends in the end of its matter / I wish I had been, before what has appeared to me, grazing the wild goats on the mountain crags."

"On the Day of Reckoning, a great day, in which the young grow old with heavy sleep."

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Recite to me your brother's poetry." She recited to him:

"To You is the praise, the bounty and the grace, our Lord, and nothing is higher than You in majesty and glory, / King over the throne of the heavens, Guardian, before whose might faces are humbled and bow down."

It was a long poem, until she came to its end. She recited to him his poem:

"The people stood for the reckoning, all of them, so the wretched one is punished and the happy one is blessed."

Then she recited to him his poem in which he says:

"Before the Lord of the Throne they are presented to Him, / He knows the open and the secret, the hidden. / The Day when the Merciful comes, and He is compassionate; / Indeed His promise is ever to be fulfilled. / The Day when there comes to him what he said, a single one, / then he will be surely guided or astray, / or happy with a happiness I hope for, / or humiliated, wretched for what he has earned. / If I am called to account for what I have committed, / I shall surely be cast into strong punishment. / And my Lord, if You pardon, then pardon is my hope, / or if You punish, You do not punish one who is innocent."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved."

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [al-Isabah: 8/261, abridged. See also the story and the verses in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 2/285.]

Some said: It was revealed concerning al-Busus.

He was a man who had been given three answered supplications. He had a wife, and he had a child by her. She said to him: "Make one of them for me." He said: "One of them is yours. What do you want?" She said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel." He prayed for her, and she became the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was none like her among them, she turned away from him, and the man was angry. He prayed against her, and she became a barking bitch. Two of the supplications were used up. Her sons came and said: "We have no peace over this. You prayed against our mother, and she became a barking bitch, and the people taunt us. Pray to Allah that He returns her to the state she was in." He prayed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and she returned as she was, and the supplications were all used up.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning Abu 'Amir ibn al-Nu'man ibn Sayfi, the monk, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) named "the Wicked" (al-Fasiq). He had been a monk in the Jahiliyyah and wore woollen garments. He came to Madinah and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is this that you have brought?" He said: "I have brought the Hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." He said: "I am the one who brought it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You are not upon it, but you have introduced Iblis into it." Abu 'Amir said: "May Allah cause the liar among us to die, a stranger, alone." He went out to al-Sham and sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare strength and weapons, and build me a mosque." Then he went to the monk, Caesar, and came with troops to expel the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions from Madinah. This is His saying: ﴿and in ambush for those who had fought against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning waiting for his coming. He died in al-Sham, a stranger, alone.

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: It was revealed concerning the Quraysh. Allah brought them the signs, but they withdrew from them and did not accept them.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites of the People of the Book, who used to recognise the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿as they recognise their own sons﴾.

'Amr ibn Dinar said: 'Ikrimah was asked about this verse, and he said: "This and that are not specific to one matter."

Qatadah said: This is a parable that Allah struck for one to whom guidance was presented but who did not accept it. This is His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: It is the Greatest Name of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: He would ask Allah for nothing without being given it.

Ibn 'Abbas, in another narration, said: It is greater in that it is a book of the books of Allah. Mujahid said: He was a prophet from the Children of Israel called Bal'am. He was given prophethood, but his people bribed him to keep silent, so he did, and left them as they were. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

﴿So he withdrew [went out] from them﴾, as the snake sheds its skin. ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he overtook him and caught up with him, ﴿and he became of the misguided.﴾ ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾, meaning We would have favoured him, honoured him and raised his station by the signs.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We would have raised him by them.

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: Meaning, We would have lifted disbelief from him through the signs and protected him.

﴿But he inclined to the earth﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He leaned toward the earth. Mujahid said: He settled. Muqatil said: He was content with the world. Abu 'Ubaydah said: He clung to it and was slow. The one who is "mukhallad" among men is one whose white hair is slow to appear, and among animals, one whose incisors remain until the molars come out. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

Al-Zajjaj said: Khalada and akhlada are one, and it is derived from khuld, which means lasting and dwelling. One says "khalada fulan bi al-maqam" when he stays in a place. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"To whom do these dwellings belong, which you have passed through in al-Gharqad, / like the writing in the hollow of the watercourse, long-lasting."

Meaning: remaining.

Malik ibn Nuwayrah said:

"Then no tidings of a tribe from the tribes of Malik / and 'Amr ibn Yarbu' who stayed and clung to the land."

[Lisan al-'Arab: 3/164.] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

﴿And followed his desire.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: He follows base affairs and abandons the lofty ones. Abu Rawq said: He chose the world over the hereafter. Ibn Zayd said: His desire was with [the ancient ones]. 'Ata' said: He wanted the world and obeyed his Satan. Yaman said: ﴿and followed his desire﴾, meaning his wife, because she drove him to betrayal.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verse 172–179 (part 2 of 2):

So his likeness is like the likeness of the dog: if you chase it, it pants; or if you leave it, it pants. Mujahid said: "It is the likeness of one who reads the Book but does not act by it." Ibn Jurayj said: "The dog is one whose heart is cut off, having no heart; if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. This is the likeness of one who abandons guidance, having no heart; rather, his heart is cut off."

Ma'mar narrated from some of them, who said: "It is the disbeliever who is astray, whether you admonish him or do not admonish him."

Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning, "if you chase it [with wisdom], it will not take it up; and if you leave it, it will not be guided to any good, like the dog: if it is lying down it pants, and if it is driven away it pants."

Al-Hasan said: "It is the hypocrite, who does not turn back to the truth, whether he is called or not called, admonished or not admonished. [Like the dog], it pants whether it is driven away or left alone." 'Ata' said: "It barks whether it is chased or not chased." Al-Qutabi said: "Every creature pants from exhaustion or thirst except the dog, for it pants in a state of fatigue and in a state of rest, in health and in sickness, in hunger and in thirst." So God struck this as a likeness for one who denies His signs.

He said: whether you admonish him, he is astray; and whether you leave him, he is astray, like the dog: if you drive it, it pants, and if you leave it, it pants. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 193]. ﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Salim [Abu al-Khadr], who said: he means the likeness of the Children of Israel, i.e., if you bring them news of what was among them, which you did not witness (﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾).

They would know that no one brings this news of the past among them except a prophet, one who is informed by heaven. ﴿Evil is the likeness﴾, i.e., "evil is the likeness" as a circumstantial clause from the implied noun (al-mathal). As Jarir said:

"How excellent is the provision of your father's provision, a provision."

This is when you make "sa'a" (evil) a verb of the likeness and take "al-qawm" (the people) as a substitute for the pronoun within it. If you transfer its verb to "the people" and make them its agent, it becomes a specification (tamyiz), meaning: "I shall liken the people," and when you transfer it to them, the likeness becomes explanatory, as one says: "qarrabahu 'aynan" and "daqa dharʿan," whenever the tanwin falls from the specified noun that is genitive by annexation. Its evidence is the recitation of al-Jahdari and al-A'mash: "sa-umaththil al-qawm" (with annexation). Abu Hatim said: they mean by it "mithl" (the likeness), i.e., "the likeness of the people," so "mithl" was omitted.

"The people" were placed in a position with "ummah," so he raised them, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾.

﴿And themselves they were wronging﴾, up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾. He said this only because of His complete knowledge concerning them, that they would arrive at it through their disbelief in their Lord. Some scholars of meanings call this the "lam of becoming" (lam al-sayrurah), as in His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 8]. And they recited:

"Our wealth we gather for the heirs of inheritance, and our houses we build for the ruin of time."

And another said:

"For death the mothers bear their young, just as houses are built for the ruin of time."

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr narrated from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this verse, he said: "Just as God, Exalted is He, created for Hell what He created, the child of fornication was among those created for Hell."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, i.e., they do not comprehend good and guidance; ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾, i.e., the path of truth and right guidance; ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾, i.e., the admonitions of God and the Qur'an, so that they might reflect and take heed, thereby knowing the oneness of God, then acting upon the realization of prophethood. Then He struck for them a likeness in ignorance and in limiting themselves to eating and drinking, and their distance from the requirements of action. The Mighty One said: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray﴾, because livestock know their Lord and remember Him and obey Him, while the disbelievers do not know their Lord nor obey Him.

And in a report: "Every creature is more obedient to God than the son of Adam" [al-Mu'jam al-Saghir: 2/51].

﴿Those are the heedless.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 172–179 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.﴾

The commentators (mufassirun) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it all his descendants, and they are the offspring. They differed about the place of the covenant (mithaq).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was in the valley of Nu'man, beside 'Arafah. It is also related from him that it was [Barhaba], a land in India, and it is the place where Allah caused Adam (ﷺ) to descend. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/316. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/55.]

Al-Kalbi said: Between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Al-Suddi said: Allah had brought Adam out of the Garden and he had not descended from the heavens. Then He wiped over his back and brought forth his descendants. They said: He brought forth from the left side of his back black offspring, and said to them: "Enter the Fire, and I do not mind." That is when the people of the right and the people of the left are spoken of. And the people of al-Manamah.

And He said to them all: "Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord; you have no lord other than Me. So do not associate anything with Me, for I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you a Book." They said: "We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God, and we have no lord other than You." On that day they all acknowledged it, some willingly and obediently, and some under compulsion, out of taqiyyah (fear). They thereby took their pledges, and their terms of life, their provisions and their accounts were determined. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I wished to be thanked." [See Tarikh Dimashq: 7/398.]

They said: Among them, on that day, were the prophets, like lamps. Adam saw a shining light and said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is Dawud, a prophet from your descendants." He said: "How old is he?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "My Lord, increase him."

He said: The pen had run with the terms of the children of Adam. He said: "My Lord, increase him by forty years from my life." So forty years were recorded for Dawud, and Adam's life was a thousand years. When Adam completed nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came, and when Adam saw him he said: "What is it with you?" He said: "You have completed your term." Adam said to him: "Forty years remain of my life." He said: "Did you not grant them to Dawud?" He said: "No," and Adam denied it. So his descendants denied it, and Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot, and he erred, so his descendants erred. The angel returned to his Lord and said: "Adam claims that forty years of his life remain." He said: "Inform Adam that he granted them to his son Dawud." The pens were slow, so they recorded them for Dawud.

When He had made them confess His Oneness and had preferred some of them over others, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not be established until every one whose pledge was taken is born, and nothing will be added to them or taken from them. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾. The construction of the verse (nazm al-ayah) is: "And when your Lord took from the backs of the Children of Adam their descendants." The matter of Adam is not mentioned, because they were brought out on the Day of the Covenant from his back. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam, some from the backs of others, in the way children are born from their fathers. So He dispensed with mentioning the back of Adam by saying "from the Children of Adam." When it became known that they were all his sons and had come out from his back, the mention of Adam's back was dropped and the mention of the backs of his sons was retained.

As for His words, ﴿their descendants﴾: the people of Makkah and Kufah read ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ without an alif, as a singular, while the rest read it in the plural with an alif. ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves﴾, and said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, a question for confirmation. ﴿They said: "Yes, we bear witness."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr read ﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ with the ya' (يقولوا), while the rest read it with the ta' (تقولوا), as in His saying ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾.

They differed about His words ﴿We bear witness﴾. Al-Suddi said: It is an announcement from Allah, speaking of Himself and of His angels, that they bore witness to the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam. Others said: Rather, it is about the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam, when some of them were made to bear witness against others, lest they say ﴿on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾, meaning, lest they should not say it. ﴿Or [lest] you say: "Our fathers only associated [others with Allah] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾, meaning the polytheists. We only followed them, and we were heedless of the Oneness. ﴿Thus We detail the verses﴾, O Muhammad, to your people, ﴿so that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾. They differed about him.

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: He is Bal'am ibn Abirah. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ura. Mujahid said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ir. Muqatil said: He is Bal'am ibn Ba'ur ibn Mathh ibn Lut. 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas: He is from the Children of Israel.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: He was from the Canaanites, from the city of the giants. Muqatil said: He was from the city of Balqa', and it was named Balqa' because its king was a man called Baliq. His testament, as related by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi and others, was this: When Musa (ﷺ) intended to fight the giants and settled in the land of the Banu Kan'an in the land of al-Sham, the people of Bal'am came to Bal'am, and he had the Greatest Name of Allah.

They said: "Musa is a fierce man, and he has large armies, and he has come to drive us out of our lands and kill us and give them to the Children of Israel. We are your people and your cousins, and we have no say. You are a man whose supplication is answered. Go out and ask Allah, Exalted is He, to turn Musa and his people away from us." He said: "Woe to you! The Prophet of Allah has with him the angels and the believers. How can I curse them, when I know what I know from Allah? If I do this, my worldly life and my hereafter are lost." They said: "We have no [other] recourse," and they kept urging him about it. He said: "Until I consult my Lord." He would not supplicate until he saw in a dream what he was commanded, and he would be commanded to curse them.

In a dream it was said to him: "Do not curse them." He said to his people: "I have consulted my Lord about cursing them, and I have been forbidden." They gave him a gift, and he accepted it. Then they came back to him and said: "Curse them!" He said: "Until I am commanded." When he was commanded, nothing came to him. He said: "I was commanded, but nothing came to me." They said: "If your Lord disliked your cursing them, He would have forbidden you as He did the first time." They kept at him, soothing him and pleading with him, until they seduced him, and he was seduced. He mounted his she-ass and set out toward a mountain overlooking the army of the Children of Israel, called Jasban.

When she had gone but a short distance, she lay down with him, so he dismounted and beat her until she was made to stand. He mounted her again, and she did not go far before she lay down, so he did the same to her, and she stood up and he mounted her again. She did not go far before she lay down, so he beat her until she was made to suffer, and then Allah gave her permission to speak, and she spoke as a proof against him. She said: "Woe to you, O Bal'am! Where are you going? Do you not see the angels before me, turning me from this way, so that we might go to the Prophet of Allah and to the believers whom you curse?" He did not desist, so Allah released her, and she went on until she brought him up over the mountain of Jasban. He began to curse them, but he cursed them with nothing without his tongue being turned toward his own people, and he prayed for his people for no good without his request being turned to the Children of Israel.

His people said to him: "Do you know what you are doing, O Bal'am? You are praying for them and cursing us." He said: "This is something I do not control; it is a matter in which Allah has prevailed." His tongue hung out and fell upon his chest, and he said to them: "Now this world and the hereafter are gone from me. Nothing remains but scheming and trickery. I will devise for you and contrive. Adorn your women and perfume them and give them goods, then send them to the army to mingle with them, and command them not to refuse any man who desires them, for if a single man of them commits fornication, they will be led into temptation." They did so.

When the women entered the army, a woman passed among the Canaanites, named Bashti, daughter of Sur, by a man of the notables of the Children of Israel called Zimri ibn Shalum, chief of the tribe of Shim'un ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim (ﷺ). He stood up to her and took her hand, for her beauty had tempted him. Then he came and stood before Musa and said: "I think you will say, 'This is forbidden to you.'" He said: "Indeed she is forbidden to you; do not approach her." He said: "By Allah, we will not obey you in this." Then he entered with her into his tent and lay with her, so Allah sent the plague (ta'un) upon the Children of Israel at once.

Fanhas ibn al-'Izar ibn Harun, the one in charge of Musa's affairs, was a man who had been given physical stature and strength in grasping. He had been absent when Zimri ibn Shalum did what he did. He came while the plague was spreading among the Children of Israel and was informed of the matter. He took his spear, which was made entirely of iron, and entered the tent upon them while they were lying together. He pierced them both with his spear and lifted them up toward the sky, with the spear in his arm, leaning with his elbow on his side and resting the spear against his beard.

He had been [disliking 'Izar], and he kept saying: "O Allah, this is what we do to those who disobey You." Then the plague was lifted. Those of the Children of Israel who died in the plague, from the time Zimri had the woman until Fanhas killed him, were counted, and seventy thousand had perished in one hour of the day. From that time the Children of Israel give the descendants of Fanhas the cheek, the foreleg and the jaw of every animal they slaughter, because he leaned on the spear with his arm and rested it against his beard; and the firstborn of all their wealth and their persons, because he was the firstborn of 'Izar ibn Harun. And concerning Bal'am, Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [At length in Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/169.]

Muqatil said: The king of al-Balqa' said to Bal'am: "Curse Musa." He said: "He is of my religion; I will not curse him." So a wooden cross was set up for him to be crucified on. When he saw that, he set out on his she-ass to curse them. When he saw their army, the she-ass stood still and halted. He beat her, and she said: "Why do you beat me? I am commanded; do not wrong me. And there is a fire before me that has prevented me from walking." He returned and informed the king. The king said: "You must curse him, or I will crucify you." So he cursed Musa by the Greatest Name, that he should not enter the city, and it was answered for him. Musa and the Children of Israel fell into the wilderness (tih) because of his supplication. Musa said: "O Lord, for what sin have we fallen into the wilderness?" He said: "Because of the supplication of the scholar (al-'alim)." He said: "Just as You heard his supplication against me, hear my supplication against him." Musa prayed that He strip him of the Greatest Name and of faith. So Allah stripped him of what he had and removed knowledge from him, and it came out of his chest like a white dove. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he withdrew from them﴾ (fa-insalakha minha). Then Allah revealed this verse concerning him.

'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Rawq said: This verse was revealed concerning Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi. His story was that at the beginning of his affair he read the books and knew that Allah would send a messenger at that time, and he hoped that he himself would be that messenger. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

When Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, he envied him. He had intended to go to some kings, but when he returned he passed by the slain of Badr and asked about them. It was said: "Muhammad killed them." He said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have killed his own kin." When Umayyah died, his sister Farida came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked her about her brother's death. She said: "While he was with us, he slept on my couch, and two birds came and landed; one sat by his foot and the other by his head. The one by his foot said to the one by his head: 'Shall I strike?' He said: 'Strike.' He said: 'Shall I cut open?' He said: 'No.'" She said: "I asked him about that, and he said: 'Good, my sister.' Then they flew off from me, and he fainted. When he came round, he said:"

"Every life, however long it lasts, ends in the end of its matter / I wish I had been, before what has appeared to me, grazing the wild goats on the mountain crags."

"On the Day of Reckoning, a great day, in which the young grow old with heavy sleep."

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Recite to me your brother's poetry." She recited to him:

"To You is the praise, the bounty and the grace, our Lord, and nothing is higher than You in majesty and glory, / King over the throne of the heavens, Guardian, before whose might faces are humbled and bow down."

It was a long poem, until she came to its end. She recited to him his poem:

"The people stood for the reckoning, all of them, so the wretched one is punished and the happy one is blessed."

Then she recited to him his poem in which he says:

"Before the Lord of the Throne they are presented to Him, / He knows the open and the secret, the hidden. / The Day when the Merciful comes, and He is compassionate; / Indeed His promise is ever to be fulfilled. / The Day when there comes to him what he said, a single one, / then he will be surely guided or astray, / or happy with a happiness I hope for, / or humiliated, wretched for what he has earned. / If I am called to account for what I have committed, / I shall surely be cast into strong punishment. / And my Lord, if You pardon, then pardon is my hope, / or if You punish, You do not punish one who is innocent."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "His poetry believed, but his heart disbelieved."

And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾, the verse. [al-Isabah: 8/261, abridged. See also the story and the verses in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 2/285.]

Some said: It was revealed concerning al-Busus.

He was a man who had been given three answered supplications. He had a wife, and he had a child by her. She said to him: "Make one of them for me." He said: "One of them is yours. What do you want?" She said: "Pray to Allah that He makes me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel." He prayed for her, and she became the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was none like her among them, she turned away from him, and the man was angry. He prayed against her, and she became a barking bitch. Two of the supplications were used up. Her sons came and said: "We have no peace over this. You prayed against our mother, and she became a barking bitch, and the people taunt us. Pray to Allah that He returns her to the state she was in." He prayed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and she returned as she was, and the supplications were all used up.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning Abu 'Amir ibn al-Nu'man ibn Sayfi, the monk, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) named "the Wicked" (al-Fasiq). He had been a monk in the Jahiliyyah and wore woollen garments. He came to Madinah and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is this that you have brought?" He said: "I have brought the Hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." He said: "I am the one who brought it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You are not upon it, but you have introduced Iblis into it." Abu 'Amir said: "May Allah cause the liar among us to die, a stranger, alone." He went out to al-Sham and sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare strength and weapons, and build me a mosque." Then he went to the monk, Caesar, and came with troops to expel the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions from Madinah. This is His saying: ﴿and in ambush for those who had fought against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning waiting for his coming. He died in al-Sham, a stranger, alone.

'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: It was revealed concerning the Quraysh. Allah brought them the signs, but they withdrew from them and did not accept them.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites of the People of the Book, who used to recognise the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿as they recognise their own sons﴾.

'Amr ibn Dinar said: 'Ikrimah was asked about this verse, and he said: "This and that are not specific to one matter."

Qatadah said: This is a parable that Allah struck for one to whom guidance was presented but who did not accept it. This is His saying: ﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi said: It is the Greatest Name of Allah. Ibn Zayd said: He would ask Allah for nothing without being given it.

Ibn 'Abbas, in another narration, said: It is greater in that it is a book of the books of Allah. Mujahid said: He was a prophet from the Children of Israel called Bal'am. He was given prophethood, but his people bribed him to keep silent, so he did, and left them as they were. [Zad al-Masir: 3/195.]

﴿So he withdrew [went out] from them﴾, as the snake sheds its skin. ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning he overtook him and caught up with him, ﴿and he became of the misguided.﴾ ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾, meaning We would have favoured him, honoured him and raised his station by the signs.

Ibn 'Abbas said: We would have raised him by them.

Mujahid and 'Ata' said: Meaning, We would have lifted disbelief from him through the signs and protected him.

﴿But he inclined to the earth﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He leaned toward the earth. Mujahid said: He settled. Muqatil said: He was content with the world. Abu 'Ubaydah said: He clung to it and was slow. The one who is "mukhallad" among men is one whose white hair is slow to appear, and among animals, one whose incisors remain until the molars come out. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

Al-Zajjaj said: Khalada and akhlada are one, and it is derived from khuld, which means lasting and dwelling. One says "khalada fulan bi al-maqam" when he stays in a place. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"To whom do these dwellings belong, which you have passed through in al-Gharqad, / like the writing in the hollow of the watercourse, long-lasting."

Meaning: remaining.

Malik ibn Nuwayrah said:

"Then no tidings of a tribe from the tribes of Malik / and 'Amr ibn Yarbu' who stayed and clung to the land."

[Lisan al-'Arab: 3/164.] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 6/171.]

﴿And followed his desire.﴾ Al-Kalbi said: He follows base affairs and abandons the lofty ones. Abu Rawq said: He chose the world over the hereafter. Ibn Zayd said: His desire was with [the ancient ones]. 'Ata' said: He wanted the world and obeyed his Satan. Yaman said: ﴿and followed his desire﴾, meaning his wife, because she drove him to betrayal.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verse 172–179 (part 2 of 2):

So his likeness is like the likeness of the dog: if you chase it, it pants; or if you leave it, it pants. Mujahid said: "It is the likeness of one who reads the Book but does not act by it." Ibn Jurayj said: "The dog is one whose heart is cut off, having no heart; if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. This is the likeness of one who abandons guidance, having no heart; rather, his heart is cut off."

Ma'mar narrated from some of them, who said: "It is the disbeliever who is astray, whether you admonish him or do not admonish him."

Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning, "if you chase it [with wisdom], it will not take it up; and if you leave it, it will not be guided to any good, like the dog: if it is lying down it pants, and if it is driven away it pants."

Al-Hasan said: "It is the hypocrite, who does not turn back to the truth, whether he is called or not called, admonished or not admonished. [Like the dog], it pants whether it is driven away or left alone." 'Ata' said: "It barks whether it is chased or not chased." Al-Qutabi said: "Every creature pants from exhaustion or thirst except the dog, for it pants in a state of fatigue and in a state of rest, in health and in sickness, in hunger and in thirst." So God struck this as a likeness for one who denies His signs.

He said: whether you admonish him, he is astray; and whether you leave him, he is astray, like the dog: if you drive it, it pants, and if you leave it, it pants. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 193]. ﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Salim [Abu al-Khadr], who said: he means the likeness of the Children of Israel, i.e., if you bring them news of what was among them, which you did not witness (﴿perhaps they will reflect﴾).

They would know that no one brings this news of the past among them except a prophet, one who is informed by heaven. ﴿Evil is the likeness﴾, i.e., "evil is the likeness" as a circumstantial clause from the implied noun (al-mathal). As Jarir said:

"How excellent is the provision of your father's provision, a provision."

This is when you make "sa'a" (evil) a verb of the likeness and take "al-qawm" (the people) as a substitute for the pronoun within it. If you transfer its verb to "the people" and make them its agent, it becomes a specification (tamyiz), meaning: "I shall liken the people," and when you transfer it to them, the likeness becomes explanatory, as one says: "qarrabahu 'aynan" and "daqa dharʿan," whenever the tanwin falls from the specified noun that is genitive by annexation. Its evidence is the recitation of al-Jahdari and al-A'mash: "sa-umaththil al-qawm" (with annexation). Abu Hatim said: they mean by it "mithl" (the likeness), i.e., "the likeness of the people," so "mithl" was omitted.

"The people" were placed in a position with "ummah," so he raised them, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾.

﴿And themselves they were wronging﴾, up to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾. He said this only because of His complete knowledge concerning them, that they would arrive at it through their disbelief in their Lord. Some scholars of meanings call this the "lam of becoming" (lam al-sayrurah), as in His saying: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 8]. And they recited:

"Our wealth we gather for the heirs of inheritance, and our houses we build for the ruin of time."

And another said:

"For death the mothers bear their young, just as houses are built for the ruin of time."

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr narrated from the Prophet ﷺ concerning this verse, he said: "Just as God, Exalted is He, created for Hell what He created, the child of fornication was among those created for Hell."

Then He described them, saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, i.e., they do not comprehend good and guidance; ﴿and they have eyes with which they do not see﴾, i.e., the path of truth and right guidance; ﴿and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾, i.e., the admonitions of God and the Qur'an, so that they might reflect and take heed, thereby knowing the oneness of God, then acting upon the realization of prophethood. Then He struck for them a likeness in ignorance and in limiting themselves to eating and drinking, and their distance from the requirements of action. The Mighty One said: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray﴾, because livestock know their Lord and remember Him and obey Him, while the disbelievers do not know their Lord nor obey Him.

And in a report: "Every creature is more obedient to God than the son of Adam" [al-Mu'jam al-Saghir: 2/51].

﴿Those are the heedless.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 7, verses 172–179 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.﴾

The commentators (mufassirun) said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, He wiped over his back and brought forth from it all his descendants, and they are the offspring. They differed about the place of the covenant (mithaq).

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was in the valley of Nu'man, beside 'Arafah. It is also related from him that it was [Barhaba], a land in India, and it is the place where Allah caused Adam (ﷺ) to descend. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/316. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/55.]

Al-Kalbi said: Between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Al-Suddi said: Allah had brought Adam out of the Garden and he had not descended from the heavens. Then He wiped over his back and brought forth his descendants. They said: He brought forth from the left side of his back black offspring, and said to them: "Enter the Fire, and I do not mind." That is when the people of the right and the people of the left are spoken of. And the people of al-Manamah.

And He said to them all: "Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord; you have no lord other than Me. So do not associate anything with Me, for I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I will send down to you a Book." They said: "We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God, and we have no lord other than You." On that day they all acknowledged it, some willingly and obediently, and some under compulsion, out of taqiyyah (fear). They thereby took their pledges, and their terms of life, their provisions and their accounts were determined. Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the beautiful in form and others less so. He said: "My Lord, why did You not make them equal?" He said: "I wished to be thanked." [See Tarikh Dimashq: 7/398.]

They said: Among them, on that day, were the prophets, like lamps. Adam saw a shining light and said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is Dawud, a prophet from your descendants." He said: "How old is he?" He said: "Sixty years." He said: "My Lord, increase him."

He said: The pen had run with the terms of the children of Adam. He said: "My Lord, increase him by forty years from my life." So forty years were recorded for Dawud, and Adam's life was a thousand years. When Adam completed nine hundred and sixty years, the Angel of Death came, and when Adam saw him he said: "What is it with you?" He said: "You have completed your term." Adam said to him: "Forty years remain of my life." He said: "Did you not grant them to Dawud?" He said: "No," and Adam denied it. So his descendants denied it, and Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot, and he erred, so his descendants erred. The angel returned to his Lord and said: "Adam claims that forty years of his life remain." He said: "Inform Adam that he granted them to his son Dawud." The pens were slow, so they recorded them for Dawud.

When He had made them confess His Oneness and had preferred some of them over others, He returned them to his loins. The Hour will not be established until every one whose pledge was taken is born, and nothing will be added to them or taken from them. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam﴾. The construction of the verse (nazm al-ayah) is: "And when your Lord took from the backs of the Children of Adam their descendants." The matter of Adam is not mentioned, because they were brought out on the Day of the Covenant from his back. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought forth the descendants of Adam, some from the backs of others, in the way children are born from their fathers. So He dispensed with mentioning the back of Adam by saying "from the Children of Adam." When it became known that they were all his sons and had come out from his back, the mention of Adam's back was dropped and the mention of the backs of his sons was retained.

As for His words, ﴿their descendants﴾: the people of Makkah and Kufah read ﴿ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ﴾ without an alif, as a singular, while the rest read it in the plural with an alif. ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves﴾, and said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, a question for confirmation. ﴿They said: "Yes, we bear witness."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Muhaysin and Abu 'Amr read ﴿أَنْ يَقُولُوا﴾ with the ya' (يقولوا), while the rest read it with the ta' (تقولوا), as in His saying ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾.

They differed about His words ﴿We bear witness﴾. Al-Suddi said: It is an announcement from Allah, speaking of Himself and of His angels, that they bore witness to the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam. Others said: Rather, it is about the acknowledgment of the Children of Adam, when some of them were made to bear witness against others, lest they say ﴿on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this"﴾, meaning, lest they should not say it. ﴿Or [lest] you say: "Our fathers only associated [others with Allah] before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾, meaning the polytheists. We only followed them, and we were heedless of the Oneness. ﴿Thus We detail the verses﴾, O Muhammad, to your people, ﴿so that they may return﴾ from their disbelief.

﴿And recite to them the story of him to whom We gave Our signs﴾. They differed about him.
